knowledge_statements.statement_title: PDE-constrained reduced-gradient iteration using sensitivities or an adjoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-solve and design-update algorithm for the stated semilinear PDE, offering sensitivity-based and adjoint-based gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\alpha^{(0)}=(\alpha_1^{(0)},\ldots,\alpha_K^{(0)})\). For \(m=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(-
abla\!\cdot(a
abla\phi^{(m)})+\mathbf b\cdot
abla\phi^{(m)}+(\phi^{(m)})^3=\sum_{k=1}^K\alpha_k^{(m)}f_k\) in \(\Omega\), with \(\phi^{(m)}=0\) on \(\Gamma\). Then either solve, for each \(k\), \(-
abla\!\cdot(a
abla\phi_k^{(m)})+\mathbf b\cdot
abla\phi_k^{(m)}+3(\phi^{(m)})^2\phi_k^{(m)}=f_k\), \(\phi_k^{(m)}|_\Gamma=0\), and compute \(D\mathcal J/D\alpha_k=\sigma\alpha_k^{(m)}+\int_\Omega(\phi^{(m)}-\Phi)\phi_k^{(m)}\,d\Omega\); or solve \(-
abla\!\cdot(a
abla\lambda^{(m)})-
abla\!\cdot(\mathbf b\lambda^{(m)})+3(\phi^{(m)})^2\lambda^{(m)}=\phi^{(m)}-\Phi\), \(\lambda^{(m)}|_\Gamma=0\), and compute \(D\mathcal J/D\alpha_k=\sigma\alpha_k^{(m)}+\int_\Omega\lambda^{(m)}f_k\,d\Omega\). Choose an increment from the gradient, for example \(\delta\alpha_k^{(m)}=- eta_mD\mathcal J/D\alpha_k\), and update \(\alpha_k^{(m+1)}=\alpha_k^{(m)}+\delta\alpha_k^{(m)}\) until satisfactory convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from initial design parameters, repeatedly solve the nonlinear state PDE, compute the gradient using either K sensitivity solves or one adjoint solve, choose a design increment, and update the parameters until satisfactory convergence.
assumptions_latex: \beta_m\text{ is an appropriately chosen step size when the gradient update is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_k^{(m+1)}=\alpha_k^{(m)}+\delta\alpha_k^{(m)},\qquad k=1,\ldots,K,\text{ with the gradient computed by either the sensitivity or adjoint formula.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiate-then-discretize approach
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of continuous differentiation and numerical discretization for PDE sensitivity or adjoint systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the differentiate-then-discretize approach, one first differentiates the governing PDEs together with their boundary and initial conditions with respect to the design or control parameters, thereby obtaining continuous sensitivity or adjoint equations. One then discretizes those continuous systems; solving the resulting discrete equations produces discrete approximations of the sensitivities or adjoint variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiate-then-discretize means deriving sensitivity or adjoint equations at the continuous PDE level and discretizing those derived systems afterward.
assumptions_latex: \text{The governing model consists of parameter-dependent PDEs with the associated boundary and, when present, initial conditions.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Discretizing and solving the continuous sensitivity or adjoint systems yields discrete approximations to the corresponding variables.}

children.title: Jacobian–Vector Products
children.top_down_role: Forward linearized actions for square and rectangular models.

assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(x+t v\in U\) for all sufficiently small \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]=\left.\dfrac{d}{dt}F(x+t v)\right|_{t=0}\in\mathbb{R}^m\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the vector-valued map at the evaluation point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional forward derivative action without materializing the Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable map \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), its Jacobian–vector product at \(x\in U\) in direction \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is the directional derivative
\[
J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{F(x+t v)-F(x)}{t}.
\]
The product is an element of \(\mathbb{R}^m\) and can be exposed as an operator that accepts \(v\) without storing the possibly rectangular matrix \(J_F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Jacobian–vector product is the forward directional derivative of a vector-valued map and can be evaluated without forming its Jacobian matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian–Vector Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional Jacobian–vector representation is mathematically standard, internally consistent, and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the derivative formula or matrix-free interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix-free Jacobian–vector products for inexact Newton–Krylov solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator realizations explicitly supported by the extract; the separate convergence-invariance, Krylov-applicability, and GMRES-storage claims are not conflated with this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a Krylov method approximately solves \(Jp=-r\), products \(Jd\) can be computed without explicitly forming \(J\). The extract identifies two realizations: a finite-difference approximation requiring one evaluation of \(r(\cdot)\), and forward-mode automatic differentiation, which computes \(Jd\) to finite-precision accuracy at a cost no more than a small multiple of evaluating \(r(\cdot)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact Newton–Krylov implementation can supply Jacobian–vector products without forming the Jacobian, using either residual-based finite differencing or forward-mode automatic differentiation.
assumptions_latex: Jp=-r\text{ is solved approximately by a Krylov method}
Jd\text{ is required by the inner iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Jd\text{ can be supplied without explicitly forming }J

children.title: Transpose-Jacobian–Vector Products
children.top_down_role: Adjoint actions for least-squares, sensitivity, and reduced-space constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb{R}^m\), with Euclidean inner products on the domain and codomain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w=\nabla_x\bigl(w^{\mathsf T}F(x)\bigr)\), and \(u^{\mathsf T}J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w=(J_F(x)u)^{\mathsf T}w\) for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Transpose-Jacobian action on an output-space vector.
Euclidean inner product, written by matrix transposition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean adjoint action for a finite-dimensional vector-valued map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) differentiable at \(x\), the transpose-Jacobian–vector product with \(w\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is characterized by
\[
u^{\mathsf T}\bigl(J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w\bigr)=\bigl(J_F(x)u\bigr)^{\mathsf T}w\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w=\nabla_x\bigl(w^{\mathsf T}F(x)\bigr).
\]
Thus the action maps an output-space seed to an input-space vector without requiring explicit storage of \(J_F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transpose-Jacobian product is the Euclidean adjoint of the forward Jacobian action, equivalently the gradient of a seeded scalar output.
knowledge_statements.title: Transpose-Jacobian–Vector Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean adjoint characterization and seeded-gradient identity are correct and duality is the appropriate content kind, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Block Derivative Actions
children.top_down_role: Multiple-direction interfaces for block Krylov methods and batched execution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_F(x)V=[J_F(x)v_1,\ldots,J_F(x)v_p]\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-direction extension of a Jacobian–vector interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a block of directions \(V=[v_1,\ldots,v_p]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), the block derivative action of \(F\) at \(x\) is
\[
J_F(x)V=\bigl[J_F(x)v_1,\ldots,J_F(x)v_p\bigr]\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}.
\]
It is linear in \(V\). A valid matrix-free block interface returns this matrix of directional derivatives without requiring assembly of \(J_F(x)\); implementations may evaluate columns jointly, but must agree mathematically with applying the single-direction operator to every column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block derivative action applies one Jacobian to several directions, returning the corresponding directional derivatives as columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Derivative Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The columnwise block action fits the leaf and is correct, but no source is supplied and the domain of the block size p should be declared explicitly.

children.title: Objective Hessian–Vector Products
children.top_down_role: Curvature actions for unconstrained truncated-Newton models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_f(x)v=\nabla^2 f(x)v=\left.\dfrac{d}{dt}\nabla f(x+t v)\right|_{t=0}\).

notation.meaning: Objective Hessian at the evaluation point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective curvature action for smooth unconstrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a twice continuously differentiable objective \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), the objective Hessian–vector product at \(x\in U\) is
\[
H_f(x)v=\nabla^2 f(x)v=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\nabla f(x+t v)\right|_{t=0}.
\]
It equals the directional derivative of the gradient and is linear in \(v\). A matrix-free curvature oracle returns this vector for a supplied \(v\) without assembling or storing \(H_f(x)\), as required by truncated-Newton inner iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective Hessian–vector product is the directional derivative of the gradient and supplies exact curvature without forming the Hessian.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Hessian–Vector Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hessian–vector identity is correct under the stated smoothness assumptions and representation fits the operator-action leaf, but it lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Difference Hessian–Vector Products for Hessian-Free Newton–CG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free objective-curvature interface, forward-gradient approximation, first-order error, and gradient-evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Newton--CG requires products $
abla^2f(x_k)d$ but need not form or store $
abla^2f(x_k)$. For a small $h>0$, one may use $$
abla^2f(x_k)d\approx rac{
abla f(x_k+hd)-
abla f(x_k)}{h}.$$ If $
abla^2f$ is locally Lipschitz on the segment from $x_k$ to $x_k+hd$, then, for fixed $d$, $$ rac{
abla f(x_k+hd)-
abla f(x_k)}{h}=
abla^2f(x_k)d+O(h).$$ When $
abla f(x_k)$ is reused, each approximated product requires one new gradient evaluation, hence one new gradient evaluation per CG iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton–CG can be Hessian-free because it needs only Hessian–vector products. A forward difference of gradients supplies such a product with first-order error under sufficient local smoothness. Reusing the base gradient leaves one new gradient evaluation per CG iteration.
assumptions_latex: d\in\mathbb R^n\text{ is fixed for the }O(h)\text{ statement}
\nabla^2f\text{ is locally Lipschitz on }\{x_k+td:0\leq t\leq h\}
\nabla f(x_k)\text{ is available for reuse in the cost count}

children.title: Gauss–Newton Curvature Actions
children.top_down_role: Least-squares curvature actions assembled compositionally from forward and adjoint products.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauss–Newton Curvature Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted nonlinear least-squares Gauss–Newton action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the nonlinear least-squares objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\), the Gauss–Newton curvature action is
\[
B_{\mathrm{GN}}(x)v=J_r(x)^{\mathsf T}J_r(x)v=J_r(x)^{\mathsf T}\bigl(J_r(x)v\bigr).
\]
It is computed by one forward Jacobian action followed by one transpose-Jacobian action. Moreover,
\[
v^{\mathsf T}B_{\mathrm{GN}}(x)v=\lVert J_r(x)v\rVert_2^2\ge0,
\]
so the operator is symmetric positive semidefinite, even though the exact objective Hessian may be indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauss–Newton curvature applies the residual Jacobian forward and then adjoint, producing a symmetric positive-semidefinite least-squares approximation even when the exact objective Hessian is indefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(r:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x\), and \(f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{\mathrm{GN}}(x)v=J_r(x)^{\mathsf T}(J_r(x)v)\), with \(v^{\mathsf T}B_{\mathrm{GN}}(x)v=\lVert J_r(x)v\rVert_2^2\ge0\).

children.title: Lagrangian Hessian Actions
children.top_down_role: Curvature actions for constrained Newton, reduced-Hessian, and KKT systems.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)v=
abla^2f(x)v+\sum_{i=1}^q\lambda_i
abla^2c_i(x)v\).

notation.meaning: Hessian with respect to primal variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained Lagrangian curvature with fixed multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), where \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_q)\), its primal Hessian action at fixed \(\lambda\) is
\[

abla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)v=
abla^2f(x)v+\sum_{i=1}^q\lambda_i
abla^2c_i(x)v.
\]
Equivalently, it is the directional derivative in direction \(v\) of \(
abla_xL(x,\lambda)\). The action can therefore be supplied to constrained Newton, reduced-Hessian, or KKT iterations without explicitly assembling \(
abla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian Hessian action combines objective curvature with multiplier-weighted constraint curvature while holding the multipliers fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Hessian Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-multiplier Lagrangian Hessian action is correct for the stated equality-constrained convention and fits the leaf, but no constrained-optimization source is supplied.

children.title: Structured Curvature Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Problem-derived approximations retaining separability, sparsity, low rank, or physical structure.

assumptions_latex: \(B(x):\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is a computationally applicable linear operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(x)v\) replaces \(H(x)v\), while the declared structural class and approximation criterion determine whether the substitution is admissible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract operator definition covering problem-derived curvature approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured curvature surrogate for a target operator \(H(x)\) is a specified linear operator \(B(x)\) whose action \(B(x)v\) is used in place of \(H(x)v\), and whose representation preserves a declared problem structure such as block separability, sparsity pattern, low-rank coupling, or a physical discretization operator. Its definition must include an approximation criterion, for example \(\lVert B(x)-H(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), or an exact agreement condition on a stated subspace \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), such as \(B(x)v=H(x)v\) for every \(v\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured curvature surrogate replaces exact curvature by an applicable operator that preserves declared problem structure and satisfies a stated approximation or subspace-agreement criterion.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured Curvature Surrogates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition imposes a mandatory approximation or subspace-agreement criterion that is not a universal definition of structured curvature surrogates; the norm, tolerance, and admissible structural class are also unspecified. A supporting source is required to establish the intended local meaning.

children.title: Algorithmic-Differentiation Actions
children.top_down_role: Forward, reverse, and mixed differentiation routes for operator products.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is represented by a differentiable finite computational composition at the evaluation point \(x\).
\(v\) and \(w\) are compatible forward and reverse seeds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forward propagation returns \(J_F(x)v\), reverse propagation returns \(J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w\), and differentiating \(x\mapsto\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}v\) returns \(\nabla^2f(x)v\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint propagated backward through the computation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator products obtained by differentiating a computational composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a computational composition for \(F\), initialize the input tangent by \(\dot x=v\) and propagate each elemental derivative forward; the output tangent is \(\dot F=J_F(x)v\). Alternatively, initialize the output adjoint by \(\bar F=w\) and propagate elemental transposes backward; the input adjoint is \(\bar x=J_F(x)^{\mathsf T}w\). For a scalar \(f\), a Hessian action is obtained by applying a forward derivative to the reverse-computed gradient, equivalently by differentiating \(x\mapsto\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}v\). The returned product is the algorithm output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algorithmic differentiation propagates tangent or adjoint seeds through a computation to obtain Jacobian, transpose-Jacobian, or mixed second-order products.
knowledge_statements.title: Algorithmic-Differentiation Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Forward and reverse seed propagation fit this algorithm leaf, but the Hessian-action sentence needs explicit twice differentiability of the scalar function and justification that differentiating the seeded gradient yields \(\nabla^2 f(x)v\) rather than merely its transpose action. No source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward-then-reverse evaluation of a Hessian–vector product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-mode automatic differentiation for Hessian–vector products, with source-specific operation-count estimates for dense and sparsity-compressed Hessian recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ be twice differentiable and represented by a differentiable scalar computational graph, and fix $q\in\mathbb{R}^n$. First use a forward sweep to evaluate $f(x)$ and $D_qf=
abla f(x)^Tq$. Then apply reverse-mode differentiation to the computed scalar function $D_qf$. At the independent-variable nodes, the reverse sweep produces
\[
 rac{\partial}{\partial x_i} igl(
abla f(x)^Tq igr)=[
abla^2f(x)q]_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Under the operation-count model stated in the extract, one Hessian–vector product costs approximately twelve times an evaluation of $f$, independently of $n$. Repetition with $q=e_1,\ldots,e_n$ recovers the full Hessian with an increase of at most approximately $12n$. If the Hessian sparsity structure is known and $N_c(
abla^2f)$ coloring seed vectors suffice for recovery, the corresponding increase is up to approximately $12N_c(
abla^2f)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward sweep computes the directional derivative of the scalar function, after which a reverse sweep differentiates that directional derivative. The input adjoints are the components of the Hessian–vector product. In the extract's operation-count model, one product costs a constant factor over evaluating the function; coordinate seeds recover the full Hessian, while graph-coloring seeds can reduce the number of sweeps when the Hessian's sparsity pattern is known.

N_c(\nabla^2f)\text{ denotes the number of seed vectors used for sparse Hessian recovery}

children.top_down_role: Residual- and gradient-difference products used when differentiated actions are unavailable.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On Using Approximate Finite Differences in Matrix-Free Newton–Krylov Methods
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: On Using Approximate Finite Differences in Matrix-Free Newton–Krylov Methods

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x\), and \(v\ne0\).
\(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is three times continuously differentiable when the gradient-difference Hessian formula is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_hF(x)[v]=J_F(x)v+O(h\lVert v\rVert_2^2)\) and \(G_hf(x)[v]=\nabla^2f(x)v+O(h\lVert v\rVert_2^2)\) as \(h\to0\).

notation.meaning: Forward finite-difference action on the residual or map.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-difference approximations in exact arithmetic; step selection is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonzero \(h\), define the residual-difference action
\[
D_hF(x)[v]=\frac{F(x+h v)-F(x)}{h},
\]
and, when gradients are available, define
\[
G_hf(x)[v]=\frac{\nabla f(x+h v)-\nabla f(x)}{h}.
\]
Taylor expansion gives \(D_hF(x)[v]=J_F(x)v+O(h\lVert v\rVert_2^2)\) and \(G_hf(x)[v]=\nabla^2f(x)v+O(h\lVert v\rVert_2^2)\) as \(h\to0\), with constants locally uniform for bounded directions. These actions require function or gradient evaluations but no derivative matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward differences of residuals approximate Jacobian products, while forward differences of gradients approximate Hessian products, both with first-order truncation error.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Operator Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward residual- and gradient-difference formulas and their exact-arithmetic first-order truncation estimates are consistent with the stated smoothness and scope, but no finite-difference source is supplied.

children.title: Analytic Operator Actions
children.top_down_role: Hand-derived derivative-product interfaces using problem-specific analytic structure.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) has an available analytic derivative formula at \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The analytic action returns exactly \(DF(x)[v]=J_F(x)v\) in exact arithmetic, evaluated from the derivative formula without assembling the full Jacobian.

notation.meaning: Derivative of the model at the evaluation point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact matrix-free evaluation from a derived derivative formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An analytic operator action for a differentiable map \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is an implementation \(\mathcal A_F\) obtained from an explicit derivative formula and satisfying
\[
\mathcal A_F(x;v)=DF(x)[v]=J_F(x)v
\]
for every admissible \(x\in U\) and \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), in exact arithmetic. The implementation evaluates contractions, local linearized equations, or structured recurrences supplied by that formula, but does not need to assemble the complete matrix \(J_F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analytic operator action evaluates an explicitly derived directional derivative exactly in exact arithmetic without assembling the full derivative matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Operator Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the analytic-action leaf, but the assumptions provide an analytic derivative formula only at one point while the statement quantifies over every admissible point. No source establishes the intended operator domain or implementation notion.

children.title: Complex-Step Operator Actions
children.top_down_role: Complex-step product evaluation within compatible numerical software.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a holomorphic extension to a complex neighborhood of the real point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Im}F(x+i h v)/h=J_F(x)v+O(h^2\lVert v\rVert_2^3)\) as \(h\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward complex-step Jacobian action under holomorphic extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) extend holomorphically near the real point \(x\) and be real-valued on real inputs. For a real direction \(v\), the complex-step action is
\[
C_hF(x)[v]=\frac{\operatorname{Im}F(x+i h v)}{h}.
\]
Taylor expansion in the scalar parameter gives
\[
C_hF(x)[v]=J_F(x)v+O(h^2\lVert v\rVert_2^3)
\]
as \(h\to0\). The formula avoids subtracting two nearby real function values, but it is valid only when the evaluated computation preserves the required complex differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The imaginary part of a holomorphic model evaluated at a complex perturbation gives a second-order-accurate Jacobian action without real subtraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Complex-Step Operator Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The holomorphic complex-step formula, error order, and stated failure boundary are mathematically appropriate for this leaf, but no authoritative complex-step citation with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Hybrid Operator Actions
children.top_down_role: Mixed analytic-numerical interfaces assembled from heterogeneous derivative sources.

assumptions_latex: \(F=F_k\circ\cdots\circ F_1\) is a differentiable composition at \(x\).
Each component action \(A_j(z;u)\) is declared and approximates or equals \(J_{F_j}(z)u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The propagated action \(u_j=A_j(z_{j-1};u_{j-1})\) returns \(u_k\), which equals \(J_F(x)v\) when every component action is exact.

notation.meaning: Chosen analytic or numerical component action.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional mixing of exact and approximate derivative actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=F_k\circ\cdots\circ F_1\), compute primal states by \(z_0=x\) and \(z_j=F_j(z_{j-1})\). Initialize \(u_0=v\), choose for each component an analytic, algorithmically differentiated, complex-step, or finite-difference action \(A_j\), and update
\[
u_j=A_j(z_{j-1};u_{j-1}),\qquad j=1,\ldots,k.
\]
Return \(u_k\). If every \(A_j(z;u)=J_{F_j}(z)u\), the chain rule yields \(u_k=J_F(x)v\). Otherwise, \(u_k\) is a hybrid approximation whose validity requires a separately declared component-error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid action propagates a direction through a composition while choosing an analytic or numerical derivative product separately for each component.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Operator Actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-component case follows the chain rule and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. The approximate hybrid case deliberately leaves its component-error model unspecified, and no source supports the proposed hybrid construction.

children.title: Operator Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and structural mismatches capable of invalidating the algebraic geometry assumed by inner solvers.

children.title: Finite-Difference Precision Boundary
children.top_down_role: Noisy and finite-precision regimes affecting approximate products.

children.title: Differencing Noise
children.top_down_role: Perturbation-sensitive product estimates affected by noisy function or residual evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Differencing Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error boundary for finite-difference Hessian–vector products formed from noisy gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=\nabla f\), and suppose the available gradient is \(\widehat g(y)=g(y)+e(y)\), with \(\|e(y)\|\leq\varepsilon(y)\). For \(h>0\), define \(D_hv=(\widehat g(x+hv)-\widehat g(x))/h\). If \(\nabla^2 f\) is \(\rho\)-Lipschitz near the segment from \(x\) to \(x+hv\), then
\[
\|D_hv-\nabla^2 f(x)v\|\leq \frac{\rho h}{2}\|v\|^2+\frac{\varepsilon(x+hv)+\varepsilon(x)}{h}.
\]
Thus decreasing \(h\) reduces truncation error but amplifies gradient-evaluation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-difference Hessian action has truncation error proportional to the step and gradient-noise error inversely proportional to the step.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|D_hv-\nabla^2 f(x)v\|\leq \rho h\|v\|^2/2+(\varepsilon(x+hv)+\varepsilon(x))/h\).

notation.meaning: Forward-difference approximation to the Hessian action on v.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Taylor remainder and additive-noise decomposition for finite-difference Hessian actions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound and failure-boundary classification are mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the precise Lipschitz-Hessian remainder and additive-noise formula.

children.title: Subtractive Cancellation
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision loss arising when nearby evaluations are differenced.

knowledge_statements.title: Subtractive Cancellation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point cancellation boundary for forward-difference matrix-free products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under a floating-point model with unit roundoff \(u\), the computed difference \(\operatorname{fl}(g(x+hv)-g(x))\) can incur absolute error of order \(u(\|g(x+hv)\|+\|g(x)\|)\). After division by \(h\), the induced error in the forward-difference Hessian action therefore scales as
\[
O\!\left(\frac{u(\|g(x+hv)\|+\|g(x)\|)}{h}\right).
\]
When \(g(x+hv)\) and \(g(x)\) are close relative to their magnitudes, their significant common digits cancel, so taking \(h\) smaller can reduce rather than improve accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting nearly equal gradients loses significant digits; division by a small perturbation then magnifies the floating-point error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cancellation contribution to the action error is \(O(u(\|g(x+hv)\|+\|g(x)\|)/h)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cancellation scaling is standard, but its precise big-O claim requires a cited floating-point model specifying the subtraction and gradient-evaluation errors.

children.title: Perturbation-Scale Conflict
children.top_down_role: Regimes where truncation sensitivity conflicts with noise or roundoff sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Scale Conflict
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balancing boundary for a model upper bound containing competing truncation and evaluation-error terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an operator-action error \(E(h)\) satisfies \(E(h)\leq ah+b/h\) for every \(h>0\), where \(a>0\) and \(b>0\). The model bound \(M(h)=ah+b/h\) is minimized at
\[
h_*=\sqrt{b/a},\qquad M(h_*)=2\sqrt{ab}.
\]
Thus \(h\ll h_*\) makes the noise term \(b/h\) dominate the model bound, whereas \(h\gg h_*\) makes the truncation term \(ah\) dominate. The positive minimum is a floor for this bound, not necessarily a lower bound on the actual error \(E(h)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model error bound balances truncation against noise at the square-root step size. Its positive minimum is a floor for the bound, not necessarily for the actual error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_*=\sqrt{b/a}\) minimizes \(M(h)=ah+b/h\), and \(M(h_*)=2\sqrt{ab}\).

notation.meaning: Actual operator-action error at perturbation scale h.
Perturbation scale minimizing the model bound.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary minimization of the canonical finite-difference error model

children.title: Operator Reciprocity Consistency Boundary
children.top_down_role: Product mismatches that disrupt symmetric Krylov or least-squares interpretations.

children.title: Symmetry Inconsistency
children.top_down_role: Departures from self-adjoint behavior in nominally symmetric curvature products.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative self-adjointness consistency test for a matrix-free operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be a linear matrix-free action. Its symmetry defect is
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{sym}}(B)=\sup_{u,v\neq0}\frac{|u^{\mathsf T}Bv-v^{\mathsf T}Bu|}{\|u\|\,\|v\|}.
\]
The action is exactly symmetric in the Euclidean inner product if and only if \(\delta_{\mathrm{sym}}(B)=0\). A positive defect is a symmetry inconsistency; a tolerance-based interface declares consistency only when \(\delta_{\mathrm{sym}}(B)\leq\tau\) for a prescribed \(\tau\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free action is symmetric exactly when reciprocal bilinear products agree for every pair of vectors; their normalized worst-case mismatch measures inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: The domain uses the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) if and only if \(\delta_{\mathrm{sym}}(B)=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operator-norm characterization of Euclidean self-adjointness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized bilinear defect correctly characterizes Euclidean symmetry for a linear finite-dimensional action, and condition is an appropriate kind for this consistency test, but no citation is supplied.

children.title: Adjoint Inconsistency
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between forward products and their supplied transpose actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocity test between independently implemented forward and adjoint actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(A^\sharp:Y\to X\) be linear actions on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, where \(A^\sharp\) is intended to implement the adjoint of \(A\). Define
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{adj}}(A,A^\sharp)=\sup_{x\neq0,\,y\neq0}\frac{|\langle Ax,y\rangle_Y-\langle x,A^\sharp y\rangle_X|}{\|x\|_X\|y\|_Y}.
\]
The implementations are adjoint-consistent exactly when \(\delta_{\mathrm{adj}}(A,A^\sharp)=0\). Any positive value measures a failure of the defining adjoint identity and can invalidate algorithms relying on reciprocal forward and reverse products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and claimed adjoint actions are consistent exactly when their inner products satisfy the adjoint identity for every input pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^\sharp=A^*\) if and only if \(\delta_{\mathrm{adj}}(A,A^\sharp)=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining inner-product identity for an adjoint operator
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The defect correctly characterizes equality with the adjoint in finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, but the record has no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Krylov Compatibility Loss
children.top_down_role: Solver-family restrictions caused by inconsistent symmetry or adjoint structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Compatibility Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for fixed symmetric-operator Krylov recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classical conjugate-gradient and symmetric Lanczos recurrences require every product to equal \(Bv\) for one fixed self-adjoint operator \(B\). If iteration \(k\) instead returns \(B_kv\), and there exist indices \(i\neq j\) and a vector \(v\) such that \(B_iv\neq B_jv\), then no iteration-independent operator represents both actions on \(v\). Consequently, generated vectors need not belong to a single sequence \(\mathcal K_m(B,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Br_0,\ldots,B^{m-1}r_0\}\), and the usual three-term recurrence, orthogonality, and finite-termination interpretations are no longer justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If repeated products do not come from one fixed self-adjoint operator, classical CG or Lanczos vectors need not form a single Krylov sequence.
assumptions_latex: Products at iteration \(k\) are generated by linear actions \(B_k\).
The Krylov method assumes one fixed self-adjoint operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B_iv\neq B_jv\) for some \(i\neq j\), the actions cannot all represent one fixed operator on \(v\).

notation.meaning: Operator action used at iteration k.
Order-m Krylov subspace generated by B and the initial residual.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed-operator requirement in classical CG and Lanczos constructions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-operator incompatibility observation is sound, but the broader claims about CG/Lanczos recurrences, orthogonality, and finite termination require an authoritative Krylov-method locator.

children.title: Nonstationary Operator Action Boundary
children.top_down_role: State changes, randomized evaluation, and parallel variability within nominally fixed operator applications.

children.title: State-Dependent Operator Actions
children.top_down_role: Nominally fixed inner operators altered by changing nonlinear or cached state.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Operator Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstationarity caused by changing the state underlying a matrix-free derivative action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a state set, let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, and let \(H(z):V\to W\) be linear for every \(z\in Z\). During one inner solve, query \(k\) returns \(H(z_k)v_k\). The realized queries are compatible with a fixed linear operator precisely when there exists a linear map \(B:V\to W\) such that \(Bv_k=H(z_k)v_k\) for every query \(k\). They admit a frozen-state interpretation at \(\bar z\in Z\) when \(H(\bar z)v_k=H(z_k)v_k\) for every query \(k\). In particular, if the same direction \(v\) is queried at indices \(i\) and \(j\) and \(H(z_i)v\neq H(z_j)v\), no fixed operator can represent both returned actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing states need not destroy fixed-operator compatibility on the queried directions, but different outputs for the same repeated direction rule out any single fixed operator.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a state set and \(V,W\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
For each \(z\in Z\), \(H(z):V\to W\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(v_i=v_j\) and \(H(z_i)v_i\neq H(z_j)v_j\) for some \(i\neq j\), no linear map \(B:V\to W\) satisfies \(Bv_k=H(z_k)v_k\) for every query \(k\).

notation.meaning: Putative fixed linear operator matching all realized queries.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic compatibility of queried actions with a fixed linear map

children.title: Randomized Operator Actions
children.top_down_role: Product variability introduced by sampling or randomized evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Operator Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-operator boundary for stochastic matrix-free products using fresh randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and let \(B:V\to W\) be linear. Suppose query \(k\) returns \(Y_k(v)=Bv+\xi_k(v)\), where \(\mathbb E[\xi_k(v)\mid v]=0\). Unbiasedness identifies only the conditional mean action: \(\mathbb E[Y_k(v)\mid v]=Bv\). If, for some fixed \(v\in V\), repeated-query errors \(\xi_i(v)\) and \(\xi_j(v)\) are independent and identically distributed and satisfy \(\mathbb E\|\xi_k(v)\|^2>0\), then \(Y_i(v)\neq Y_j(v)\) with positive probability. Hence fresh randomized realizations do not define one deterministic fixed action pathwise without additional coupling or consistency structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased randomized product equals the target only in expectation. With fresh independent nondegenerate noise, repeated calls on the same vector can differ and therefore do not form one deterministic fixed action.
assumptions_latex: \(V,W\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces and \(B:V\to W\) is linear.
For the repeated direction under consideration, the errors are independent and identically distributed across the two calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathbb E\|\xi_k(v)\|^2>0\), then independent repeated calls on \(v\) return different values with positive probability and cannot represent one deterministic fixed action pathwise.

notation.meaning: Random action returned by query k.
Random action error for query k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distinction between unbiased oracle actions and pathwise fixed operators under fresh sampling

children.title: Parallel Reproducibility Loss
children.top_down_role: Application-to-application variation caused by concurrency or reduction ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Reproducibility Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonreproducibility induced by order-dependent parallel floating-point dot products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_i\), and suppose a floating-point dot product is evaluated without overflow or underflow in arithmetic with unit roundoff \(u\). Under the standard model, each admissible reduction order satisfies
\[
|\widehat s-s|\leq\gamma_n\sum_{i=1}^n|a_i b_i|,
\qquad \gamma_n=\frac{nu}{1-nu},
\]
provided \(nu<1\). Consequently, results \(\widehat s_1\) and \(\widehat s_2\) from two such orders satisfy
\[
|\widehat s_1-\widehat s_2|\leq2\gamma_n\sum_{i=1}^n|a_i b_i|.
\]
Because floating-point addition is not associative, the two results need not be equal. Schedule-dependent reductions inside matrix-free products can therefore make repeated actions non-bitwise-reproducible and can violate an exact fixed-operator interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different valid parallel reduction orders can return different floating-point dot products. This can make repeated matrix-free actions non-bitwise-reproducible and exactly nonstationary.
assumptions_latex: No overflow or underflow occurs during the dot-product computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two admissible reduction orders satisfy \(|\widehat s_1-\widehat s_2|\leq2\gamma_n\sum_{i=1}^n|a_i b_i|\), although their results need not be equal.

notation.meaning: Standard accumulated rounding-error factor for the dot product.
Dot-product results from two admissible reduction orders.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard floating-point dot-product error model

children.title: Fixed-Operator Assumption Failure
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where classical fixed-operator Krylov interpretations cease to apply.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Operator Assumption Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic boundary separating a fixed linear action from a varying oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A deterministic oracle \(\mathcal O(k,v)\) represents one fixed linear operator \(B\) exactly when it is independent of \(k\) and, as a function of \(v\), satisfies
\[
\mathcal O(k,\alpha u+\beta v)=\alpha\mathcal O(k,u)+\beta\mathcal O(k,v)
\]
for all vectors \(u,v\), scalars \(\alpha,\beta\), and query indices \(k\). Thus iteration dependence, failure of additivity, or failure of homogeneity rules out the model \(\mathcal O(k,v)=Bv\). Algorithms whose derivation assumes powers or polynomials of one operator then require a variable-operator reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed matrix model fails whenever the action depends on the query index or violates linearity in its vector argument.
assumptions_latex: The vector domain and codomain are finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed linear \(B\) exists exactly when \(\mathcal O\) is query-independent and linear in \(v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic characterization of a deterministic fixed linear operator
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic characterization of a deterministic fixed linear oracle is correct and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent and iteration cost of an SPG-based inexact projected Newton step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee for early termination of the inner SPG solve, together with the stated limited-memory implementation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration $k$, let $Q^k(x)=f(x^k)+(x-x^k)^T\nabla f(x^k)+\frac12(x-x^k)^TH^k(x-x^k)$ with $H^k\succ0$. If an SPG inner solve over $\Omega$ is initialized at $x^k$ and produces $z^k$ with $Q^k(z^k)<Q^k(x^k)=f(x^k)$, then $(z^k-x^k)^T\nabla f(x^k)<0$. In particular, the first Armijo-accepted SPG iterate and every subsequent accepted iterate provide a descent direction, so the inner solve may be terminated after any positive number of iterations. If $H^k=\sigma^kI-NM^{-1}N^T$ is an L-BFGS compact representation with $N\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times2m}$, projection costs $O(n)$, and at most $c$ inner iterations are used, the outer-iteration cost is $O(mnc)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic Newton model, any inner SPG iterate that lowers the model below its value at the current point defines a strict descent direction for the original objective. Starting SPG at the current point gives this property after the first Armijo-accepted iteration and thereafter, permitting safe early termination. With a compact L-BFGS model, linear-time projection, and at most c inner steps, the work per outer iteration is O(mnc).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (z^k-x^k)^T\nabla f(x^k)<0,\qquad \operatorname{cost\ per\ outer\ iteration}=O(mnc)

children.title: Fixed-Quality Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy maintained at a uniform relative level.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Quality Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform relative residual condition for inexact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For solving \(F(x)=0\), an inexact Newton step \(s_k\) has fixed quality \(\bar\eta\in[0,1)\) when its linear residual
\[
r_k=F'(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)
\]
satisfies \(\|r_k\|\leq\bar\eta\|F(x_k)\|\) at every iteration. Equivalently, the forcing terms may vary but obey \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\). This condition demands a uniform relative reduction by the inner solve while not requiring its accuracy to increase as \(x_k\) approaches a root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inner Newton solve reduces its linear residual by the same uniform relative factor, without progressively tightening the requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is differentiable at each \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|F'(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\bar\eta\|F(x_k)\|\) for every \(k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical relative-residual definition of an inexact Newton step
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform relative-residual condition correctly expresses fixed-quality inexactness and condition is the appropriate content kind, but an authoritative inexact-Newton source is required.

children.title: Vanishing Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy tightened as the nonlinear iteration approaches a solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local superlinear inexact Newton result with nonnegative vanishing forcing terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(x_*\), let \(F'(x_*)\) be nonsingular, and suppose \(F'\) is Lipschitz near \(x_*\). Assume \(x_k\to x_*\), define \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and let the forcing terms satisfy \(\eta_k\geq0\), \(\eta_k\to0\), and
\[
\|F'(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
Then, unless a root is reached in finitely many iterations, the iterates converge \(q\)-superlinearly:
\[
\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular root with a Lipschitz derivative, convergent inexact Newton iterates are q-superlinear when their nonnegative relative forcing terms vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable and has a locally Lipschitz derivative near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unless \(x_k=x_*\) for some finite \(k\), \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|/\|x_k-x_*\|\to0\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative relative forcing term for the kth inner solve.
Root at which the Jacobian is nonsingular.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical local inexact Newton forcing-term theorem

children.title: Higher-Order Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy matched to higher-order local Newton behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence order for inexact Newton iterations with residuals matched to the nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(x_*\), with \(J(x_*)\) nonsingular and \(J\) locally Lipschitz. Suppose \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\), where \(\|r_k\|\leq \eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). If \(\eta_k=O(\!\left(\|F(x_k)\|^q\right)\!)\) for some \(q>0\), then, for sufficiently close \(x_0\), \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O\!\left(\|x_k-x_*\|^{\min\{2,1+q\}}\right).\] In particular, \(q\geq1\) preserves quadratic local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forcing term of residual order q yields local order min(2,1+q); linear residual matching preserves quadratic Newton convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable and \(J\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x_*\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the nonlinear residual map
residual of the approximate Newton equation

review_flags: Exact local-order theorem requires an authoritative inexact-Newton source.

children.title: Conditioning-Sensitive Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Limits of residual-based accuracy when the Newton operator is ill-conditioned or nearly singular.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Sensitive Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual accuracy does not uniformly control step accuracy near singular or ill-conditioned Newton operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an invertible Newton matrix \(J_k\), let \(s_k^*=-J_k^{-1}F_k\) and let \(J_ks_k=-F_k+r_k\), with \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F_k\|\). Then \[\frac{\|s_k-s_k^*\|}{\|s_k^*\|}\leq \kappa(J_k)\eta_k,\qquad \kappa(J_k)=\|J_k\|\,\|J_k^{-1}\|.\] Hence a fixed residual tolerance gives no uniform relative-step guarantee when \(\kappa(J_k)\) is unbounded. To target relative step error at most \(\varepsilon\), the sufficient residual rule \(\eta_k\leq\varepsilon/\kappa(J_k)\) becomes arbitrarily stringent as \(J_k\) approaches singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative linear residual can amplify into relative step error by the Newton matrix condition number, failing near singularity.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\) is invertible in the chosen induced norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s_k-s_k^*\|/\|s_k^*\|\leq\kappa(J_k)\eta_k\), so residual control is nonuniform as \(\kappa(J_k)\to\infty\).
review_flags: Condition-number bound is standard but lacks a supplied supporting locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number bound is standard and the failure_boundary kind fits, but no inspectable source locator supports the claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Iteration and Descent from Truncated Positive-Definite Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic definition, exact quadratic behavior, local contraction, and a descent certificate for approximate Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\). When \(
abla^2F(x(t))\) is invertible, Newton's update is \[x(t+1)=x(t)-\gamma[
abla^2F(x(t))]^{-1}
abla F(x(t)).\] If \(F(x)=	frac12x^	op Ax-x^	op b\), \(A\) is invertible, and \(\gamma=1\), then one step gives \(x(t+1)=A^{-1}b\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer with \(
abla^2F(x^*)\succ0\), then for every norm and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that the full Newton step satisfies \[\|x(t+1)-x^*\|\le\alpha\|x(t)-x^*\|\quad	ext{whenever }\|x(t)-x^*\|\le\epsilon.\] For an approximate Newton step, set \(H=
abla^2F(x(t))\), \(g=
abla F(x(t))\), and compute \(\widehat s\) by finitely iterating on \(Hs=-g\). If \(g
eq0\), \(H\) is symmetric positive definite, the inner method strictly decreases \(q(s)=	frac12s^	op Hs+g^	op s\), and its initial point satisfies \(	frac12s_0^	op Hs_0\le-g^	op s_0\), then \[q(\widehat s)<0\quad	ext{and hence}\quad g^	op\widehat s<0.\] Thus \(\widehat s\) is a descent direction and \(x(t+1)=x(t)+\gamma\widehat s\) is an approximate Newton update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton uses the inverse Hessian times the gradient. With a unit step it solves an invertible quadratic problem in one iteration, and near a nondegenerate local minimizer its contraction factor can be made arbitrarily small. An approximate Newton direction obtained by truncating a quadratic-decreasing iterative solve is still descending when the Hessian is symmetric positive definite and the stated initialization condition holds.

F(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-x^\top b,\ A\text{ invertible},\ \gamma=1\quad\text{for one-step convergence}
x^*\text{ is a local minimizer and }\nabla^2F(x^*)\succ0\quad\text{for local contraction}
q(s)=\tfrac12s^\top Hs+g^\top s\text{ is strictly decreased by the inner iteration}

children.title: Prescribed Forcing Schedules
children.top_down_role: Iteration-indexed accuracy policies chosen independently of observed model behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Prescribed Forcing Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An iteration-indexed inexact Newton policy fixed before observing nonlinear model behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and a prescribed sequence \((\eta_k)_{k\geq0}\subset[0,\bar\eta]\) with \(\bar\eta<1\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\varepsilon\): use a Krylov method to compute \(s_k\) satisfying \[\|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\] globalize the trial step if required, and set \(x_{k+1}\) to the accepted iterate. The values \(\eta_k\) depend only on the iteration index and predetermined parameters, not on measured residual reduction, model agreement, or acceptance history. Output the first iterate satisfying the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predetermined sequence sets each Krylov residual tolerance independently of observed nonlinear progress or step acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\) at every completed inner solve.
review_flags: Prescribed-schedule formulation needs an inexact Newton–Krylov source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches a prescribed iteration-indexed forcing policy, but no source supports the stated Newton–Krylov formulation or safeguards.

children.title: Residual-Adaptive Forcing
children.top_down_role: Accuracy policies driven by nonlinear residual evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Adaptive Forcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A forcing schedule updated from successive nonlinear residual norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\), \(0<\eta_{\max}<1\), \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), \(\alpha\in(1,2]\), and \(\eta_0\in[0,\eta_{\max}]\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \(s_k\) such that \[\|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\] accept or globalize \(x_k+s_k\), and, after an accepted update, set \[\eta_{k+1}=\min\left\{\eta_{\max},\gamma\left(\frac{\|F(x_{k+1})\|}{\|F(x_k)\|}\right)^{\alpha}\right\}.\] Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\). Thus unexpectedly weak nonlinear reduction tightens subsequent inner accuracy relative to schedules based solely on iteration count only when the chosen formula dictates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next Krylov tolerance is computed from the observed ratio of consecutive nonlinear residual norms.
review_flags: The selected residual-ratio schedule is one specific family and requires source confirmation.
Check whether the intended node instead requires an Eisenstat–Walker model-mismatch formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-ratio update is a specific, noncanonical schedule requiring a source. Moreover, the final LaTeX sentence suggests weak reduction tightens accuracy, whereas the displayed formula generally makes eta larger when the residual ratio is larger.

children.title: Globalization-Aware Forcing
children.top_down_role: Accuracy policies coordinated with step acceptance and model agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Globalization-Aware Forcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner tolerance updates coupled to step acceptance and agreement between predicted and actual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\eta_{\min}\leq\eta_{\\max}<1\), \(0<\tau_-<1<\tau_+\), and let \(\rho_k\) denote the globalization agreement ratio for a trial step computed to forcing term \(\eta_k\). Choose thresholds \(0<\rho_-<\rho_+<1\). After the trial, update \[\eta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\max\{\eta_{\min},\tau_-\eta_k\},&\rho_k<\rho_-\text{ or the step is rejected},\\ \eta_k,&\rho_-\leq\rho_k<\rho_+,\\ \min\{\eta_{\max},\tau_+\eta_k\},&\rho_k\geq\rho_+.\end{cases}\] Retry rejected steps under the globalization mechanism and output an accepted iterate satisfying the outer stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poor agreement or rejection tightens the next inner solve; strong agreement permits a looser tolerance within fixed safeguards.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k\) compares actual with predicted reduction for the same trial step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The forcing term is tightened after poor agreement and may be relaxed after strong agreement.
review_flags: Generic policy needs a source and may require adaptation to the chapter's intended globalization scheme.
Formula is a representative safeguarded interface, not a claimed canonical update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representative acceptance-ratio policy lacks a supporting source, and poor agreement does not universally justify tighter inner solves. The token \eta_{\\max} is malformed TeX and must be corrected once the intended sourced policy is established.

children.title: Inner-Accuracy Work-Reliability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Work imbalance and unreliable-step regimes caused by mismatched inner accuracy.

children.title: Inner Oversolving
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy regimes whose computational expense exceeds their outer-step value.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Oversolving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner residual accuracy substantially stronger than needed for the attainable outer convergence order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume local quadratic inexact Newton convergence is already guaranteed whenever \(\eta_k=O(\!\left(\|F(x_k)\|\right)\!)\). A schedule oversolves asymptotically if \[\eta_k=o\!\left(\|F(x_k)\|\right).\] Under this stronger condition, the local outer order cannot exceed the quadratic order imposed by a Lipschitz Jacobian, while a Krylov work model \(W_k(\eta)\) that increases as \(\eta\downarrow0\) assigns at least as much inner work as the order-preserving schedule. Thus the additional residual reduction has no asymptotic outer-order benefit and can increase total operator products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving much more accurately than the quadratic-order requirement can add Krylov work without improving the attainable outer order.
assumptions_latex: The Jacobian is locally Lipschitz and nonsingular at the root.
Inner work \(W_k(\eta)\) is nonincreasing in the allowed tolerance \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k=o(\|F(x_k)\|)\) cannot improve the attainable order beyond two but may increase inner work.

notation.meaning: inner work required at tolerance eta

review_flags: Oversolving boundary and work conclusion require a supporting inexact Newton–Krylov reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Inner Oversolving, but the asymptotic threshold and operator-product consequence depend on an explicit inexact-Newton convergence theorem and inner-work model, neither of which is cited.

children.title: Inner Undersolving
children.top_down_role: Inner accuracy regimes producing unreliable or ineffective outer steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Undersolving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Realized inner residuals too large to support superlinear local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x_*\), where \(F(x_*)=0\), \(J(x_*)\) is nonsingular, and \(J\) is continuous. Define the realized relative linear residual by \[\theta_k=\frac{\|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|}{\|F(x_k)\|}.\] Superlinear inexact Newton convergence requires \(\theta_k\to0\). Consequently, if \(\theta_k\geq c>0\) along an infinite subsequence, the standard vanishing-residual condition fails and superlinear convergence is not ensured; persistent inner truncation can leave only a linear local rate. The statement concerns realized residuals, since a loose requested tolerance may accidentally be exceeded by the inner solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If realized relative linear residuals do not vanish, the usual guarantee of superlinear inexact Newton convergence is lost.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable near \(x_*\), with continuous Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Superlinear convergence requires \(\theta_k\to0\); a positive subsequential lower bound violates this requirement.
review_flags: Necessity statement requires an authoritative local-convergence theorem and its precise hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The realized-residual distinction is appropriate, but the claimed necessity of theta_k tending to zero requires a precise theorem and regularity hypotheses from an authoritative source.

children.title: Accuracy-Work Imbalance
children.top_down_role: The boundary between useful residual reduction and disproportionate inner work.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Work Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto domination of an inner-accuracy policy in work and outer reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a problem instance, stopping rule, and admissible policy class \(\mathcal{P}\). For \(p\in\mathcal{P}\), let \(W(p)\) be total inner operator products and let \(R(p)\) be a scalar reliability measure, ordered so that larger values are better. Policy \(p\) exhibits accuracy-work imbalance if there exists \(q\in\mathcal{P}\) such that \[W(q)\leq W(p),\qquad R(q)\geq R(p),\] with at least one inequality strict. Equivalently, \((W(p),-R(p))\) is not Pareto minimal. The comparison is meaningful only when both policies use the same outer stopping, failure accounting, and operator-product cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accuracy policy is imbalanced when another admissible policy uses no more work, is no less reliable, and improves one criterion.
assumptions_latex: Policies are compared on the same problem instance and outer stopping rule.
\(W\) and \(R\) use common cost and reliability conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is imbalanced exactly when it is Pareto dominated in \((W,-R)\).

notation.meaning: total inner work of policy p
outer reliability score of policy p

review_flags: Operational Pareto formulation is locally natural but lacks a supplied canonical source.
Reliability metric must be specialized before empirical use.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a locally constructed Pareto definition rather than a sourced mathematical condition. A source or explicit standard-field rationale is required, and the reliability functional must be specialized for the statement to be operational.

children.title: Newton–Krylov Globalization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Outer frameworks that consume approximate Newton directions and inner-solve diagnostics.

children.title: Line-Search Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Descent-oriented coupling between approximate Newton directions and line-search acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo globalization of an approximate Newton direction for a smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\), \(c\in(0,1)\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), at iteration \(k\) use Krylov products with \(H_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)\) to compute \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|H_ks_k+g_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and require \(g_k^{\mathsf T}s_k<0\). Choose the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \[f(x_k+\beta^{j_k}s_k)\leq f(x_k)+c\beta^{j_k}g_k^{\mathsf T}s_k,\] set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^{j_k}s_k\), and stop when \(\|g_k\|\leq\varepsilon\). If the Krylov step is not descent, modify or replace it before line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Krylov-computed approximate Newton descent direction is shortened until it satisfies Armijo sufficient decrease.
assumptions_latex: The accepted search direction satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}s_k<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)+c\beta^{j_k}g_k^{\mathsf T}s_k\).
review_flags: Supplied line-search locator concerns derivative-free simplex models, not Newton–Krylov directions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Line-Search Newton–Krylov, but no Newton–Krylov-specific source is supplied. The available derivative-free line-search inventory does not support the Hessian–Krylov construction or descent-direction safeguard.

children.title: Trust-Region Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Restricted-step coupling using residual, curvature, and boundary information from the inner process.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free approximate minimization of a quadratic Newton model inside a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), form \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}H_ks\) through Hessian-vector products. Use a truncated Krylov method to return \(s_k\) with \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\), stopping on an inner residual test, detected nonpositive curvature, or the trust-region boundary. Define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] Accept \(x_k+s_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\rho_{\mathrm{acc}}\); otherwise retain \(x_k\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit enlargement after strong agreement with a boundary-active step. Stop when the prescribed outer stationarity test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated Krylov solve supplies a curvature-aware trust-region step, accepted according to actual versus predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted steps satisfy \(\rho_k\geq\rho_{\mathrm{acc}}\) and \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).

children.title: Regularized Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Stabilized Newton models for singular, indefinite, or poorly scaled regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shifted matrix-free Newton equations stabilize indefinite or nearly singular Hessian models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), gradient \(g_k\), symmetric Hessian operator \(H_k\), and \(\lambda_k\geq0\), use a Krylov method to compute \(s_k\) satisfying \[\|(H_k+\lambda_k I)s_k+g_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|.\] Choose or increase \(\lambda_k\) until the shifted model has adequate positive curvature and the trial step meets the globalization acceptance test; decrease it after successful, well-predicted steps. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) only upon acceptance and stop at the outer stationarity tolerance. If \(\lambda_k>-\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\), then \(H_k+\lambda_k I\) is positive definite, so the exact shifted step is a descent direction when \(g_k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative spectral shift stabilizes the Newton equation; globalization adjusts the shift according to curvature and step success.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) is symmetric and accessed through products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k+\lambda_k I\succ0\), and the exact shifted step satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}s_k<0\) for \(g_k\neq0\).
review_flags: Regularized Newton–Krylov update and globalization details need a supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shifted-system calculation is standard and the algorithm kind fits, but the regularization update, curvature criterion, and globalization interface have no supporting locator and are not specified precisely enough as a canonical algorithm.

children.title: Continuation-Stabilized Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Continuation and pseudo-transient interfaces for difficult nonlinear systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation-Stabilized Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudo-transient continuation regularizes Newton steps and approaches Newton’s method as stabilization vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(x_0\), nonsingular \(M\), and \(\tau_0>0\), compute at iteration \(k\) a Krylov step \(s_k\) satisfying \[\|(\tau_k^{-1}M+J(x_k))s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] Accept or damp \(x_k+s_k\) using a residual-reduction test. Increase \(\tau_k\) after reliable reduction and decrease it after rejection or poor agreement. Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\). Since \(\tau_k^{-1}M\to0\) when \(\tau_k\to\infty\), accepted steps asymptotically recover the ordinary inexact Newton equation, while finite \(\tau_k\) supplies continuation stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudo-time regularization stabilizes early Krylov solves and fades toward the ordinary inexact Newton equation as the time step grows.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable on the region traversed by the iterates.
\(M\) is a fixed nonsingular scaling or mass matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\tau_k\to\infty\), then \(\tau_k^{-1}M+J(x_k)\) approaches \(J(x_k)\).
review_flags: Pseudo-transient Newton–Krylov formulation and update policy require an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pseudo-transient form fits the node, but nonsingularity of M alone does not ensure stabilization. The mass-matrix assumptions, acceptance rule, and tau update require an authoritative pseudo-transient Newton–Krylov source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobi–Davidson iteration for the leftmost eigenpair of a symmetric matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ritz extraction, optional search-space contraction, approximate correction solve, and orthonormal expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=A^T and let V_1=[v_1|\cdots|v_{k_0}] have k_0\ge1 orthonormal columns. For k=1,2,\ldots, form H_k=V_k^TAV_k; compute a normalized leftmost eigenpair (\rho_k,y_k) of H_k; set x_k=V_ky_k; optionally replace V_k by V_k[y_k^{(1)}|\cdots|y_k^{(j_{\min})}] using the j_{\min} leftmost eigenvectors of H_k; approximately solve the Jacobi correction equation for s_k; and orthonormalize [V_k|s_k] to obtain V_{k+1}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct, condensed, and preconditioned iterative solution of primal–dual barrier systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebra realizations and conditioning boundaries for nonlinear-programming primal–dual interior-point steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\) in the symmetric primal–dual barrier system. Eliminating \(p_s\) gives
\[
K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A_E^T&A_I^T\\A_E&0&0\\A_I&0&-\Sigma^{-1}\end{bmatrix},
\]
and eliminating \(p_z\) further gives the condensed matrix
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H+A_I^T\Sigma A_I&A_E^T\\A_E&0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
A symmetric-indefinite direct factorization has the form \(P^TKP=LBL^T\), where \(B\) has \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks. As \(\mu\to0\), entries of \(\Sigma\) can tend to both \(0\) and \(+\infty\), yet a stable direct factorization is usually accurate unless some \(s_i\) or \(z_i\) is extremely small or \(H\) or \(A_E\) is nearly rank deficient. Iterative solution requires scaling and structured preconditioning: if \(SZ\approx\mu I\), then \(S\Sigma S\approx\mu I\), \(S\Sigma S/\mu\to I\), and the scaling \(\widetilde p_s=\Sigma^{1/2}p_s\) normalizes the \(\Sigma\)-block. Indefinite full systems call for methods such as GMRES, QMR, or LSQR; CG is appropriate only after a null-space reduction yields a positive-definite reduced system. A constraint preconditioner may retain \(A_E,A_I\) while using \(G\) positive definite on their null space and diagonal \(T\approx\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal–dual barrier equations can be reduced first to a three-block symmetric KKT system and then to a smaller condensed equality-constrained system. Stable symmetric-indefinite factorization is generally reliable despite barrier-induced ill conditioning, with loss of accuracy concentrated near vanishing slacks or multipliers and nearly rank-deficient Hessian or equality-Jacobian blocks. Iterative solution needs barrier scaling plus problem-structured preconditioning; general indefinite solvers apply to the full systems, while conjugate gradients require a positive-definite null-space reduction.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the stated asymptotic scalings, }SZ\approx\mu I\text{ as }\mu\to0.
\text{For reduced-space CG, the reduced operator is positive definite; for the constraint preconditioner, }G\succ0\text{ on the constraint null space and }T\approx\Sigma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The barrier KKT system admits the stated eliminations and direct factorization; reliable iterative solution requires scaling and structured preconditioning, and CG requires a positive-definite reduced space.}

children.title: Newton–Conjugate Gradient
children.top_down_role: Positive-curvature Newton models solved through conjugate-gradient subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton–Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free truncated CG for a symmetric positive-definite local Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a point \(x\), gradient \(g=\nabla f(x)\), symmetric positive-definite Hessian model \(H\), tolerance \(\eta\in[0,1)\), and initial step \(p_0=0\), apply conjugate gradients to \(Hp=-g\) using only products \(v\mapsto Hv\). With residual \(r_j=Hp_j+g\), terminate at the first \(j\) satisfying \(\|r_j\|\leq \eta\|g\|\), and return \(p_j\). In exact arithmetic the iterates satisfy \(p_j\in\mathcal K_j(H,-g)\) and minimize \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\) over \(\mathcal K_j(H,-g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradients approximately solves the positive-definite Newton system using Hessian-vector products, returning the first Krylov step meeting the prescribed relative residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice differentiable at \(x\).
Arithmetic is exact for the Krylov minimization property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_j\in\mathcal K_j(H,-g)\), \(p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal K_j(H,-g)}q(p)\), and \(\|Hp_j+g\|\leq\eta\|g\|\) at termination.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic separability in conjugate directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a quadratic objective expressed in coordinates along mutually conjugate search directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\), where \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\), and suppose \(h_i^{\mathsf T}Ah_j=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\). Then
\[
F\!\left(x_1+\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i h_i\right)=F(x_1)+\sum_{i=1}^d\left[\lambda_i h_i^{\mathsf T}(Ax_1+c)+\tfrac12\lambda_i^2h_i^{\mathsf T}Ah_i\right].
\]
Consequently, minimizing over \((\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)\) is separable and may be performed by successively solving \(d\) one-dimensional quadratic problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic objective, all cross terms vanish in mutually conjugate directions. Minimization over their coefficients therefore separates into d scalar quadratic minimizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d}F\!\left(x_1+\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i h_i\right)\text{ separates into }d\text{ one-dimensional quadratic problems.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consequences of Mutually Conjugate Search Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of the conjugate-direction iterates through the last nonzero mutually A-conjugate direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose s(0),s(1),\ldots,s(t) are nonzero and mutually A-conjugate. Then they are linearly independent; g(k+1)^\top s(i)=0 for 0\le i\le k\le t; for every k\in\{0,\ldots,t+1\}, x(k) minimizes F over M_k=\{x(0)+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\alpha_j s(j):\alpha_j\in\mathbb R\}; and F(x(k+1))\le F(x(k)) for every k\le t.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonzero mutually A-conjugate search directions are linearly independent. Each new gradient is orthogonal to all preceding search directions, every iterate minimizes the objective over the affine space generated by the directions used so far, and the objective values are nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{s(0),\ldots,s(t)\}\text{ is linearly independent},\quad g(k+1)^\top s(i)=0\ (0\le i\le k\le t),\quad x(k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in M_k}F(x)\ (0\le k\le t+1),\quad F(x(k+1))\le F(x(k))\ (k\le t).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate gradients on a tangent space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-gradient iteration for a positive-definite tangent-space system arising in Newton-step computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M be positive definite and let 0\ne b\in T_x\mathcal M. Set v_0=0, r_0=b, and p_0=r_0. For n=1,2,\ldots, compute Hp_{n-1} and set \alpha_n=\frac{\|r_{n-1}\|_x^2}{\langle p_{n-1},Hp_{n-1}\rangle_x},\quad v_n=v_{n-1}+\alpha_np_{n-1},\quad r_n=r_{n-1}-\alpha_nHp_{n-1}. If r_n=0, return s=v_n, which solves Hs=b. Otherwise set \beta_n=\frac{\|r_n\|_x^2}{\|r_{n-1}\|_x^2} and p_n=r_n+\beta_np_{n-1}, and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite operator on a tangent space and a nonzero right-hand side, conjugate gradients updates its iterate, residual, and conjugate search direction. If the residual becomes zero, the current iterate solves the linear system.
assumptions_latex: H:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\text{ is positive definite}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_n=0\implies H v_n=b

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-gradient identity and exact CG termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual identity and termination characterization for Algorithm 6.2 and its associated positive-definite quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Algorithm 6.2 generates v_0,\ldots,v_n and r_0,\ldots,r_n before termination, then r_n=-\operatorname{grad}g(v_n)=b-Hv_n. Consequently, Algorithm 6.2 terminates with v_n if and only if v_n minimizes g.
