knowledge_statements.title: Lanczos Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric Krylov compression of a matrix-free Newton quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and define \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\). Run \(j\) Lanczos steps from \(v_1=g/\|g\|_2\) without breakdown. The orthonormal matrix \(V_j=[v_1,\ldots,v_j]\) and symmetric tridiagonal matrix \(T_j\) satisfy \(V_j^{\mathsf T}HV_j=T_j\) and \(HV_j=V_jT_j+\beta_{j+1}v_{j+1}e_j^{\mathsf T}\). Consequently, for \(p=V_jy\), \(q(V_jy)=\|g\|_2e_1^{\mathsf T}y+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}T_jy\); every negative eigenvalue of \(T_j\) identifies a negative-curvature direction within \(\operatorname{range}(V_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos represents a symmetric Newton quadratic on an orthonormal Krylov basis by a small symmetric tridiagonal matrix, including any negative curvature present in that subspace.
assumptions_latex: No Lanczos breakdown occurs before step \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_j^{\mathsf T}HV_j=T_j\) and \(q(V_jy)=\|g\|_2e_1^{\mathsf T}y+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}T_jy\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-term Lanczos basis recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned Lanczos construction for a symmetric Krylov space in exact arithmetic, through the last nonzero normalization coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H=H^T\) and \(r_0\), initialize \(y_0=r_0\) and \(q_{-1}=0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), whenever \(\gamma_k=\|y_k\|_2>0\), compute \[q_k=\frac{y_k}{\gamma_k},\qquad \delta_k=\langle q_k,Hq_k\rangle,\qquad y_{k+1}=Hq_k-\delta_kq_k-\gamma_kq_{k-1}.\] In exact arithmetic, the generated vectors constitute the stated orthonormal basis of the corresponding Krylov space until breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize the current Lanczos residual, compute its Rayleigh coefficient, and obtain the next residual with the symmetric three-term recurrence. The process continues only while the normalization coefficient is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_k=\frac{y_k}{\gamma_k},\quad \delta_k=q_k^THq_k,\quad y_{k+1}=Hq_k-\delta_kq_k-\gamma_kq_{k-1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degeneracy of a Krylov space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditions associated with loss of full Krylov-space growth in the Lanczos setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=U\Lambda U^T\), where the columns of \(U\) are orthonormal eigenvectors of \(H\), and let \(r_0\in\mathbb R^n\). The Krylov space is called degenerate if \((U^Tr_0)_j=0\) for some \(j\), or if \(\lambda_j=0\) for some \(j\). In the stated spectral-growth setting, if neither event occurs, the Krylov space expands to \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric matrix with eigenvector matrix U, the Krylov space is termed degenerate when the starting vector has zero component in at least one eigendirection or when the matrix has a zero eigenvalue. In the stated spectral-growth setting, absent both events the space grows to all of R^n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\left[\exists j:(U^Tr_0)_j=0\right]\lor\left[\exists j:\lambda_j=0\right]\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{Krylov degeneracy};\qquad \left[\forall j,
(U^Tr_0)_j\ne0,\ \lambda_j\ne0\right]\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal K(H,r_0,\cdot)=\mathbb R^n

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned three-term Lanczos recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preliminary preconditioned Lanczos recurrence with M-weighted normalization; no orthogonality or convergence guarantee is asserted by this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(r_0\) and a matrix \(M\) for which the displayed inverse operations exist, initialize \(y_0=M^{-1}r_0\) and \(q_{-1}=0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), whenever \(\langle y_k,My_k\rangle>0\), compute \[\gamma_k=\sqrt{\langle y_k,My_k\rangle},\qquad q_k=\frac{y_k}{\gamma_k},\qquad \delta_k=\langle q_k,Hq_k\rangle,\] \[y_{k+1}=M^{-1}Hq_k-\delta_kq_k-\gamma_kq_{k-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the preconditioned residual, normalize using the displayed M-weighted quadratic form, compute the H-Rayleigh coefficient, and update with the three-term recurrence involving M^{-1}H. The iteration is defined only while the inverse operations exist and the normalization quantity is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_k=\sqrt{y_k^TMy_k},\quad q_k=\frac{y_k}{\gamma_k},\quad \delta_k=q_k^THq_k,\quad y_{k+1}=M^{-1}Hq_k-\delta_kq_k-\gamma_kq_{k-1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned Lanczos recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The recurrence is valid at every iteration before a zero or undefined normalization causes breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(r_0\), initialize \(t_0=r_0\) and \(w_{-1}=0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set \(y_k=M^{-1}t_k\), \(\gamma_k=\sqrt{\langle t_k,y_k\rangle}\), \(w_k=t_k/\gamma_k\), \(q_k=y_k/\gamma_k\), \(\delta_k=\langle q_k,Hq_k\rangle\), and \(t_{k+1}=Hq_k-\delta_k w_k-\gamma_k w_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from t_0=r_0 and w_{-1}=0, each preconditioned Lanczos step applies the inverse preconditioner to t_k, normalizes the resulting pair, computes the projected coefficient from H, and forms the next recurrence vector. The iteration proceeds only while the inverse application and positive normalization are well defined.
assumptions_latex: M^{-1}t_k\ \text{is defined for every performed iteration }k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge 0\ \text{before breakdown},\quad (y_k,\gamma_k,w_k,q_k,\delta_k,t_{k+1})\ \text{are generated by the stated preconditioned Lanczos recurrence}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Theorem for Real Symmetric Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real spectral theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, then it has \(n\) real eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\), counted with multiplicity, and corresponding eigenvectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) that form an orthonormal basis of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric n-by-n matrix has n real eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, and an orthonormal basis of corresponding eigenvectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lanczos recurrence in transformed coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The three-term Lanczos construction applied to the barred matrix and residual variables, through the last nonzero normalization coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix \(\bar H\) and \(\bar r_0\), initialize \(\bar y_0=\bar r_0\) and \(\bar q_{-1}=0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), whenever \(\gamma_k=\|\bar y_k\|_2>0\), compute \[\bar q_k=\frac{\bar y_k}{\gamma_k},\qquad \delta_k=\langle\bar q_k,\bar H\bar q_k\rangle,\qquad \bar y_{k+1}=\bar H\bar q_k-\delta_k\bar q_k-\gamma_k\bar q_{k-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the standard three-term Lanczos recurrence to the barred matrix and residual variables, stopping if a normalization coefficient vanishes.

children.title: Symmetric Minimum-Residual Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Residual-oriented inner solves for indefinite or singular symmetric systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Minimum-Residual Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MINRES-type inner Newton solve for symmetric indefinite or singular models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix \(H\), gradient \(g\), initial step \(p_0=0\), and tolerance \(\eta\in[0,1)\), construct the Lanczos basis for \(\mathcal K_j(H,-g)\). At iteration \(j\), choose \(p_j\) to minimize \(\|Hp+g\|_2\) over \(p\in\mathcal K_j(H,-g)\). Stop when \(\|Hp_j+g\|_2\leq\eta\|g\|_2\), or report the attained minimum residual if the Krylov space becomes invariant first. This residual minimization remains well-defined when \(H\) is indefinite and, for singular consistent systems, returns a solution upon zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric minimum-residual method minimizes the Newton-equation residual on successive Lanczos spaces and remains applicable to indefinite or singular symmetric systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal K_j(H,-g)}\|Hp+g\|_2\), with the stated residual stopping rule.

notation.meaning: symmetric Newton matrix or Hessian model

children.title: Arnoldi Newton Projections
children.top_down_role: Hessenberg-based projected Newton models for general square Jacobians.

knowledge_statements.title: Arnoldi Newton Projections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal Krylov reduction of a general Newton Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), nonzero residual \(b\), and \(v_1=b/\|b\|_2\), \(j\) Arnoldi steps without breakdown produce orthonormal \(V_{j+1}\) and upper-Hessenberg \(\bar H_j\) satisfying \(JV_j=V_{j+1}\bar H_j\). Every projected Newton correction has the form \(p=V_jy\), and its linearized residual obeys \(\|b-Jp\|_2=\|\|b\|_2e_1-\bar H_jy\|_2\). Thus the large residual-minimization problem on \(\mathcal K_j(J,b)\) is represented by a \((j+1)\)-by-\(j\) least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arnoldi orthogonalization compresses a general Jacobian and converts Newton residual minimization on a Krylov space into a small Hessenberg least-squares problem.
assumptions_latex: No Arnoldi breakdown occurs before step \(j\).

notation.meaning: Arnoldi basis for the Krylov space
negative nonlinear residual defining the Newton equation

children.title: GMRES Newton Solves
children.top_down_role: Residual-minimizing Newton inner solves over Arnoldi-generated spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: GMRES Newton Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestarted GMRES as an inexact inner solve for a general Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At nonlinear iterate \(x_k\), set \(F_k=F(x_k)\), \(J_k=F'(x_k)\), and choose a forcing term \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\). Starting with \(p_0=0\), Arnoldi-GMRES selects \(p_j\in\mathcal K_j(J_k,-F_k)\) minimizing \(\|J_kp+F_k\|_2\). Stop at the first \(j\) for which \(\|J_kp_j+F_k\|_2\leq\eta_k\|F_k\|_2\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_j\), subject to any outer globalization rule. Jacobian actions may be supplied without forming \(J_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GMRES computes a matrix-free inexact Newton correction by minimizing the linearized residual over an Arnoldi Krylov space until the forcing tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal K_j(J_k,-F_k)}\|J_kp+F_k\|_2\), and termination implies \(\|J_kp_j+F_k\|_2\leq\eta_k\|F_k\|_2\).

notation.meaning: nonlinear residual at the current iterate

children.title: Residual-Minimization Geometry
children.top_down_role: Residual interpretations linking the projected representation to the Newton correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Minimization Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonality characterization of a minimum-residual Newton projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a linear subspace. A vector \(p_*\in S\) minimizes \(\|b-Jp\|_2\) over \(p\in S\) if and only if its residual \(r_*=b-Jp_*\) is orthogonal to \(JS\); equivalently, \(\langle r_*,Js\rangle=0\) for every \(s\in S\). For \(S=\mathcal K_j(J,b)\), the GMRES residual is therefore orthogonal to \(J\mathcal K_j(J,b)\), and successive unrestarted residual norms are nonincreasing because the trial spaces are nested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-residual Newton correction is characterized by residual orthogonality to the Jacobian image of the trial space; nested Krylov spaces make residual norms nonincreasing.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in S}\|b-Jp\|_2\iff b-Jp_*\perp JS\).

notation.meaning: image of the trial subspace under the Jacobian

children.title: Restarted Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Cycle-based Krylov methods limiting stored basis vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-memory restarted GMRES for an inexact Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Jp=b\), restart length \(m\geq1\), initial correction \(p^{(0)}=0\), and tolerance \(\tau>0\), define \(r^{(\ell)}=b-Jp^{(\ell)}\). During cycle \(\ell\), perform at most \(m\) Arnoldi steps and choose \(s^{(\ell)}\in\mathcal K_m(J,r^{(\ell)})\) minimizing \(\|r^{(\ell)}-Js\|_2\). Set \(p^{(\ell+1)}=p^{(\ell)}+s^{(\ell)}\), discard the cycle basis, and restart from \(r^{(\ell+1)}\). Return the first correction satisfying \(\|r^{(\ell)}\|_2\leq\tau\); otherwise report nonconvergence at a prescribed cycle limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarted Newton–Krylov repeatedly minimizes the linearized residual in an m-dimensional Krylov space, discarding each basis to cap storage before starting another cycle.
assumptions_latex: Restart length \(m\geq1\) and tolerance \(\tau>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each completed cycle satisfies \(\|r^{(\ell+1)}\|_2\leq\|r^{(\ell)}\|_2\), while storing at most \(m+1\) Arnoldi vectors per cycle.

notation.meaning: correction at the start of cycle l

children.title: Short-Recurrence Newton–Krylov
children.top_down_role: Memory-limited Krylov methods using compact recurrence structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Short-Recurrence Newton–Krylov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory reduction through operator-compatible Krylov recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Newton equation \(Ap=b\), a short-recurrence Krylov implementation generates each new basis or search vector from a number of preceding vectors bounded independently of the iteration index, while using products with \(A\) and any stated preconditioner. Symmetric positive-definite \(A\) permits the conjugate-gradient three-term structure; symmetric indefinite \(A\) permits Lanczos-based minimum-residual recurrences. For a general nonsymmetric \(A\), the Arnoldi orthogonalization coefficients against all previous basis vectors are generally nonzero, so exact unrestarted residual minimization does not generically admit fixed storage through the same recurrence mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short recurrences give fixed vector storage when the Newton operator has compatible symmetry; general nonsymmetric residual minimization normally requires growing Arnoldi storage or restarts.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) defines the linearized Newton equation.
Claims concern exact-arithmetic Krylov constructions without special additional matrix structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Symmetry supports fixed-length Lanczos recurrences, whereas a general nonsymmetric Arnoldi reduction has iteration-dependent orthogonalization and storage.

children.title: Restart Information Loss
children.top_down_role: Convergence degradation caused by discarding useful subspace information.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Information Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of the accumulated Arnoldi search space at a restart boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After an unrestarted \(k\)-step GMRES cycle from residual \(r_0\), the correction lies in \(\mathcal K_k(J,r_0)\), and the resulting residual \(r_k\) is orthogonal to \(J\mathcal K_k(J,r_0)\). Restarting preserves that correction and residual at the boundary, but discarding the Arnoldi basis removes the stored subspace and its Ritz data. The next increments are restricted to \(\mathcal K_m(J,r_k)\), which need not contain the earlier directions, and residuals produced later need not remain orthogonal to \(J\mathcal K_k(J,r_0)\). Consequently, after the same total number of matrix-vector products, restarted GMRES can have a larger residual norm than unrestarted GMRES.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarting initially preserves the current correction, residual, and completed-cycle orthogonality, but discards the basis and Ritz data; later cycles need not retain the earlier projection conditions and can converge more slowly than unrestarted GMRES.
assumptions_latex: No retained or augmented Krylov vectors are carried across cycles.
The comparison uses exact-arithmetic GMRES iterates from the same initial residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restart preserves \(r_k\perp J\mathcal K_k(J,r_0)\) at the boundary, but later restarted residuals need not preserve this orthogonality because their increments are generated from \(\mathcal K_m(J,r_k)\).

notation.meaning: j-th Krylov space generated by J and r

children.title: Recurrence Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Operator regimes restricting stable short-recurrence formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Recurrence Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary separating Lanczos short recurrences from general Arnoldi orthogonalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_j\) be an orthonormal Krylov basis. If \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\), the projected matrix \(V_j^{\mathsf T}AV_j\) is symmetric Hessenberg and therefore tridiagonal, yielding a three-term Lanczos recurrence. If symmetry is removed, Arnoldi gives an upper-Hessenberg projection whose entries above the first subdiagonal may all be nonzero. Consequently, a generic nonsymmetric Newton Jacobian cannot use the Lanczos three-term recurrence while retaining an orthonormal basis and the exact unrestarted minimum-residual projection; one must accept growing orthogonalization, restart or truncate, or exploit additional operator structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The three-term Lanczos recurrence relies on symmetry. A generic nonsymmetric Jacobian produces a dense upper-Hessenberg projection, forcing growing storage, restarting, truncation, or extra structure.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and the Krylov basis is Euclidean-orthonormal.
The comparison concerns exact Arnoldi and Lanczos projections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\) implies a tridiagonal Krylov projection; without symmetry, an upper-Hessenberg projection is generically not tridiagonal.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Krylov Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free Krylov solution of a Gauss–Newton least-squares subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\), let \(J=F'(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(r=F(x)\in\mathbb R^m\). If \(J^{\mathsf T}r=0\), return \(p=0\). Otherwise, for \(j\geq1\), generate \(S_j=\mathcal K_j(J^{\mathsf T}J,-J^{\mathsf T}r)\) using products with \(J\) and \(J^{\mathsf T}\), without explicitly forming \(J^{\mathsf T}J\), and choose \(p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in S_j}\|Jp+r\|_2\). Stop when a prescribed residual or normal-residual tolerance is met. The subspace optimality condition is \(J^{\mathsf T}(Jp_j+r)\perp S_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-squares Krylov Newton method minimizes the linearized nonlinear residual over a normal-residual Krylov space, using Jacobian and adjoint products without explicitly forming the normal matrix.
assumptions_latex: Products with \(J\) and \(J^{\mathsf T}\) are available.
The Krylov iteration is performed in exact arithmetic for the stated subspace characterization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(S_j=\mathcal K_j(J^{\mathsf T}J,-J^{\mathsf T}r)\), \(p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in S_j}\|Jp+r\|_2\) and \(J^{\mathsf T}(Jp_j+r)\perp S_j\).

children.title: Normal-Equation Routes
children.top_down_role: Square inner representations formed through normal-equation structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-equation representation of a rectangular Gauss–Newton subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^m\). A vector \(p_*\) minimizes \(\|Jp+r\|_2\) if and only if it satisfies the normal equations \(J^{\mathsf T}Jp_*=-J^{\mathsf T}r\). If \(J\) has full column rank, \(J^{\mathsf T}J\) is positive definite and the minimizer is unique, so conjugate gradients may be applied through products \(v\mapsto J^{\mathsf T}(Jv)\). In the Euclidean norm, the nonzero singular values are squared, giving \(\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}J)=\kappa_2(J)^2\) for full-column-rank \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangular least squares can be represented by symmetric normal equations, enabling CG but squaring the Jacobian’s spectral condition number when it has full column rank.
assumptions_latex: For uniqueness and the condition-number identity, \(J\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_p\|Jp+r\|_2\iff J^{\mathsf T}Jp_*=-J^{\mathsf T}r\), and \(\kappa_2(J^{\mathsf T}J)=\kappa_2(J)^2\) under full column rank.

children.title: Augmented-System Routes
children.top_down_role: Coupled square representations retaining primal and residual-space variables.

assumptions_latex: The step solves the linear least-squares model \(\min_s \tfrac12\lVert Js+r\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any solution of the augmented system yields a least-squares stationary step without explicitly forming \(J^T J\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric augmented formulation of an unregularized rectangular least-squares Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The first-order condition for \(\min_{s\in\mathbb{R}^n}\tfrac12\lVert Js+r\rVert_2^2\) admits the augmented representation
\[
\begin{pmatrix}I_m&J\\J^T&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}y\\s\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}-r\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its first block equation gives \(y=-(r+Js)\), while its second gives \(J^Ty=0\). Eliminating \(y\) therefore produces \(J^TJs=-J^Tr\). Conversely, every least-squares stationary step \(s\) extends to an augmented-system solution by setting \(y=-(r+Js)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rectangular least-squares step can be computed from a symmetric augmented system whose elimination recovers the normal equations without explicitly forming their coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Routes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The augmented representation is mathematically consistent and fits the representation leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Conditioning Amplification
children.top_down_role: Numerical sensitivity associated with transformed rectangular problems.

assumptions_latex: Condition numbers use the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(J^TJ)=\kappa_2(J)^2\), so the normal-equation representation squares spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic spectral conditioning of full-column-rank normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because the eigenvalues of \(J^TJ\) are the squared singular values of \(J\),
\[
\kappa_2(J^TJ)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(J^TJ)}{\lambda_{\min}(J^TJ)}
=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(J)^2}{\sigma_{\min}(J)^2}
=\kappa_2(J)^2.
\]
Thus replacing a rectangular least-squares system by its normal equations amplifies ill-conditioning quadratically. In particular, if \(\kappa_2(J)=\varepsilon^{-1/2}\), then \(\kappa_2(J^TJ)=\varepsilon^{-1}\), placing the normal-equation coefficient matrix at the corresponding precision scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-column-rank matrix, forming normal equations squares the spectral condition number and can substantially magnify numerical sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Amplification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-column-rank condition-number identity is correct and the property kind fits, but the record has no citation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Representation choice should balance conditioning, storage, symmetry, definiteness, preconditioning, and available matrix-free products.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection principle for matrix-free rectangular Newton and Gauss–Newton subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose normal equations for a well-preconditioned positive-definite reduction; choose an augmented system to avoid squared conditioning or explicit product formation.

children.top_down_role: Classical truncated-CG family for large-scale trust-region models.

knowledge_statements.title: Steihaug–Toint Truncated CG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical matrix-free truncated CG for a Euclidean trust-region quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^TBs\). Initialize \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=g\), and \(p_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(j\), if \(p_j^TBp_j\leq0\), choose the positive forward boundary intersection \(\tau_j\) satisfying \(\lVert s_j+\tau_jp_j\rVert_2=\Delta\) and return \(s_j+\tau_jp_j\). Otherwise set \(\alpha_j=(r_j^Tr_j)/(p_j^TBp_j)\). If \(\lVert s_j+\alpha_jp_j\rVert_2\geq\Delta\), choose \(\tau_j\in(0,\alpha_j]\) satisfying \(\lVert s_j+\tau_jp_j\rVert_2=\Delta\) and return \(s_j+\tau_jp_j\). If the boundary is not reached, set \(s_{j+1}=s_j+\alpha_jp_j\) and \(r_{j+1}=r_j+\alpha_jBp_j\). Return \(s_{j+1}\) when the declared residual stopping test holds; otherwise set \(\beta_{j+1}=(r_{j+1}^Tr_{j+1})/(r_j^Tr_j)\), set \(p_{j+1}=-r_{j+1}+\beta_{j+1}p_j\), and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated CG applies explicit conjugate-gradient recurrences until the residual test succeeds, the trust-region boundary is reached, or nonpositive curvature is detected; every returned step is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The declared residual stopping test is evaluated before a recurrence requiring division by a zero residual norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a feasible step after residual convergence, boundary intersection, or detection of nonpositive curvature.

notation.meaning: conjugate-gradient search direction at iteration j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated conjugate gradients for a tangent-space trust-region subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Steihaug–Toint truncated CG instantiated on the inner-product tangent space of a smooth manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $H:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M$ be self-adjoint, $b\in T_x\mathcal M$, $\Delta>0$, $\kappa\ge 0$, and $\theta\in(0,1]$. For $m(s)=\tfrac12\langle s,Hs\rangle_x-\langle b,s\rangle_x$ subject to $\|s\|_x\le\Delta$, initialize $v_0=0$, $r_0=b$, and $p_0=r_0$; return $v_0$ if $r_0=0$. At iteration $n\ge1$, compute $Hp_{n-1}$ and $q_n=\langle p_{n-1},Hp_{n-1}\rangle_x$. If $q_n\le0$, return $v_{n-1}+tp_{n-1}$ with $t\ge0$ chosen so that $\|v_{n-1}+tp_{n-1}\|_x=\Delta$. Otherwise set $\alpha_n=\|r_{n-1}\|_x^2/q_n$ and $v_{n-1}^+=v_{n-1}+\alpha_np_{n-1}$. If $\|v_{n-1}^+\|_x\ge\Delta$, return $v_{n-1}+tp_{n-1}$ with $t\ge0$ chosen so that its norm is $\Delta$. Otherwise set $v_n=v_{n-1}^+$ and $r_n=r_{n-1}-\alpha_nHp_{n-1}$. Return $v_n$ if $\|r_n\|_x\le\|r_0\|_x\min\{\|r_0\|_x^\theta,\kappa\}$; otherwise set $\beta_n=\|r_n\|_x^2/\|r_{n-1}\|_x^2$, $p_n=r_n+\beta_np_{n-1}$, and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply conjugate-gradient recurrences to the self-adjoint tangent-space quadratic model. Return a boundary point upon nonpositive curvature or when the next CG iterate reaches or crosses the trust-region boundary; otherwise return when the prescribed residual tolerance is met.
assumptions_latex: H:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\text{ is self-adjoint}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\in T_x\mathcal M,\qquad \|s\|_x\le\Delta,\qquad s\text{ is the tCG approximate solution returned for }\min_{\|u\|_x\le\Delta}\left(\tfrac12\langle u,Hu\rangle_x-\langle b,u\rangle_x\right).

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On the Generalized Lanczos Trust-Region Method

assumptions_latex: Lanczos products with \(B\) are computed in exact arithmetic for the stated representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the reduced trust-region problem gives the best model value over the current Krylov subspace and retains projected indefinite-curvature information.

notation.meaning: Lanczos basis of the Krylov subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean Lanczos reduction underlying generalized large-scale trust-region solvers.

source_refs.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Starting with \(q_1=g/\lVert g\rVert_2\), perform \(k\) Lanczos steps to obtain an orthonormal matrix \(Q_k\) and symmetric tridiagonal matrix \(T_k=Q_k^TBQ_k\). Solve
\[
y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lVert y\rVert_2\leq\Delta}
\left(\lVert g\rVert_2e_1^Ty+\tfrac12y^TT_ky\right),
\qquad s_k=Q_ky_k.
\]
Increase \(k\) until a prescribed projected optimality or model-quality test holds. Each \(s_k\) minimizes the quadratic model over \(\mathcal{K}_k(B,g)\cap\{s:\lVert s\rVert_2\leq\Delta\}\), including boundary solutions generated by negative Ritz values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos projects the trust-region model onto a growing Krylov subspace, where a small tridiagonal trust-region problem retains boundary and indefinite-curvature information.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Lanczos Trust-Region Methods

children.title: Spectral Degeneracy Boundary
children.top_down_role: Spectral degeneracy regimes requiring more than ordinary residual reduction.

children.title: Trust-Region Hard Case
children.top_down_role: Degenerate trust-region models whose decisive direction is weakly represented by ordinary Krylov progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Hard Case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical hard case for the Euclidean quadratic trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{\lVert s\rVert_2\leq\Delta} g^Ts+\tfrac12s^TBs\), and let \(\lambda_1<0\) be the smallest eigenvalue of \(B\). The hard case is the situation in which \(g\perp\ker(B-\lambda_1I)\), the optimal multiplier is \(\lambda_*=-\lambda_1\), and the minimum-norm shifted solution \(s_p=-(B-\lambda_1I)^\dagger g\) satisfies \(\lVert s_p\rVert_2<\Delta\). Then \(B+\lambda_*I=B-\lambda_1I\) is singular, and an optimizer is \(s_*=s_p+z\), where \(z\in\ker(B-\lambda_1I)\) is chosen so that \(\lVert s_p+z\rVert_2=\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the trust-region hard case, the gradient is orthogonal to the leftmost eigenspace and the singular shifted solution lies inside the trust region, so a leftmost-eigenspace component must complete the step to the boundary.
assumptions_latex: The smallest eigenvalue \(\lambda_1\) of \(B\) is negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the stated hard-case conditions hold, the optimal multiplier is \(-\lambda_1\) and an extremal-eigenspace component supplies the missing boundary norm.

notation.meaning: minimum-norm solution of the singular shifted equation

children.title: Near-Singular Newton Models
children.top_down_role: Newton systems with poorly identified directions near the operator null space.

assumptions_latex: \(B=B^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular but \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\) is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small residual alone need not control step error or norm when \(B\) is near singular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual sensitivity boundary for symmetric near-singular Newton equations.

source_refs.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_*=-B^{-1}g\) and let \(r=B\widehat{s}+g\) be the residual of an approximate Newton step. Then
\[
\widehat{s}-s_*=B^{-1}r,
\qquad
\lVert\widehat{s}-s_*\rVert_2\leq\frac{\lVert r\rVert_2}{\sigma_{\min}(B)}.
\]
This amplification factor is sharp along a singular vector belonging to \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\). Consequently, as \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\to0\), a fixed normwise residual tolerance ceases to imply a uniformly accurate or bounded Newton step; regularization, a trust-region constraint, or a scaled stopping test is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near singularity, inverse-Hessian amplification makes a small Newton residual compatible with a large step error, motivating regularization or trust-region control.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singular Newton Models

source_witnesses.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

children.title: Degenerate Spectral Separation
children.top_down_role: Regimes where critical eigeninformation cannot be cleanly distinguished.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Spectral Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-gap boundary for matrix-free detection of leftmost curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the leftmost spectral gap by \(\gamma=\lambda_2-\lambda_1\). If \(\gamma>0\), the leftmost eigenspace is one-dimensional and an approximate Ritz vector may be assessed relative to a distinguished eigenvector up to sign. When \(\gamma=0\), the eigenvalue \(\lambda_1\) is multiple: individual eigenvectors in \(\mathcal{E}_1=\ker(B-\lambda_1I)\) are not identifiable, although the invariant subspace remains meaningful. As \(\gamma\downarrow0\), perturbation and Krylov convergence estimates that depend inversely on \(\gamma\) lose uniform force. Curvature certification should then use invariant-subspace or Rayleigh-quotient information rather than a uniquely oriented eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the leftmost spectral gap vanishes, individual extreme eigenvectors are nonunique and gap-dependent Krylov identification guarantees become unstable.
assumptions_latex: A Krylov method estimates the leftmost eigenspace from matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\lambda_2-\lambda_1\) vanishes, a uniquely oriented leftmost eigenvector and inverse-gap convergence guarantees cease to be stable.

children.title: Krylov Curvature Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Inner-solve information used to distinguish adequate solutions, nonpositive curvature, near-null directions, and stagnation.

children.title: Linear Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Normwise progress measures for approximate Newton equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise certificate for an approximate matrix-free Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(s\), compute \(r=Bs+g\). The inequality \[\lVert r\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\eta\lVert g\rVert_2,\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0,\qquad 0\leq\eta<1\] is a directly verifiable linear residual certificate. With \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}=0\), it is the relative inexact Newton condition \(\lVert Bs+g\rVert_2\leq\eta\lVert g\rVert_2\). The certificate measures equation satisfaction only; even when \(B\) is invertible, it does not bound \(\lVert s+B^{-1}g\rVert_2\) without conditioning information for \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed Newton residual certifies absolute or relative equation accuracy, but it does not alone certify step accuracy for an ill-conditioned Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the target equation is \(Bs=-g\).
An approximate step \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and the product \(Bs\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable residual norm certifies satisfaction of the inexact Newton equation at the declared absolute or relative tolerance.

children.title: Model-Decrease Certificates
children.top_down_role: Projected-model quality measures supporting outer acceptance decisions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar \(-g^Ts-	frac12s^TBs\) certifies predicted decrease and can be compared with an explicit benchmark.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable predicted-decrease certificate for quadratic trust-region steps.

source_refs.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any feasible trial step \(s\), its predicted decrease is exactly
\[
D(s)=q(0)-q(s)=-g^Ts-	frac12s^TBs.
\]
Thus \(D(s)>0\) certifies strict model improvement. A stronger, scale-aware certificate compares this value with the Cauchy benchmark: if \(g\neq0\), define \(s_C=-t_Cg\), where \(t_C\) minimizes \(q(-tg)\) over \(0\leq t\leq\Delta/\lVert g\rVert_2\). The check \(D(s)\geq\theta D(s_C)\), with declared \(0<\theta\leq1\), certifies a specified fraction of Cauchy decrease using matrix-vector products and scalar inner products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predicted reduction is directly computable; comparison with the Cauchy step certifies a declared fraction of baseline trust-region model decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Decrease Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

children.title: Nonpositive-Curvature Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Krylov and spectral indicators of indefinite or weakly identified models.

children.title: Negative-Curvature Certificates
children.top_down_role: Inner-solve evidence identifying directions with indefinite model curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rayleigh-quotient certificate of strict negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((d,Bd)\) is a negative-curvature certificate with margin \(\gamma>0\) when \[d\neq0,\qquad d^TBd\leq-\gamma\lVert d\rVert_2^2.\] This verifiable inequality implies \(\lambda_{\min}(B)\leq\rho(d)\leq-\gamma<0\), where \(\rho(d)=d^TBd/(d^Td)\). Hence \(B\) is not positive semidefinite. For a trust-region quadratic \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^TBs\), the sign of \(d\) may be chosen so that \(g^Td\leq0\), providing a feasible negative-curvature search direction after appropriate truncation to the trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector with a Rayleigh quotient at most minus the declared margin certifies Hessian indefiniteness and provides a negative-curvature direction for a trust-region model.
assumptions_latex: A nonzero vector \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the product \(Bd\), and a margin \(\gamma>0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Rayleigh quotient no greater than \(-\gamma\) certifies that \(B\) is not positive semidefinite.

source_refs.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

source_witnesses.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

children.title: Near-Null-Curvature Certificates
children.top_down_role: Inner-solve evidence identifying weakly determined curvature directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Null-Curvature Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free certificate distinguishing small directional curvature from approximate nullspace membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directional near-null-curvature certificate is \[d\neq0,\qquad |d^TBd|\leq\tau\lVert d\rVert_2^2,\] equivalently \(|\rho(d)|\leq\tau\). This certifies only that the quadratic form is small along \(d\); cancellation between positive and negative spectral components may produce the same result. The stronger approximate-nullspace certificate \[\lVert Bd\rVert_2\leq\tau\lVert d\rVert_2\] implies \(\min_i|\lambda_i(B)|\leq\tau\) and verifies that \(d\) has a small operator residual for eigenvalue zero. The tolerance \(\tau\) must be reported together with the scaling used for \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Rayleigh quotient certifies weak directional curvature; a small operator residual additionally certifies that the spectrum lies within the declared tolerance of zero.
assumptions_latex: A nonzero vector \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the product \(Bd\), and a tolerance \(\tau\geq0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed tests certify small curvature along \(d\), while only the operator-residual test certifies a spectral value within \(\tau\) of zero.

children.title: Curvature-Sign Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision regimes where negative and near-zero curvature are difficult to distinguish.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Sign Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision ambiguity in classifying a Krylov direction by its directional curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), let \(\delta\geq0\), and suppose \(\lvert\widehat q-v^{\mathsf T}Hv\rvert\leq\delta\lVert v\rVert_2^2\). The certified interval for the true curvature is \(I=[\widehat q-\delta\lVert v\rVert_2^2,\widehat q+\delta\lVert v\rVert_2^2]\). If \(\lvert\widehat q\rvert\leq\delta\lVert v\rVert_2^2\), then \(0\in I\), so the available bound certifies neither \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv<0\) nor \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv>0\). A strict curvature sign therefore requires a sharper error bound or an independent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the certified curvature interval contains zero, the direction cannot be certified as having strictly negative or strictly positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert\widehat q\rvert\leq\delta\lVert v\rVert_2^2\Longrightarrow 0\in I\), so neither strict curvature sign is certified

notation.meaning: symmetric curvature operator or Hessian approximation
certified interval containing the true directional curvature

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval-error logic for an inexact quadratic form

children.title: Finite-Precision Krylov Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Residual gaps and basis degradation that weaken nominal inner certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Krylov Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-gap and loss-of-orthogonality boundary for nominal Krylov stopping certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), let the recursively updated residual be \(\widehat r_k\), the true residual be \(r_k=b-A\widehat x_k\), and the residual gap be \(g_k=r_k-\widehat r_k\). A stopping test \(\lVert\widehat r_k\rVert_2\leq\tau\) certifies \(\lVert r_k\rVert_2\leq\tau+\eta_k\) only when an independently justified bound \(\lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq\eta_k\) is available. If \(\eta_k\) is comparable to the requested tolerance, or if loss of Krylov-basis orthogonality prevents further reduction of \(\widehat r_k\), nominal residual convergence may stagnate and the recursive residual alone is not a reliable inner certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small recursive Krylov residual is trustworthy only after accounting for its gap from the true residual and for basis degradation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widehat r_k\rVert_2\leq\tau\ \wedge\ \lVert g_k\rVert_2\leq\eta_k\Longrightarrow\lVert r_k\rVert_2\leq\tau+\eta_k\)

notation.meaning: true residual evaluated from the iterate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual-gap triangle inequality and finite-precision Krylov stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-gap bound follows from the triangle inequality, but the assertions connecting loss of basis orthogonality to stagnation and certificate failure require a finite-precision Krylov source with a specific locator.

children.title: Preconditioner Sources
children.top_down_role: Sources of approximate inverse information when the exact Newton matrix remains implicit.

children.title: Assembled Surrogate Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Simplified sparse matrices assembled specifically for inner acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Assembled Surrogate Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse assembled approximations used to precondition a matrix-free curvature operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be available through products but not necessarily assembled. An assembled surrogate preconditioner is an explicitly stored sparse nonsingular matrix \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) constructed from an approximation \(\widetilde H\) to \(H\), such that applications of \(M^{-1}\) are substantially cheaper than solving with \(H\). For symmetric positive-definite Krylov methods, \(M\) must be symmetric positive definite. Its quality is measured by clustering or bounding the spectrum of \(M^{-1}H\), while its cost includes assembly, storage, factorization or setup, and repeated triangular or approximate solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assembled surrogate preconditioner is a sparse stored approximation whose inverse is cheap to apply and improves the spectrum seen by Krylov iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is explicitly assembled, sparse, and nonsingular
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{-1}H\) is the left-preconditioned operator, with \(M=M^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) required for standard preconditioned conjugate gradients

notation.meaning: assembled approximation to the curvature operator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the preconditioner-source container and is mathematically conventional, but no cited source supports the matrix-free surrogate construction, SPD restriction, or spectral-quality characterization.

children.title: Physics-Based Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Approximations derived from governing equations, discretizations, or scale separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Physics-Based Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioners derived by simplifying the governing model while retaining its dominant scales and couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(H\) is the linearized or second-order operator induced by a discretized governing model. A physics-based preconditioner is an invertible operator \(M\) obtained by analytically simplifying that model—such as omitting weak couplings, freezing coefficients, separating scales, or approximating a constitutive block—rather than approximating \(H\) solely from algebraic entries. The simplification must retain the dominant modes responsible for poor conditioning, and \(M^{-1}v\) must be computable at acceptable cost. When constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) independent of discretization size satisfy \(c\,v^{\mathsf T}Mv\leq v^{\mathsf T}Hv\leq C\,v^{\mathsf T}Mv\), the preconditioned condition number is bounded by \(C/c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A physics-based preconditioner cheaply solves a simplified governing model that preserves the difficult scales or couplings of the original operator.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) is induced by a discretized physical model
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(cM\preceq H\preceq CM\Longrightarrow\kappa(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})\leq C/c\)

notation.meaning: discretized curvature or linearized physics operator

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral equivalence characterization of physics-based preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and conditional spectral-equivalence bound are coherent and fit the container, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the physics-based characterization or its mesh-independent interpretation.

children.title: Curvature-Correction Preconditioner Family
children.top_down_role: Curvature-history and low-rank corrections used to accelerate inner solves.

children.title: Secant Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners derived from stored curvature-history pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature preconditioners updated using displacement and gradient-difference interpolation conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable at \(x_i\) and \(x_{i+1}\), and define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\). A secant preconditioner is a nonsingular approximate Hessian \(B_k\), or an inverse approximation \(P_k=B_k^{-1}\), constructed so that a selected secant condition \(B_ks_i=y_i\), equivalently \(P_ky_i=s_i\), holds. Enforcing several pairs simultaneously is a multisecant construction and requires compatible interpolation conditions. If \(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite and satisfies a nonzero secant pair, then necessarily \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\); particular updates such as positive-definite BFGS updates preserve symmetry and positive definiteness under their stated curvature and initialization conditions. Krylov acceleration applies \(P_k\), possibly through a limited-memory representation, without assembling the true Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secant preconditioner uses a step and gradient-difference pair to build a cheaply applicable curvature approximation; multiple simultaneous pairs require a compatible multisecant construction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at the sampled iterates
\(B_k\) is nonsingular and \(P_k=B_k^{-1}\) when both forms are used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_ks_i=y_i\Longleftrightarrow P_ky_i=s_i\) when \(P_k=B_k^{-1}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quasi-Newton secant equation and curvature condition

children.title: Low-Rank Correction Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Base preconditioners modified by compact low-rank spectral corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Correction Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A baseline preconditioner augmented by a small-rank curvature correction with an explicit inverse formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), and define \(M=M_0+UV^{\mathsf T}\). If \(I_r+V^{\mathsf T}M_0^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then \(M\) is nonsingular and its inverse action is represented by \[M^{-1}=M_0^{-1}-M_0^{-1}U\bigl(I_r+V^{\mathsf T}M_0^{-1}U\bigr)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}M_0^{-1}.\] Thus applying the corrected preconditioner requires baseline inverse actions, products with the correction factors, and solution of an \(r\)-dimensional dense system. Symmetric corrections take \(V=U C\) with a symmetric small matrix \(C\), subject to definiteness requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-limited correction modifies a baseline preconditioner while retaining cheap inverse application through a small dense auxiliary solve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is the correctly conditioned Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury formula and fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source is cited for the representation or preconditioning interpretation.

children.title: Correction-Rank Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Memory, application cost, and spectral benefit across correction ranks.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction-Rank Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and application costs versus spectral benefit for rank-corrected preconditioners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=M_0+UV^{\mathsf T}\) with \(U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), assume actions of \(M_0^{-1}\) cost \(T_0\) and the reduced inverse \(S^{-1}=(I_r+V^{\mathsf T}M_0^{-1}U)^{-1}\) is stored after setup. One application of \(M^{-1}\) costs \(T_0+O(nr+r^2)\) arithmetic and requires \(O(nr+r^2)\) additional storage. Increasing \(r\) can represent more curvature directions and may reduce Krylov iterations, but it increases setup, storage, and per-application cost. Hence rank selection should minimize total work, not the iteration count alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher correction rank can improve spectral approximation, but costs linear-in-rank vector work, quadratic small-system work, and greater storage each application.
assumptions_latex: \(S^{-1}\) and required baseline-transformed factors are precomputed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{M^{-1}}=T_0+O(nr+r^2)\), with additional storage \(O(nr+r^2)\)

notation.meaning: cost of one baseline inverse action

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operation count from the low-rank inverse representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The application and storage counts are plausible under the stated precomputation assumptions, but an authoritative locator is needed to support the complexity model and distinguish application costs from setup costs.

children.title: Hierarchical-Partition Preconditioner Family
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy- and partition-based approximations for discretized systems.

children.title: Multilevel Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy-based approximations transferring correction information across resolution levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive coarse-level correction combined with fine-level smoothing for curvature systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the levels be indexed by \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\), with spaces \(V_\ell\), operators \(A_\ell:V_\ell\to V_\ell\), restrictions \(R_\ell:V_\ell\to V_{\ell-1}\), prolongations \(P_\ell:V_{\ell-1}\to V_\ell\), and prescribed smoothers on every noncoarse level. Define \(z=\mathcal M_\ell^{-1}r\) recursively. At \(\ell=0\), solve \(A_0z=r\). For \(\ell>0\), initialize \(z=0\), apply the prescribed pre-smoothing steps to \(A_\ell z=r\), form \(r_c=R_\ell(r-A_\ell z)\), compute \(e_c=\mathcal M_{\ell-1}^{-1}r_c\), update \(z\leftarrow z+P_\ell e_c\), and apply the prescribed post-smoothing steps. The output \(z\) is the multilevel preconditioner action. Use with a symmetric positive-definite Krylov method additionally requires compatible transfers and a symmetric positive-definite cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilevel preconditioner alternates smoothing with recursively computed coarse-level corrections and returns the resulting approximate solve.
assumptions_latex: \(R_\ell:V_\ell\to V_{\ell-1}\) and \(P_\ell:V_{\ell-1}\to V_\ell\) are defined for \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\)
\(A_0\) is solved exactly or to the accuracy prescribed by the cycle
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z=\mathcal M_L^{-1}r\) is the multilevel approximate solve used as the preconditioner action

children.title: Domain-Decomposition Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Spatially partitioned approximations assembled from local subproblem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Decomposition Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global inverse approximation assembled from local subdomain solves, optionally with a coarse correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and let \(R_i\) restrict global vectors to possibly overlapping subdomains. With local matrices \(A_i=R_iAR_i^{\mathsf T}\) nonsingular, an additive domain-decomposition preconditioner has the form \[M^{-1}=R_0^{\mathsf T}A_0^{-1}R_0+\sum_{i=1}^{N}R_i^{\mathsf T}A_i^{-1}R_i,\] where the first term is an optional coarse correction. Each local solve acts on a subdomain residual and is prolonged globally. For symmetric positive-definite \(A\), symmetric transfers and positive-definite local and coarse solvers make \(M^{-1}\) suitable for preconditioned conjugate gradients; scalable bounds additionally require stable decomposition and controlled overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive domain-decomposition preconditioner sums prolonged local subdomain solves and, when needed for scalability, a global coarse correction.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i=R_iAR_i^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) for each local or coarse space

notation.meaning: restriction to subdomain or coarse degrees of freedom

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive Schwarz representation fits the domain-decomposition container, but the optional coarse term, SPD suitability, and scalability conditions have no cited authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Block-Decomposition Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Algebraic partitioning strategies based on variable or operator blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Decomposition Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block diagonal and block triangular inverse approximations for partitioned curvature systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partitioned operator \(A=\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{pmatrix}\) with \(A_{11}\) nonsingular, define the Schur complement \(S=A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}\). A block-diagonal preconditioner is \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde A_{11},\widetilde S)\); a block-triangular alternative is \(M_T=\begin{pmatrix}\widetilde A_{11}&A_{12}\\0&\widetilde S\end{pmatrix}\), where the tilded blocks are cheaply invertible approximations. Applying either preconditioner reduces the global operation to approximate block solves. Effectiveness requires the approximations to capture both within-block stiffness and coupling represented by the Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block preconditioners replace a coupled system by inexpensive approximate solves for principal blocks and, when appropriate, its Schur complement.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is conformably partitioned into two variable blocks
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde A_{11},\widetilde S)\) or \(M_T=\begin{pmatrix}\widetilde A_{11}&A_{12}\\0&\widetilde S\end{pmatrix}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block factorization and Schur-complement preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-diagonal and upper block-triangular representations are coherent and appropriately use a Schur-complement approximation, but no inspectable block-preconditioning source is supplied.

children.title: Hierarchy-Partition Coupling
children.top_down_role: Combined use of resolution hierarchies and decomposed subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy-Partition Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions for combining hierarchical coarse spaces with partition-based local solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be the global discrete space, \(V_0\) a coarse hierarchical space, and \(V_i\) local partition spaces with injections \(I_i:V_i\to V\). A hierarchy-partition coupling is stable when every \(v\in V\) admits \(v=I_0v_0+\sum_{i=1}^{N}I_iv_i\) with \[a_0(v_0,v_0)+\sum_{i=1}^{N}a_i(v_i,v_i)\leq C_s\,a(v,v),\] and the assembled components satisfy a strengthened Cauchy-Schwarz bound with constant \(C_o\). If \(C_s\) and \(C_o\) are uniform in mesh size and partition count, the resulting additive hierarchical-partition preconditioner has a uniform spectral condition bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coarse and partition spaces couple robustly when they provide a uniformly stable decomposition with uniformly controlled interaction among injected components.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) and each \(a_i\) are symmetric positive-definite bilinear forms
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_s,C_o=O(1)\Longrightarrow\kappa(M^{-1}A)=O(C_sC_o)\)

notation.meaning: coarse space and local partition spaces

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract additive Schwarz stable-decomposition criterion

A specific theorem and locator are required.

children.title: Left Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Left Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioner placement obtained by applying an approximate inverse to the original equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular linear system \(Ax=b\) and nonsingular preconditioner \(M\), left preconditioning replaces the system by \[M^{-1}Ax=M^{-1}b.\] The iterate variable remains \(x\), while a Krylov method constructs residuals for the transformed operator \(M^{-1}A\). If \(r_k=b-Ax_k\) is the true residual, the transformed residual is \(z_k=M^{-1}r_k\). Therefore a stopping test based on \(\lVert z_k\rVert\) measures the preconditioned residual and does not directly bound \(\lVert r_k\rVert\) unless norm-equivalence bounds for \(M^{-1}\) are supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Left preconditioning applies the approximate inverse to both sides; Krylov iterations then monitor a transformed residual rather than the original residual directly.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard algebraic definition of left preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic representation and distinction between original and left-preconditioned residuals are correct and fit the placement taxonomy, but the record contains no authoritative Krylov-preconditioning citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Difference Preconditioned CG Inner Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computes an approximate Newton direction at a fixed point, with residual forcing, iteration-limit termination, and curvature-failure signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given x, M, \eta, k_{\max}, and a Hessian-vector approximation D_h^2f(x:p), initialize r=-\nabla f(x), \rho_0=r^Tr, d=0, and k=1. While \sqrt{\rho_{k-1}}>\eta\|\nabla f(x)\|_2 and k<k_{\max}, set z=Mr and \tau_{k-1}=z^Tr; take p=z when k=1 and otherwise p=z+(\tau_{k-1}/\tau_{k-2})p. Compute w=D_h^2f(x:p). If p^Tw=0, signal indefiniteness and stop; if p^Tw<0, signal negative curvature and stop. Otherwise set \alpha=\tau_{k-1}/(p^Tw), update d\leftarrow d+\alpha p, r\leftarrow r-\alpha w, \rho_k=r^Tr, and k\leftarrow k+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the negative gradient, apply the preconditioner to each residual and perform conjugate-gradient updates using finite-difference Hessian-vector products. Stop normally when the residual meets the forcing tolerance or the iteration limit is reached; stop with a signal when zero or negative curvature is encountered.
assumptions_latex: D_h^2f(x:p)\text{ is defined for each generated direction }p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns an accumulated direction }d\text{ on normal termination, or signals indefiniteness when }p^Tw=0\text{ and negative curvature when }p^Tw<0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterative refinement with a regularized inverse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal-point specialization for solvable symmetric positive-semidefinite linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{S}_+^n, let b\in\operatorname{range}(A), and choose \epsilon>0. For f(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx and \lambda=1/\epsilon, the proximal point step is x^{k+1}=(A+\epsilon I)^{-1}(b+\epsilon x^k)=x^k+(A+\epsilon I)^{-1}(b-Ax^k). Since A+\epsilon I\succ0, its inverse exists, and for every starting point the iteration converges asymptotically to a solution of Ax=b for every \epsilon>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a solvable symmetric positive-semidefinite system, iterative refinement adds the residual correction obtained from the shifted inverse of A. The shifted matrix is positive definite, and the iteration converges to a solution for any positive regularization parameter, even when A is singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=x^k+(A+\epsilon I)^{-1}(b-Ax^k)\longrightarrow x^\star\quad\text{with}\quad Ax^\star=b.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned Truncated Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A trust-region CG procedure with negative-curvature and boundary truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize
\[
r=-\nabla f(x),\quad \rho_0=\|r\|_2^2,\quad k=1,\quad d=0.
\]
While \(\sqrt{\rho_{k-1}}>\eta\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\) and \(k<k_{\max}\), set \(z=Mr\), \(\tau_{k-1}=z^Tr\), and
\[
p=\begin{cases}z,&k=1,\\ z+(\tau_{k-1}/\tau_{k-2})p,&k>1.\end{cases}
\]
Set \(w=\nabla^2f(x)p\). If \(p^Tw\le0\), choose \(\tau\) with \(\|d+\tau p\|_C=\Delta\), return \(d+\tau p\). Otherwise set \(\alpha=\tau_{k-1}/(p^Tw)\), update \(r\leftarrow r-\alpha w\), \(\rho_k=r^Tr\), and \(\widehat d=d+\alpha p\). If \(\|\widehat d\|_C>\Delta\), choose \(\tau\) with \(\|d+\tau p\|_C=\Delta\) and return \(d+\tau p\); otherwise set \(d\leftarrow\widehat d\), \(k\leftarrow k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the negative gradient and zero step, precondition the residual and perform conjugate-gradient updates using Hessian-vector products. Truncate and return a boundary step upon nonpositive curvature or when the next step leaves the trust region; otherwise stop when the relative residual test or iteration cap is reached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^T\nabla^2f(x)p\le0\ \text{or}\ \|d+\alpha p\|_C>\Delta\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{return }d+\tau p\text{ with }\|d+\tau p\|_C=\Delta;\text{ otherwise terminate by the residual test or iteration cap.}

assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, and applications of \(M^{-1}\) are available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Right preconditioning represents the system \(Ax=b\) by \[(AM^{-1})y=b,\qquad x=M^{-1}y.\] Given \(x_0=M^{-1}y_0\) and \(r_0=b-Ax_0\), a Krylov approximation satisfies \[y_k\in y_0+\mathcal{K}_k(AM^{-1},r_0),\qquad x_k=M^{-1}y_k.\] The residual generated by the transformed equation is exactly the physical residual: \[b-(AM^{-1})y_k=b-Ax_k.\] Thus right preconditioning changes the correction space while leaving the residual vector and its norm in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right preconditioning solves for a transformed variable, maps it back through the inverse preconditioner, and preserves the original system's residual vector.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CGLS Recurrence from the Zero Initial Vector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unpreconditioned conjugate gradient for linear least squares, implemented without explicitly forming the normal-equation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^{(0)}=0\), \(r^{(0)}=b-Ax^{(0)}\), and \(d^{(0)}=A^Tr^{(0)}\). For \(k=1,2,\ldots\), provided the displayed denominators are nonzero, set
\[
\bar\alpha_k=\frac{\|A^Tr^{(k-1)}\|_2^2}{\|Ad^{(k-1)}\|_2^2},\qquad
x^{(k)}=x^{(k-1)}+\bar\alpha_kd^{(k-1)},
\]
\[
r^{(k)}=r^{(k-1)}-\bar\alpha_kAd^{(k-1)},\qquad
\bar\beta_k=\frac{\|A^Tr^{(k)}\|_2^2}{\|A^Tr^{(k-1)}\|_2^2},
\]
\[
d^{(k)}=A^Tr^{(k)}+\bar\beta_kd^{(k-1)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CGLS starts at zero with the data residual and normal residual, then updates the iterate, residual, conjugacy coefficient, and search direction using matrix-vector products with A and A transpose. Each step requires the indicated denominators to be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x^{(k)},r^{(k)},d^{(k)}\}_{k\ge 0}\ \text{is generated by the stated CGLS recurrences}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov residual minimization and residual-polynomial orthogonality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and spectral orthogonality properties of Algorithm 8.14.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(y\in\mathcal Y\), the \(k\)-th iterate of Algorithm 8.14 minimizes \(\|y-Tx\|\) over \(x_0^\dagger+L_T^\dagger\!\left(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B)\right)\). Its residual polynomials \(\{r_k\}\) are mutually orthogonal for \([\varphi,\psi]:=\int_0^{\|B\|^{2}+}\varphi(\lambda)\psi(\lambda)\,\lambda\,d\|H_\lambda y\|^2\), where \(\{H_\lambda\}\) is the spectral family of \(BB^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every data vector y, the kth iterate is the minimum-residual point in the corresponding augmented Krylov subspace. The associated residual polynomials are orthogonal under the spectral Stieltjes inner product induced by BB* and y.
assumptions_latex: x_k\text{ is the }k\text{-th iterate of Algorithm 8.14}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in\operator*{arg\,min}_{x\in x_0^\dagger+L_T^\dagger(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B))}\|y-Tx\|,\qquad [r_i,r_j]=0\ \text{for }i\ne j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recurrence and Krylov-subspace characterization of Algorithm 8.14.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0=x_0^\dagger\), \(d_0=y-Tx_0\), \(s_0=(L_T^\dagger)^*T^*d_0\), and \(p_1=L_T^\dagger s_0\). For \(k=1,2,\ldots\), while \(s_{k-1}\ne0\), set \(q_k=Tp_k\), \(\alpha_k=\|s_{k-1}\|^2/\|q_k\|^2\), \(x_k=x_{k-1}+\alpha_kp_k\), \(d_k=d_{k-1}-\alpha_kq_k\), \(s_k=(L_T^\dagger)^*T^*d_k\), \(\beta_k=\|s_k\|^2/\|s_{k-1}\|^2\), and \(p_{k+1}=L_T^\dagger s_k+\beta_kp_k\). The generated directions satisfy \(p_k\in L_T^\dagger\!\left(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B)\right)\), and \(x_k\in x_0^\dagger+L_T^\dagger\!\left(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B)\right)\), with the corresponding polynomial representation having degree \(k-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the prescribed initial point and residual, then apply the stated CGNE recurrences until the transformed residual vanishes. Each search direction is the image under the generalized inverse of the associated Krylov subspace, and each iterate has the corresponding degree-(k−1) polynomial Krylov representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k\in L_T^\dagger\!\left(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B)\right),\qquad x_k\in x_0^\dagger+L_T^\dagger\!\left(\mathcal K_k(B^*y,B^*B)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence–divergence dichotomy for residual-polynomial Krylov approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of semiiterative approximations according to membership of the datum in the pseudoinverse domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $x_k^\delta=g_k(T^*T)T^*y^\delta$ and $r_k(\lambda)=1-\lambda g_k(\lambda)$. If $\{r_k\}$ is uniformly bounded on $[0,\|T\|^2]$ and $r_k(\lambda)\to0$ for every $\lambda\in(0,\|T\|^2]$, then, as $k\to\infty$, $x_k^\delta\to T^\dagger y^\delta$ when $y^\delta\in\mathcal D(T^\dagger)$, whereas $\|x_k^\delta\|\to\infty$ when $y^\delta\notin\mathcal D(T^\dagger)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded residual polynomials that vanish pointwise away from zero yield convergence to the pseudoinverse solution for data in the pseudoinverse domain and norm divergence for data outside that domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y^\delta\in\mathcal D(T^\dagger)\Rightarrow x_k^\delta\to T^\dagger y^\delta,\qquad y^\delta\notin\mathcal D(T^\dagger)\Rightarrow\|x_k^\delta\|\to\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov subspace and polynomial bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-operator Krylov spaces and conditions ensuring polynomially generated bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear operator $A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$, $x\in\mathcal X$, and $k\geq1$, define $\mathcal K_k(x,A)=\operatorname{span}\{x,Ax,\ldots,A^{k-1}x\}$. Every $z\in\mathcal K_k(x,A)$ has the form $z=g(A)x$ for a polynomial $g$ of degree at most $k-1$. If $A$ is self-adjoint and $x$ cannot be expressed as a sum of $k-1$ eigenvectors of $A$, then $\{x,Ax,\ldots,A^{k-1}x\}$ is a basis of $\mathcal K_k(x,A)$. Under the same hypothesis, $\{g_j(A)x:j=1,\ldots,k\}$ is also a basis whenever $\deg g_j=j-1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The kth Krylov subspace is spanned by the first k operator powers applied to x, so each of its elements is a polynomial in A applied to x. For self-adjoint A, if x is not a sum of k−1 eigenvectors, the monomial vectors form a basis; so does any polynomial sequence having respective exact degrees 0 through k−1.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the basis claims, }A=A^*\text{ and }x\text{ is not a sum of }k-1\text{ eigenvectors of }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal K_k(x,A)=\{g(A)x:\deg g\leq k-1\},\quad \{g_j(A)x\}_{j=1}^k\text{ is a basis if }\deg g_j=j-1.

children.top_down_role: Two-sided placement distributing transformations across the operator.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=M_R^{-1}y\) solves \(Ax=b\) exactly when \(y\) solves \(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}y=M_L^{-1}b\).

source_refs.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Split preconditioning replaces \(Ax=b\) by \[M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}y=M_L^{-1}b,\qquad x=M_R^{-1}y.\] For an approximate transformed solution \(y_k\), define \(x_k=M_R^{-1}y_k\) and the physical residual \(r_k=b-Ax_k\). The transformed residual is then \[\widetilde r_k=M_L^{-1}b-M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}y_k=M_L^{-1}r_k.\] If a single preconditioner factors as \(M=M_LM_R\), this placement distributes its action across the operator's two sides; symmetry requires additional compatibility between the factors and \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split preconditioning applies one invertible factor to equations and another to unknowns; its computed residual is the left-transformed physical residual.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde r_k=r_k\) for right placement, \(\widetilde r_k=M^{-1}r_k\) for left placement, and \(\widetilde r_k=M_L^{-1}r_k\) for split placement.

source_refs.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k=b-Ax_k\) denote the physical residual. For left preconditioning, the residual of \(M^{-1}Ax=M^{-1}b\) is \(\widetilde r_k=M^{-1}r_k\). For right preconditioning, with \(x_k=M^{-1}y_k\), the residual of \(AM^{-1}y=b\) is \(\widetilde r_k=r_k\). For split preconditioning, with \(x_k=M_R^{-1}y_k\), the residual of \(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}y=M_L^{-1}b\) is \(\widetilde r_k=M_L^{-1}r_k\). Consequently, stopping on \(\|\widetilde r_k\|_2\) controls the physical norm directly only for right placement unless norm-equivalence constants are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right placement preserves the physical residual; left and split placements expose a transformed residual, so stopping tolerances require norm conversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence preconditioning for symmetric positive-definite systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(M=CC^{\mathsf T}\) be symmetric positive definite with nonsingular \(C\). Symmetric preconditioning represents \(Ax=b\) as \[C^{-1}AC^{-\mathsf T}z=C^{-1}b,\qquad x=C^{-\mathsf T}z.\] The transformed matrix \(C^{-1}AC^{-\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite, so Krylov methods requiring a symmetric positive-definite operator remain structurally applicable to the transformed system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring a positive-definite preconditioner on both sides gives an equivalent symmetric positive-definite system suitable for symmetric Krylov methods.
assumptions_latex: \(M=CC^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite with nonsingular \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^{-1}AC^{-\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite, and \(x=C^{-\mathsf T}z\) gives an equivalent representation of \(Ax=b\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive definiteness condition for a damped Jacobi splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded statement; the inclusion of the upper endpoint should be independently verified because equality ordinarily corresponds to a singular boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a real symmetric matrix with \(a_{ii}>0\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(A)\), and let \(\omega>0\). If \(\mu_{\min}\le 0\) is the minimum eigenvalue of \(I-D^{-1}A\), then \(2\omega^{-1}D-A\) is positive definite if and only if \(0<\omega\le \frac{2}{1-\mu_{\min}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a real symmetric matrix with positive diagonal, the diagonal-splitting matrix 2D/omega minus A is positive definite exactly when the positive relaxation parameter omega does not exceed 2 divided by 1 minus the minimum eigenvalue of I minus D inverse A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 2\omega^{-1}D-A\succ0\iff 0<\omega\le\frac{2}{1-\mu_{\min}}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(\beta=\|r_0\|_2\) and \(v_1=r_0/\beta\). For \(j=1,\ldots,k\), compute \(z_j=B_j(v_j)\), form \(w=Az_j\), and orthogonalize \(w\) against \(v_1,\ldots,v_j\) to obtain the next Arnoldi vector. With \(Z_k=[z_1,\ldots,z_k]\), this gives \[AZ_k=V_{k+1}\overline H_k.\] Choose \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^k}\|\beta e_1-\overline H_ky\|_2,\qquad x_k=x_0+Z_ky_k.\] Stop when the physical residual meets the prescribed tolerance, and output \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flexible GMRES stores each iteration's preconditioned vector, builds an Arnoldi relation for those vectors, and minimizes the physical residual over their span.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable preconditioner action at iteration \(j\) is a map \(B_j\) applied to the current basis vector, producing \[z_j=B_j(v_j).\] The maps may differ between iterations and may represent varying inner tolerances, changing factorizations, or nonlinear approximate solves. After \(k\) actions, the correction space is \[\mathcal{S}_k=\operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\operatorname{span}\{z_1,\ldots,z_k\},\qquad Z_k=[z_1,\ldots,z_k].\] Unless all \(B_j\) coincide with one fixed linear operator, \(\mathcal{S}_k\) need not be a standard Krylov subspace of a single preconditioned matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable preconditioner produces a separately stored correction from each basis vector; their span generally is not one fixed-operator Krylov space.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner-Variation Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic compatibility required for variable right-preconditioner actions in flexible Arnoldi methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_0=b-Ax_0\ne0\), \(\beta=\lVert r_0\rVert_2\), and \(v_1=r_0/\beta\). Let \(V_{k+1}=[v_1,\ldots,v_{k+1}]\) have orthonormal columns, let \(z_j=B_j(v_j)\), and set \(Z_k=[z_1,\ldots,z_k]\). Variable preconditioner actions are algebraically compatible through iteration \(k\) when the generated vectors are retained and satisfy \[AZ_k=V_{k+1}\overline H_k,\qquad x_k=x_0+Z_ky_k.\] Under these conditions, the physical residual is represented by \[b-Ax_k=V_{k+1}(\beta e_1-\overline H_ky_k).\] Reconstructing every stored correction with a single current map \(B_k\) preserves this relation only if \(B_k(v_j)=B_j(v_j)\) for every retained \(v_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable preconditioning is compatible when every generated correction is retained and the Arnoldi relation, iterate reconstruction, and residual representation all use those same corrections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(x_k=x_0+Z_ky_k\), \(b-Ax_k=V_{k+1}(\beta e_1-\overline H_ky_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=U^{\mathsf T}AU\), \(Q=UE^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}\), and \(P=I-AQ\). Spectral deflation solves the singular consistent system \[PA\widehat x=Pb\] and reconstructs \[x=Qb+P^{\mathsf T}\widehat x.\] Indeed, its physical residual satisfies \[b-Ax=P(b-A\widehat x).\] If \(U\) spans eigenvectors of \(A\), the corresponding eigenvalues are replaced by zeros in \(PA\); their solution components are supplied exactly by \(Qb\), while a Krylov method acts on the complementary nonzero spectrum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deflation removes selected spectral directions from the projected operator, solves on the complement, and restores their exact coarse components during reconstruction.
