knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an augmentation basis \(U\), define the trial space \[\mathcal{S}_k=\operatorname{range}(U)+\mathcal{K}_k(A,r_0).\] An augmented Krylov iterate has \(x_k=x_0+s_k\) with \(s_k\in\mathcal{S}_k\). In the symmetric positive-definite Galerkin form it is characterized by \[v^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax_k)=0\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal{S}_k.\] Equivalently, \(x_k\) minimizes the quadratic energy over \(x_0+\mathcal{S}_k\). When \(U\) approximates an invariant subspace associated with troublesome eigenvalues, those directions are available from the first augmented iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral augmentation adds selected directions directly to every Krylov trial space and imposes the usual projection condition on the enlarged space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(A\), common basis \(U\), exact \(E^{-1}\), and matching Galerkin conditions, a deflated auxiliary vector \(\widehat x\) reconstructs the augmented physical vector by \[x=UE^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}b+(I-UE^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}A)\widehat x,\] with residual \[b-Ax=(I-AUE^{-1}U^{\mathsf T})(b-A\widehat x).\] This establishes equivalence only after physical reconstruction and compatible initialization. It can fail as an iterate-by-iterate identity when coarse solves are inexact, projectors or test spaces differ, or the preconditioner varies. If \(E\) is singular, the displayed correspondence is undefined without a pseudoinverse and additional consistency conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deflation and augmentation correspond under a shared subspace, exact coarse solve, compatible initialization, and matching projection; changing these ingredients breaks iterate-level equivalence.

children.title: Stale Spectral Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Degradation when retained directions no longer represent the current operator.

assumptions_latex: The retained one-dimensional subspace was computed for an earlier symmetric positive-definite matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A previously exact spectral subspace can leave the new projected condition number equal to \(L/\varepsilon\), although the updated subspace yields \(L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal counterexample showing loss of spectral relevance across systems.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.5.4. The spectral decomposition of a symmetric matrix p. 40
5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[A_{\mathrm{old}}=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,1,L),\qquad A_{\mathrm{new}}=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon,L).\] The old smallest-eigenvalue subspace is \(U_{\mathrm{stale}}=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}\). Deflating it from \(A_{\mathrm{new}}\) leaves nonzero eigenvalues \(\{\varepsilon,L\}\), whose condition number is \(L/\varepsilon\). The updated choice \(U_{\mathrm{fresh}}=\operatorname{span}\{e_2\}\) leaves \(\{1,L\}\), whose condition number is \(L\). Thus exact spectral information for an earlier system provides no uniform acceleration guarantee after the troublesome eigenspace moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace exactly targeting the old smallest eigenvalue may target an ordinary new eigenvalue, leaving the new ill-conditioning completely untreated.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Spectral Subspaces

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.5.4. The spectral decomposition of a symmetric matrix p. 40

children.title: Primal–Dual Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of approximate primal, dual, and reduced-space solutions in constrained sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational warm start for a sequence of nearby equality-constrained KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For problem \(k\), let \(F_k:\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\to\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be its KKT residual map, let \(\widehat z_{k-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be the preceding approximate primal–dual solution, and optionally let \(U_{k-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+p)\times r}\) be a recycled correction basis. If a basis is retained, choose \(y_k\in\mathbb{R}^r\) to approximately solve \[\min_{y\in\mathbb{R}^r}\left\|F_k\!\left(\widehat z_{k-1}+U_{k-1}y\right)\right\|.\] Otherwise set the correction to zero. Initialize the current matrix-free primal–dual solver at \[z_k^{(0)}=\widehat z_{k-1}+U_{k-1}y_k,\] interpreting \(U_{k-1}y_k=0\) when no basis is retained. Iterate using the current residual map \(F_k\) and return the first iterate satisfying the prescribed primal- and dual-feasibility tolerances for problem \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the current equality-constrained KKT solve from the preceding approximate primal–dual solution, optionally after minimizing the current residual over a recycled correction subspace, and stop under the current problem's feasibility tolerances.
assumptions_latex: For each \(k\), the equality-constrained problem has a KKT residual map \(F_k:\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\to\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) for \(z=(x,\lambda)\).
An approximate solution \(\widehat z_{k-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is available; optionally, a basis \(U_{k-1}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+p)\times r}\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initial iterate is \(z_k^{(0)}=\widehat z_{k-1}+U_{k-1}y_k\), with \(y_k\in\mathbb{R}^r\) chosen to reduce the current KKT residual when a basis is retained; termination uses the current problem's primal- and dual-feasibility tolerances.

notation.meaning: KKT residual map for problem k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nearby equality-constrained KKT systems may be initialized from a preceding approximate primal-dual solution

children.title: Preconditioner Quality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cost and structural regimes in which a preconditioner ceases to improve the nested solve.

children.title: Preconditioning Amortization Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Construction expense and reuse horizon relative to per-application savings.

children.title: Preconditioner Setup Costs
children.top_down_role: Resource expense incurred when constructing or refreshing a preconditioner.

assumptions_latex: A preconditioner \(M\) is constructed once for a linear system or a designated block of systems.
The chosen cost model assigns nonnegative costs to arithmetic, storage movement, and operator evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The setup cost is \(C_{\mathrm{set}}(M)=C_{\mathrm{build}}(M)+C_{\mathrm{aux}}(M)\), incurred before Krylov applications and separated from per-application cost.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: iterative-solver cost models conventionally separate preconditioner construction from repeated application
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-accounting definition for constructing a reusable preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a preconditioner \(M\), define its setup cost by \[C_{\mathrm{set}}(M)=C_{\mathrm{build}}(M)+C_{\mathrm{aux}}(M),\] where \(C_{\mathrm{build}}(M)\) counts work required to form or configure the action of \(M^{-1}\), and \(C_{\mathrm{aux}}(M)\) counts auxiliary analysis, factorization metadata, communication planning, or storage preparation performed before the first application. Costs incurred while computing \(M^{-1}v\) during Krylov iterations are excluded. In a matrix-free method, forming a dense or sparse representation of the system operator is likewise excluded unless the preconditioner explicitly requires it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Setup cost counts one-time construction and auxiliary preparation of a preconditioner, excluding its repeated use during Krylov iterations.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Setup Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and accounting definition fit the setup-cost leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular decomposition or its matrix-free qualifications.

children.title: Preconditioner Reuse Horizon
children.top_down_role: Number and similarity of systems over which setup expense can be amortized.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Reuse Horizon
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consecutive-system horizon under an explicitly chosen preconditioner-quality test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a preconditioner \(M_s\) built for system \(A_sx=b_s\) and an acceptance predicate \(Q(k;M_s)\). Define its reuse horizon by \[H_s=\sup\left\{h\in\mathbb{N}_0:Q(k;M_s)\text{ holds for every }k=s,\ldots,s+h-1\right\}\in\mathbb{N}_0\cup\{\infty\},\] where the condition for \(h=0\) is vacuous. Thus \(H_s=0\) if \(Q(s;M_s)\) fails, and \(H_s=\infty\) if the predicate holds for every \(k\ge s\). The predicate must be fixed before the horizon is measured and may impose an iteration cap, residual-reduction requirement, or a spectral or field-of-values condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reuse horizon is the number of consecutive systems, possibly infinite, for which a fixed preconditioner satisfies a predetermined quality test; it is zero if the test fails on its build system.
assumptions_latex: Systems \(A_kx=b_k\) are solved sequentially for indices \(k\ge s\) using a preconditioner \(M_s\) built at index \(s\).
A fixed acceptance predicate \(Q(k;M_s)\) specifies adequate preconditioner quality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reuse horizon is \(H_s=\sup\{h\in\mathbb{N}_0:Q(k;M_s)\text{ holds for all }k=s,\ldots,s+h-1\}\in\mathbb{N}_0\cup\{\infty\}\).

notation.meaning: system operator at sequence index k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a reuse horizon is the maximal consecutive duration for which a fixed quality predicate holds

children.title: Preconditioner Application Costs
children.top_down_role: Per-iteration resources required for each preconditioner action.

assumptions_latex: A Krylov solve performs \(m\) evaluations of \(v\mapsto M^{-1}v\).
Each evaluation has cost \(C_{\mathrm{app}}(M)\) in the selected resource model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preconditioner-application contribution to the solve is \(mC_{\mathrm{app}}(M)\), apart from separately counted setup and synchronization costs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated calls to a fixed preconditioner contribute their count times the per-call cost in an additive resource model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive work bound for repeated applications of a fixed preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\mathrm{app}}(M)\) denote the cost of computing one vector \(z=M^{-1}v\), including all arithmetic and data movement assigned to that operation by the cost model. If a Krylov solve invokes this operation \(m\) times, then its preconditioner-application cost is \[C_{\mathrm{apply,total}}=mC_{\mathrm{app}}(M).\] Consequently, if \(C_{\mathrm{other}}\) counts matrix-vector products, orthogonalization, and stopping tests, the solve cost is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{other}}+mC_{\mathrm{app}}(M)\), excluding the separately accounted setup cost. For variable preconditioners \(M_j\), replace the product by \(\sum_{j=1}^{m}C_{\mathrm{app}}(M_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an additive cost model, m applications of a fixed preconditioner cost m times one application, separate from setup and other Krylov work.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Application Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity role fits the application-cost leaf and the additive formula is coherent, but no cited source supports the selected resource model or its stated exclusions and variable-preconditioner extension.

children.title: Amortized Preconditioning Cost
children.top_down_role: Overall cost balance across setup, refresh, reuse, and repeated application.

assumptions_latex: A preconditioner with setup cost \(C_{\mathrm{set}}\) is reused for \(H\geq1\) solves.
Solve \(k\) performs \(m_k\) preconditioner applications, each costing \(C_{\mathrm{app}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The average preconditioning cost per solve is \(C_{\mathrm{set}}/H+C_{\mathrm{app}}H^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{H}m_k\).

notation.meaning: number of solves sharing the setup

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: amortization divides one setup charge plus accumulated application charges by the number of solves sharing the setup
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-solve amortization over a fixed reuse horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one preconditioner setup of cost \(C_{\mathrm{set}}\) supports \(H\geq1\) solves, and solve \(k\) uses the preconditioner \(m_k\) times at cost \(C_{\mathrm{app}}\) per application. The total and average preconditioning costs are \[C_{\mathrm{total}}(H)=C_{\mathrm{set}}+C_{\mathrm{app}}\sum_{k=1}^{H}m_k,\qquad \overline C(H)=\frac{C_{\mathrm{set}}}{H}+\frac{C_{\mathrm{app}}}{H}\sum_{k=1}^{H}m_k.\] Reuse is cheaper than rebuilding before every solve precisely when its total cost, including any iteration-count increases caused by aging, is smaller than the corresponding sum of setup and application costs under rebuilding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average preconditioning cost equals setup cost divided by the reuse horizon plus the average number of applications times their unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Amortized Preconditioning Cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula and complexity kind fit the amortized-cost leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the accounting model or the rebuilding comparison.

children.title: Solver-Geometry Mismatch Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure to control the operator geometry decisive for the selected Krylov family.

children.title: Spectral Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure of the preconditioned spectrum to support the intended convergence behavior.

assumptions_latex: The preconditioned operator \(B=M^{-1}A\) is diagonalizable as \(B=V\Lambda V^{-1}\).
A convergence estimate is inferred only from the eigenvalue set \(\sigma(B)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eigenvalue clustering alone is insufficient unless eigenvector conditioning is controlled, because \(\|p(B)\|\leq\kappa(V)\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(B)}|p(\lambda)|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomial Krylov bounds for diagonalizable nonnormal matrices include the eigenvector condition number
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of eigenvalue-only convergence predictions for diagonalizable preconditioned operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a diagonalizable preconditioned operator \(B=V\Lambda V^{-1}\) and any polynomial \(p\), \[\|p(B)\|\leq\|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(B)}|p(\lambda)|.\] Hence an eigenvalue-based Krylov prediction that uses only clustering of \(\sigma(B)\) can be arbitrarily misleading when \(\kappa(V)=\|V\|\|V^{-1}\|\) is unbounded. Spectral compatibility therefore requires both an eigenvalue set suited to the solver's residual polynomials and sufficient control of the eigenvector geometry, or an alternative bound based on a geometry-sensitive set. Removing the eigenvector control invalidates any uniform convergence conclusion based solely on clustered eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clustered eigenvalues do not ensure fast Krylov convergence when the eigenvector basis is badly conditioned; a spectral assessment must include operator geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the diagonalizable-matrix inequality is standard, but a source is needed for the claimed Krylov-convergence interpretation and its required norm assumptions.

children.title: Field-of-Values Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure to control nonnormal operator geometry relevant to residual reduction.

assumptions_latex: Its Euclidean field of values is \(W(B)=\{x^*Bx:x^*x=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A field-of-values convergence guarantee requiring \(0\notin W(B)\) is unavailable when \(0\in W(B)\), even if \(B\) is nonsingular.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coercivity-type GMRES estimates depend on positive separation of the numerical range from zero
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coercivity-style Krylov bounds when the numerical range reaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(
u(B)=\min\{|z|:z\in W(B)\}\). Field-of-values residual bounds based on coercive separation require \(
u(B)>0\), equivalently \(0
otin W(B)\). If preconditioning produces \(0\in W(B)\), then \(
u(B)=0\), so every bound whose contraction factor is derived from \(
u(B)/\|B\|\) becomes vacuous. This can occur although \(B\) is nonsingular because the field of values may strictly contain its spectrum. Thus spectral nonsingularity does not repair a mismatch between the solver's field-of-values geometry and the preconditioned operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When zero enters the preconditioned operator's field of values, coercivity-based Krylov contraction bounds become vacuous despite nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Field-of-Values Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly identifies the boundary of coercivity-style field-of-values estimates, but no specific theorem or section is cited for the contraction bound being declared vacuous.

children.title: Nonnormality Blind Spots
children.top_down_role: Regimes where favorable eigenvalue information obscures adverse transient behavior.

assumptions_latex: Convergence is assessed using eigenvalues alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(\sigma(B_\varepsilon)=\{1\}\) for every \(\varepsilon\), \(\|B_\varepsilon\|\) and transient polynomial effects grow without bound as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a scaled Jordan block is the canonical concrete family showing that identical spectra do not control nonnormal operator behavior
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled Jordan-block counterexample to eigenvalue-only solver diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[B_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}1&\varepsilon^{-1}\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad 0<\varepsilon\leq1.\] Every member has the perfectly clustered spectrum \(\sigma(B_\varepsilon)=\{1\}\), but it is nonnormal and satisfies \(\|B_\varepsilon\|\geq\varepsilon^{-1}\). For every polynomial \(p\), the Jordan functional calculus gives \[p(B_\varepsilon)=\begin{pmatrix}p(1)&\varepsilon^{-1}p'(1)\\0&p(1)\end{pmatrix}.\] Therefore eigenvalue values \(p(1)\) alone do not control \(\|p(B_\varepsilon)\|\); the derivative term can be arbitrarily large as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Eigenvalue clustering is consequently blind to this nonnormal amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled Jordan blocks have the same single eigenvalue but arbitrarily strong nonnormal amplification, defeating convergence judgments based only on eigenvalue clustering.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnormality Blind Spots

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits the blind-spot leaf, and the scaled Jordan-block formula is internally consistent. A source is still required for its asserted solver-convergence interpretation.

children.title: Solver-Geometry Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Alignment between preconditioner effects and the geometry used by the selected Krylov family.

assumptions_latex: A Krylov method is selected with a convergence theory based on a geometric class \(\mathcal{G}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solver-geometry compatibility holds exactly when \(B\in\mathcal{G}\) and the constants defining that class remain within the method's admissible bounds.

notation.meaning: operator class required by the selected solver
geometry constants used in the convergence bound

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Krylov guarantees require the preconditioned operator to retain the algebraic and geometric hypotheses of the selected method
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract compatibility predicate covering solver-specific algebraic and geometric hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{G}\) be the class of operators for which the chosen Krylov method's stated convergence result applies, including required symmetry, definiteness, normality, field-of-values separation, or spectral-set conditions. The pair consisting of solver and preconditioner is geometry-compatible when \[B=M^{-1}A\in\mathcal{G}\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma(B)\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}},\] where \(\gamma(B)\) denotes every quantitative geometry constant appearing in the bound and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is its admissible range. Membership must be tested in the inner product actually used by the method. Compatibility fails if preconditioning changes that geometry so that any required predicate or bound is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver and preconditioner are compatible when the preconditioned operator satisfies every algebraic and geometric hypothesis, in the solver's actual inner product.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Geometry Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility leaf, but the abstract class and admissible constants are source-dependent and no solver-specific convergence result is cited.

children.title: Preconditioner Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Degradation under changing nonlinear states and loss of symmetry or definiteness.

children.title: Stale Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners degraded by movement across nonlinear states or parameter regimes.

assumptions_latex: A fixed preconditioner \(M_s\) built for \(A_s\) is reused on \(A_k=A_s+E_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preconditioner is stale at index \(k\) when a prescribed quality test fails; the perturbation identity \(M_s^{-1}A_k=M_s^{-1}A_s+M_s^{-1}E_k\) identifies the uncontrolled drift.

notation.meaning: preconditioner built at sequence index s
operator change from index s to k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reuse becomes stale when operator drift makes the fixed preconditioner violate a predetermined convergence-quality criterion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational staleness boundary for a preconditioner reused across changing systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_s\) be built for \(A_s\), and write \(A_k=A_s+E_k\). Then \[M_s^{-1}A_k=M_s^{-1}A_s+M_s^{-1}E_k.\] Relative to a predetermined acceptance predicate \(Q(k;M_s)\), the preconditioner is stale at the first index \(k>s\) for which \(Q(k;M_s)\) fails. A sufficient perturbative validity test may require \(\|M_s^{-1}E_k\|\leq\eta\) for a method-dependent threshold \(\eta\), but small unpreconditioned drift \(\|E_k\|\) alone is insufficient when \(\|M_s^{-1}\|\) is large. Staleness therefore concerns degradation of the preconditioned operator, not merely the age of \(M_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reused preconditioner becomes stale when operator drift makes the preconditioned system fail its fixed quality test; chronological age alone is not decisive.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Preconditioners

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and perturbation identity fit the staleness leaf, but no source supports the proposed method-dependent threshold or the operational refresh criterion.

children.title: Symmetry-Breaking Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioner actions that destroy symmetry required by the solver family.

assumptions_latex: The system matrix \(A\) is symmetric and the selected Krylov method requires self-adjointness in a specified inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B\) is not self-adjoint in the solver's inner product, the symmetric-method recurrence and its guarantees are not valid for that preconditioned system.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: short-recurrence symmetric Krylov methods require self-adjointness in the inner product used by the recurrence
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for symmetric Krylov recurrences under preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the Krylov recurrence use the inner product \(\langle u,v\rangle_H=u^*Hv\), where \(H\) is Hermitian positive definite. The effective preconditioned operator \(B\) preserves the required symmetry exactly when \[HB=B^*H.\] If this identity fails, then \(B\) is not self-adjoint in the recurrence geometry, even when the original matrix \(A\) is symmetric. Orthogonality, three-term recurrence, and convergence results derived from self-adjointness then cease to be justified. A nonsymmetric left preconditioner can cause this failure; a compatible symmetric or split construction must instead establish the displayed identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioner breaks symmetry when the effective operator is not self-adjoint in the Krylov method's inner product, invalidating symmetric short-recurrence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Breaking Preconditioners

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-adjointness condition is appropriate for this failure boundary, but the recurrence and convergence consequences require a citation tied to a specific symmetric Krylov method and preconditioning form.

children.title: Definiteness-Breaking Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioner actions that invalidate positive-definiteness assumptions.

assumptions_latex: The selected Krylov method requires a positive-definite effective operator in the inner product induced by \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Definiteness is broken when some nonzero \(x\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Re}(x^*HBx)\leq0\); positive-definite-method guarantees then do not apply.

notation.meaning: quadratic form in the solver geometry

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-definite Krylov theory requires positivity of the effective operator's quadratic form in the method's inner product
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-form boundary for positive-definite Krylov methods under preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\) define the solver's inner product and let \(B\) be the effective preconditioned operator. The required positive definiteness is \[\operatorname{Re}(x^*HBx)>0\quad\text{for every }x\neq0.\] A preconditioner is definiteness-breaking for that method if there exists \(x\neq0\) with \(\operatorname{Re}(x^*HBx)\leq0\). In this case, descent identities, energy-norm interpretations, and nonbreakdown results that depend on positivity are unavailable. Positivity of the original matrix \(A\) alone is insufficient: the chosen left, right, or split preconditioning must preserve positivity in the inner product actually used by the recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioner breaks definiteness when the effective operator has a nonpositive quadratic form in the solver's inner product, invalidating positive-definite-method guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Definiteness-Breaking Preconditioners

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic-form boundary fits the leaf, but the record needs a solver-specific source establishing which positivity notion and breakdown or convergence consequences apply under the stated preconditioning geometry.

children.title: Refresh Versus Replacement
children.top_down_role: Structural boundary between updating an existing preconditioner and selecting a new construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Refresh Versus Replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision boundary for maintaining an evolving preconditioner during matrix-free Krylov solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\succ0\) precondition the current symmetric system \(H_kp=-g_k\), let \(q_k\geq1\) measure observed preconditioned-solve degradation, and let \(a_k\) be its age. Given thresholds \(1\leq q_{\mathrm{ref}}<q_{\mathrm{rep}}\) and \(0\leq a_{\mathrm{ref}}<a_{\mathrm{rep}}\), refresh the retained preconditioner structure when \(q_{\mathrm{ref}}\leq q_k<q_{\mathrm{rep}}\) or \(a_{\mathrm{ref}}\leq a_k<a_{\mathrm{rep}}\). Replace it when \(q_k\geq q_{\mathrm{rep}}\), \(a_k\geq a_{\mathrm{rep}}\), or the refreshed operator would cease to be symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moderate deterioration triggers a numerical refresh; severe deterioration, excessive age, or loss of positive definiteness triggers complete replacement.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is intended to remain symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k\) is refreshed in the intermediate regime and replaced at the stated validity boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the maintenance-boundary leaf, but the numerical thresholds and refresh/replacement policy are uncited. The disjunctive rules can also trigger both actions unless replacement is explicitly given precedence.

children.title: Gradient-Enriched Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Restricted models containing current first-order directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Enriched Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted Newton subspaces enlarged by current or recent gradient directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(V_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns, and choose indices \(I_k\subseteq\{k-m,\ldots,k\}\). The gradient-enriched subspace is \[\mathcal S_k^{g}=\operatorname{range}(V_k)+\operatorname{span}\{g_i:i\in I_k\}.\] After removing dependent components by orthogonalization, an orthonormal basis \(Q_k\) satisfies \(\operatorname{range}(Q_k)=\mathcal S_k^{g}\); the restricted Newton step has the form \(p_k=Q_kz_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient-enriched subspace augments a base model space with selected current or recent gradients, discarding linearly dependent additions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at every selected iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k^{g}\) for every restricted step \(p_k=Q_kz_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular choice of current/recent gradient enrichment or its role in the restricted Newton family.

children.title: History-Enriched Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Restricted models containing directions retained from earlier iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Enriched Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted Newton subspaces augmented by displacement or gradient-difference history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stored iterates and gradients, define \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\). Given a base basis \(V_k\) and a retained index set \(I_k\), a history-enriched subspace is \[\mathcal S_k^{h}=\operatorname{range}(V_k)+\operatorname{span}\{s_i,y_i:i\in I_k\}.\] Zero vectors and components linearly dependent on the retained basis are removed. An orthonormal basis \(Q_k\) may then be chosen so that \(\operatorname{range}(Q_k)=\mathcal S_k^{h}\), and restricted steps have the form \(p_k=Q_kz_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model space is enlarged with retained iterate displacements and gradient differences, after redundant historical directions are removed.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\) contains only indices for which both consecutive iterates are stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Q_k)=\mathcal S_k^{h}\), and restricted steps satisfy \(p_k=Q_kz_k\).

children.title: Gradient-History Coupling
children.top_down_role: Subspace composition choices balancing current information with persistent historical structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-History Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation of a restricted quadratic model on coupled gradient and history directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_k\) and \(D_k\) contain orthonormalized gradient and history directions, respectively, and set \(Q_k=[G_k\;D_k]\) with full column rank. For the quadratic model \(m_k(p)=g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}H_kp\), writing \(p=Q_k(u,v)\) gives the reduced Hessian \[Q_k^{\mathsf T}H_kQ_k=\begin{pmatrix}G_k^{\mathsf T}H_kG_k&G_k^{\mathsf T}H_kD_k\\D_k^{\mathsf T}H_kG_k&D_k^{\mathsf T}H_kD_k\end{pmatrix}.\] The off-diagonal blocks are the gradient-history coupling terms and cannot be discarded unless their omission is explicitly approximated or they vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected Hessian contains cross blocks linking gradient and historical directions; these blocks quantify their second-order coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling is represented by \(G_k^{\mathsf T}H_kD_k\) and its transpose.

notation.meaning: local Hessian or symmetric Hessian model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and projected block matrix fit the leaf, but the intended coupling model is uncited. The notation p=Q_k(u,v) is also ambiguous; a sourced version should write p=G_ku+D_kv or use an explicit stacked coordinate vector.

children.title: Enrichment Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Loss of useful dimension when current and retained directions are nearly dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Enrichment Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank condition determining whether candidate enrichment directions enlarge a model subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns and let \(W_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\) collect candidate enrichment directions. Define the orthogonal residual \(R_k=(I-Q_kQ_k^{\mathsf T})W_k\). The enrichment is exactly redundant if and only if \(R_k=0\), equivalently \(\operatorname{range}(W_k)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q_k)\). Its number of genuinely new directions is \(\operatorname{rank}(R_k)\), and the enriched dimension is \[\dim\bigl(\operatorname{range}(Q_k)+\operatorname{range}(W_k)\bigr)=r+\operatorname{rank}(R_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate directions are redundant precisely when their components orthogonal to the existing subspace vanish; residual rank counts the new dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enrichment adds exactly \(\operatorname{rank}(R_k)\) dimensions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the redundancy leaf, and the rank identity is standard finite-dimensional linear algebra. Nevertheless, the record supplies neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale as required by the evidence contract.

children.title: Structure-Aligned Subspace Family
children.top_down_role: Subspaces aligned with selected variables, blocks, or active structures.

children.title: Active-Variable Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Restricted Newton models aligned with selected individual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Variable Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate subspaces restricted to variables selected as locally active or influential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an index set \(A_k\subseteq\{1,
\ldots,n\}\), let \(E_{A_k}\) be the matrix whose columns are the coordinate vectors \(e_i\) with \(i\in A_k\). The active-variable subspace is \[\mathcal S_k^{A}=\operatorname{range}(E_{A_k})=\{p\in\mathbb{R}^n:p_i=0\text{ for }i\notin A_k\}.\] Restricting a quadratic Newton model with symmetric matrix \(H_k\) to this subspace yields the reduced system \(E_{A_k}^{\mathsf T}H_kE_{A_k}z=-E_{A_k}^{\mathsf T}g_k\) and step \(p_k=E_{A_k}z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-variable subspace contains directions supported only on selected coordinates; its Newton equation uses the corresponding principal reduced matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every restricted step satisfies \((p_k)_i=0\) for \(i\notin A_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-subspace definition and principal reduced system are coherent and fit the leaf, but no source identifies the intended active-variable selection context or supports this convention within restricted Newton methods.

children.title: Block Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Restricted Newton models aligned with grouped variables or coupled components.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model subspaces assembled from selected coordinate or application-defined variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_J\}\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and choose \(J_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,J\}\). With \(A_k=\bigcup_{j\in J_k}B_j\), the selected block subspace is \[\mathcal S_k^{B}=\{p\in\mathbb{R}^n:p_i=0\text{ for }i\notin A_k\}.\] If \(E_{A_k}\) is its coordinate basis, the restricted quadratic model uses gradient \(E_{A_k}^{\mathsf T}g_k\) and Hessian \(E_{A_k}^{\mathsf T}H_kE_{A_k}\), preserving all within-selected-block and cross-selected-block curvature entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block subspace permits motion only in a chosen union of variable blocks while retaining curvature interactions among all selected blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(\mathcal S_k^{B})=\sum_{j\in J_k}|B_j|\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the block-subspace leaf and is internally consistent for a coordinate partition, but the specific block convention and its restricted-model interpretation lack source support.

children.title: Active-Structure Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Restricted models aligned with currently identified structural activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Structure Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspaces aligned with a locally identified manifold or active structural pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the locally identified active structure near \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be represented by differentiable equations \(c_{A_k}(x)=0\), with Jacobian \(J_{A_k}(x_k)\) of full row rank. Its active-structure subspace is the tangent space \[\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{str}}=\ker J_{A_k}(x_k)=\{p\in\mathbb{R}^n:J_{A_k}(x_k)p=0\}.\] If \(Q_k\) is an orthonormal null-space basis, a structure-preserving restricted step is \(p_k=Q_kz_k\), and the reduced Hessian is \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}H_kQ_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active-structure subspace is the tangent space to the identified local structure, so restricted steps preserve its linearized equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{str}}\) satisfies \(J_{A_k}(x_k)p_k=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Active structure can denote several different objects, so a source is needed to justify the tangent-space interpretation. If it is intended as the tangent space of the equation-defined structure, the hypotheses must also state that c_{A_k}(x_k)=0.

children.title: Selection Instability
children.top_down_role: Subspace variability caused by unstable active-variable or block identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discontinuity caused by hard thresholding in structure-aligned subspace selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let scores \(s_i(x)\) be continuous and select \(A(x)=\{i:s_i(x)\geq\tau\}\) for a fixed threshold \(\tau\). If \(s_j(\bar x)=\tau\) and every neighborhood of \(\bar x\) contains points \(x^+\) and \(x^-\) with \(s_j(x^+)\geq\tau>s_j(x^-)\), then \(A(x)\) is not locally constant at \(\bar x\). Consequently, the coordinate projector \(P(x)=E_{A(x)}E_{A(x)}^{\mathsf T}\) has \(\|P(x^+)-P(x^-)\|_2=1\) whenever only membership of coordinate \(j\) changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard threshold selection is unstable at a tied score: arbitrarily small perturbations can add or remove a direction and change the projector by one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected subspace map is discontinuous at the stated threshold crossing.

notation.meaning: selection score for direction or variable i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the hard-threshold projector jump is mathematically plausible under the stated single-membership-change condition. The record nevertheless lacks either an aligned citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Problem-Mode Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Subspaces derived from physical modes, low-rank factors, or application structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Mode Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspaces generated by application modes, physical basis vectors, or known low-rank factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_k=[u_{k,1},\ldots,u_{k,r}]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) collect application-supplied modes, such as physical eigenmodes, symmetry modes, or columns of a known low-rank factor. The problem-mode subspace is \(\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{mode}}=\operatorname{range}(U_k)\). After rank-revealing orthogonalization, let \(Q_k\) span the same range. Restriction of \(m_k(p)=g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}H_kp\) to \(p=Q_kz\) produces reduced gradient \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\) and reduced Hessian \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}H_kQ_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-mode subspace is the span of application-supplied physical or low-rank modes used to form a reduced second-order model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted model is defined on \(\operatorname{range}(U_k)\) through an orthonormal basis \(Q_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the topic role and gives a coherent reduced quadratic model, but the broad grouping of physical, symmetry, eigenmode, and low-rank-factor directions requires an aligned source.

children.title: Adaptive Subspace Dimension Control
children.top_down_role: Dimension management driven by model quality, stagnation, or resource constraints.

children.title: Adaptive Subspace Expansion
children.top_down_role: Growth of restricted spaces in response to inadequate model quality or stalled progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Subspace Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven enlargement of a restricted Newton subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric operator \(H_k\), gradient \(g_k\), orthonormal basis \(Q_k\), tolerance \(\eta>0\), and dimension cap \(r_{\max}\). Solve the restricted equation \(Q_k^{\mathsf T}H_kQ_kz=-Q_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\), set \(p=Q_kz\), and form \(r=H_kp+g_k\). While \(\|r\|>\eta\|g_k\|\) and \(\dim\operatorname{range}(Q_k)<r_{\max}\), orthogonalize \(r\) against \(Q_k\), append its normalized nonzero component, and resolve. Output the final \(p\) and basis; report dimension-cap termination if the residual test remains unsatisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve in the current subspace, append the orthogonal residual direction when accuracy is inadequate, and stop at tolerance or the dimension cap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either satisfies \(\|H_kp+g_k\|\leq\eta\|g_k\|\) or terminates at dimension \(r_{\max}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the expansion leaf, but the residual-append rule is a specific method requiring a source. Its stated output guarantee also needs conditions ensuring each reduced equation is solvable and the initial dimension does not exceed the cap.

children.title: Adaptive Subspace Restart
children.top_down_role: Replacement or compression of accumulated directions under resource or relevance limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Subspace Restart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-control restart that discards stale directions while preserving selected information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an orthonormal basis \(Q_k\), mandatory vectors \(W_k\), a restart threshold \(r_{\max}\), and retained dimension \(r_{\mathrm{keep}}<r_{\max}\). When \(\dim\operatorname{range}(Q_k)<r_{\max}\), retain \(Q_k\). Otherwise choose at most \(r_{\mathrm{keep}}\) columns or linear combinations of \(Q_k\) according to the prescribed retention score, append \(W_k\), and apply rank-revealing orthogonalization to obtain \(Q_k^+\). Require \(\operatorname{range}(W_k)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q_k^+)\), then resume restricted-model expansion from \(Q_k^+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the dimension limit, retain a scored subset, force inclusion of mandatory directions, reorthogonalize, and resume expansion from the smaller basis.
assumptions_latex: \(W_k\) contains the directions that restart must preserve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After restart, \(\dim\operatorname{range}(Q_k^+)\leq r_{\mathrm{keep}}+\operatorname{rank}(W_k)\) and \(\operatorname{range}(W_k)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q_k^+)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restart leaf, but the retention score, mandatory-vector policy, and restart construction are uncited. The assumptions also do not ensure that retained and mandatory directions fit below the intended dimension cap.

children.title: Expansion Triggers
children.top_down_role: Model-quality and stagnation signals used to justify additional subspace directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Expansion Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient trigger for enlarging a deterministic restricted-Newton subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_k}\) have orthonormal columns and let \(P_k=V_kV_k^{\mathsf T}\). Given \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), expand the subspace whenever \[\|(I-P_k)g_k\|>\eta_{\mathrm{exp}}\|g_k\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_{\mathrm{exp}}<1.\] A valid expansion appends one or more orthonormal vectors spanning a nonzero component of \((I-P_k)g_k\), thereby producing \(V_{k+1}\) with \(\operatorname{range}(V_k)\subsetneq\operatorname{range}(V_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand when a prescribed fraction of the gradient lies outside the current subspace, appending orthonormal directions containing that omitted component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(V_k)\subsetneq\operatorname{range}(V_{k+1})\) and \((I-P_k)g_k\) is represented by the added directions.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the current subspace.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this particular expansion-trigger convention.
Trigger is a precise admissible policy, not a uniquely canonical rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the Expansion Triggers leaf, but the particular omitted-gradient threshold and required expansion response are an uncited policy convention.

children.title: Restart Triggers
children.top_down_role: Resource, conditioning, and obsolescence signals used to refresh the restricted space.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A model-fidelity trigger for discarding a stale restricted-Newton subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trial step \(s_k\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\), define the quadratic model \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}H_ks\) and the agreement ratio \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] If the predicted decrease is positive and \(\rho_k<\eta_{\mathrm{rst}}\), restart by replacing \(V_k\) with a newly generated basis rather than retaining its accumulated directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart when a decrease-predicting restricted quadratic model agrees too poorly with the observed objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x_k\), with \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and symmetric \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k<\eta_{\mathrm{rst}}\) triggers replacement of the accumulated basis \(V_k\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports this particular restart convention.
Trigger is a precise admissible policy, not a uniquely canonical rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The agreement-ratio trigger fits the Restart Triggers leaf, but no source supports this particular restart policy and the admissible range of the restart threshold is not specified.

children.title: Sparse Sampling Subspace Family
children.top_down_role: Sparse sampled spaces aligned with variables or blocks.

children.title: Coordinate-Sampling Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Sparse randomized spaces formed from sampled individual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Sampling Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random subspaces spanned by sampled canonical coordinate directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a random subset and let \(e_i\) denote the \(i\)-th canonical vector of \(\mathbb R^n\). The coordinate-sampling subspace associated with \(I\) is \[\mathcal S_I=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\},\] represented by the selection matrix \(V_I=[e_i]_{i\in I}\). A restricted Newton step has the form \(s=V_Ip\), where \(p\in\mathbb R^{|I|}\), and its reduced Hessian is \(V_I^{\mathsf T}HV_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled coordinate set defines the span of its canonical basis vectors; Newton steps and curvature are restricted to those coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\in\mathcal S_I\) if and only if \(s=V_Ip\) for some \(p\in\mathbb R^{|I|}\).

children.title: Block-Sampling Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Sparse randomized spaces formed from sampled groups of variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Sampling Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random subspaces formed by unions of prescribed coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_q\}\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) be random, and let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric. With \(I_J=\bigcup_{j\in J}B_j\), the block-sampling subspace is \[\mathcal S_J=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I_J\}.\] If \(V_J\) collects these canonical vectors, every restricted step has the form \(s=V_Jp\), where \(p\in\mathbb R^{|I_J|}\), and the reduced curvature matrix is \(V_J^{\mathsf T}HV_J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample whole coordinate blocks, then restrict the Newton step and Hessian to the union of coordinates in those blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_J=\operatorname{range}(V_J)\), and \(s\in\mathcal S_J\) if and only if \(s=V_Jp\) for some \(p\in\mathbb R^{|I_J|}\).

children.title: Sampling-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sparsity, and structural-coverage consequences of coordinate versus block sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dimensional and inclusion-probability consequences of coordinate block size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition into equal blocks of size \(b\), sample \(r\) distinct blocks uniformly without replacement. The resulting subspace has dimension \(rb\), and every coordinate is included with probability \(r/q=rb/n\), where \(q=n/b\). Thus increasing \(b\) at fixed \(r\) increases reduced dimension and couples inclusion of all coordinates within each block; keeping \(rb\) fixed preserves marginal coordinate inclusion but reduces the number of independently selectable groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger sampled blocks increase reduced dimension at fixed block count and force coordinates within a block to be selected together.
assumptions_latex: Exactly \(r\leq q\) blocks are sampled uniformly without replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(\mathcal S)=rb\) and \(\mathbb P(i\in I)=r/q=rb/n\) for every coordinate \(i\).
review_flags: Elementary counting claim is unambiguous, but no supplied locator directly supports the stated tradeoff.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counting formulas and stated granularity consequences are precise and fit the property leaf, but no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale supports the nontrivial tradeoff claim.

children.title: Uneven Inclusion Risk
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes caused by persistently underrepresented variables or blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Uneven Inclusion Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform progress guarantees when important coordinates have vanishing sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let coordinate \(i\) be included independently at each iteration with probability \(p_i\). The waiting time \(T_i\) until its first inclusion satisfies \[\mathbb P(T_i>k)=(1-p_i)^k,\qquad \mathbb E[T_i]=1/p_i\] for \(p_i>0\). If \(p_i=0\), that coordinate is never updated. Consequently, any convergence or coverage guarantee uniform over all coordinates requires a positive lower bound \(p_{\min}=\min_i p_i>0\); otherwise the worst-coordinate expected waiting time is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rarely sampled coordinates have expected waiting time inverse to their inclusion probability; zero probability prevents their update entirely.
assumptions_latex: Coordinate samples are independent across iterations.
Each coordinate \(i\) has fixed marginal inclusion probability \(p_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform finite expected coverage requires \(p_{\min}>0\), with \(\max_i\mathbb E[T_i]=1/p_{\min}\).

notation.meaning: Per-iteration inclusion probability of coordinate i.

children.title: Dense Oblivious Random Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Data-independent dense projections used to compress Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Oblivious Random Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data-independent dense random bases for variable-space compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense oblivious random subspace of dimension \(m\leq n\) is \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(S)\), where \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) is sampled independently of the current gradient and Hessian and is dense almost surely. A standard instance has independent entries \(S_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,1/m)\). For continuous entry distributions, \(S\) has column rank \(m\) almost surely, and a restricted Newton step is parameterized as \(s=Sp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oblivious dense random matrix, sampled independently of local derivatives, spans the compressed variable space used for restricted Newton steps.
assumptions_latex: The distribution of \(S\) is independent of current derivative information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(\operatorname{range}(S))=m\) almost surely for the Gaussian construction, and \(s=Sp\) lies in that subspace.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses dense oblivious random embeddings.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gaussian construction and almost-sure full-rank statement correctly characterize a dense oblivious random subspace, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Structured Fast Random Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Fast-transform and sparse-embedding families for lower-cost projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Fast Random Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fast-transform and sparse-embedding representations of oblivious random subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured fast random subspace is represented as \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(S^{\mathsf T})\) for a random map \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) whose multiplication cost is below dense \(O(mn)\). Two standard forms are \[S=\sqrt{n/m}\,RHD\] with a random sign diagonal \(D\), orthogonal fast transform \(H\), and row sampler \(R\); and a sparse embedding having only a fixed small number of nonzeros per column. Restricted steps are \(s=S^{\mathsf T}p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast transforms or sparse embedding matrices represent random variable subspaces while reducing multiplication cost relative to dense projections.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is orthogonal and admits a fast multiplication algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s=S^{\mathsf T}p\in\operatorname{range}(S^{\mathsf T})\), with structured multiplication cheaper than generic dense multiplication.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses fast random transforms or sparse embeddings.
Exact multiplication complexity depends on the selected transform or sparsity pattern.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the topic, but the fast-transform and sparse-embedding constructions lack a source, and the claim of cost below dense O(mn) requires parameter- and construction-specific qualification.

children.title: Adaptive Random Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Sampling distributions and dimensions changed using progress or model-fidelity information.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Random Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random subspace sampling adapted using observed model fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), a sampling distribution \(\mathcal D_k\), and dimension \(m_k\), sample \(S_k\sim\mathcal D_k\), compute \(p_k\) from a reduced quadratic model, and set \(s_k=S_kp_k\). After evaluating an agreement statistic \(\rho_k\), choose \((\mathcal D_{k+1},m_{k+1})\) measurably from the iteration history: increase coverage or dimension when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), retain it when \(\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2\), and permit reduction when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\). Stop when a prescribed stationarity test holds; otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a restricted Newton space, assess model agreement, then adapt its distribution or dimension before the next iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal D_{k+1}\) depends only on information observed through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathcal D_{k+1},m_{k+1})\) adapts to model fidelity while \(s_k\in\operatorname{range}(S_k)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a canonical adaptive-random-subspace update.
Displayed thresholds specify one admissible algorithmic template.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the threshold update policy is uncited and the reduced model, agreement statistic, acceptance rule, and meaning of increased coverage are not specified sufficiently to identify a reliable algorithm.

children.title: Sketch Placement
children.top_down_role: Alternative locations at which compression enters the Newton model or its linear algebra.

children.title: Variable-Space Restriction
children.top_down_role: Restriction of the candidate Newton direction to a sampled column space.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Space Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-model restriction to the column space of a prescribed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) have full column rank. Restricting the quadratic Newton model \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\) to \(\operatorname{range}(S)\) gives \[\min_{s\in\operatorname{range}(S)}q(s)=\min_{p\in\mathbb R^m}\left((S^{\mathsf T}g)^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}(S^{\mathsf T}HS)p\right).\] If \(S^{\mathsf T}HS\) is positive definite, the unique restricted step is \(s_*=-S(S^{\mathsf T}HS)^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterizing the step by a subspace basis converts the Newton model into a smaller quadratic problem with projected gradient and Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_*=-S(S^{\mathsf T}HS)^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g\) uniquely minimizes \(q\) over \(\operatorname{range}(S)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Space Sketching

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual map \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^N\) with Jacobian \(J\in\mathbb R^{N\times n}\), let \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times N}\). children.title: Row-Space Geometry Preservation
children.top_down_role: Geometric information that row-oriented sketches must retain for useful Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Space Geometry Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace-embedding condition for a left sketch of a matrix factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\), and choose \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). The sketch preserves the geometry induced by the rows of \(A\) when
\[
(1-\varepsilon)\lVert Av\rVert_2^2\leq \lVert SAv\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\lVert Av\rVert_2^2\qquad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Equivalently, in Loewner order,
\[
(1-\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A\preceq A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SA\preceq(1+\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A.
\]
The condition permits rank deficiency and is required only on \(\operatorname{range}(A)\), not on all of \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left sketch preserves row-induced geometry when it approximately preserves every norm of the form ||Av||, equivalently approximating the Gram matrix in Loewner order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1-\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A\preceq A^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SA\preceq(1+\varepsilon)A^{\mathsf T}A\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equivalence between a subspace embedding and its Gram-matrix Loewner bounds

children.title: Residual Weight Distortion
children.top_down_role: Sketching regimes that misrepresent influential residual or data components.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Weight Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective distortion caused by applying a row sketch to a least-squares residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(p)=Ap+b\) and define \(F(p)=\lVert r(p)\rVert_2^2\) and \(F_S(p)=\lVert Sr(p)\rVert_2^2\). If \(S\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-embedding for \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{range}(A),b)\), then every \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies
\[
(1-\varepsilon)F(p)\leq F_S(p)\leq(1+\varepsilon)F(p).
\]
Thus the residual weight distortion
\[
D_S(p)=\frac{F_S(p)}{F(p)}-1
\]
obeys \(\lvert D_S(p)\rvert\leq\varepsilon\) whenever \(F(p)>0\). Embedding only \(\operatorname{range}(A)\) does not generally give this uniform residual bound because \(b\) may have an unpreserved orthogonal component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embedding the span of the data columns and residual offset uniformly bounds sketched objective distortion; embedding the data range alone may not.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) has squared-norm distortion at most \(\varepsilon\) on \(\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{range}(A),b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert F_S(p)/F(p)-1\rvert\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(p\) with \(F(p)>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct application of a subspace-embedding inequality to affine residuals
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-distortion property is mathematically consistent and correctly requires embedding span(range(A),b), but it has no cited source. Supply a specific section, theorem, or page supporting uniform affine-residual preservation under a sketch.

children.title: Curvature-Factor Sketching

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Factor Sketching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sketched positive-semidefinite curvature represented through a compressed structured factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a quadratic model has curvature \(H=B^{\mathsf T}B+\lambda I_n\), where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(\lambda\geq0\). For a left sketch \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times m}\), curvature-factor sketching replaces \(H\) by
\[
\widetilde H=(SB)^{\mathsf T}(SB)+\lambda I_n=B^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}SB+\lambda I_n
\]
and uses \(\widetilde q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Hp\). If \(S\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-embedding for \(\operatorname{range}(B)\), then
\[
(1-\varepsilon)B^{\mathsf T}B+\lambda I_n\preceq\widetilde H\preceq(1+\varepsilon)B^{\mathsf T}B+\lambda I_n.
\]
Hence regularization is retained exactly while the factored curvature is approximated spectrally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressing a curvature factor replaces its Gram matrix by the sketched factor’s Gram matrix while preserving regularization exactly and approximately preserving curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1-\varepsilon)B^{\mathsf T}B+\lambda I_n\preceq\widetilde H\preceq(1+\varepsilon)B^{\mathsf T}B+\lambda I_n\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced Galerkin solve for a symmetric matrix-free Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given symmetric \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), gradient \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and full-column-rank \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\), form the reduced system using only products \(HP\):
\[
(P^{\mathsf T}HP)y=-P^{\mathsf T}g.
\]
If \(P^{\mathsf T}HP\) is nonsingular, solve for \(y\), set \(p=Py\), and return \(p\). The full-system residual \(r=Hp+g\) then satisfies
\[
P^{\mathsf T}r=0.
\]
For a stopping tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), an inexact reduced solve may instead terminate when \(\lVert P^{\mathsf T}r\rVert_2\leq\tau\lVert P^{\mathsf T}g\rVert_2\); its output remains restricted to \(\operatorname{range}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the Newton equation inside a chosen projection space. The returned step lies in that space and its residual is orthogonal to the space.

children.title: Projected Inner Corrections

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Inner Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace correction applied to an existing approximate Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an approximate step \(p_k\), compute its residual \(r_k=Hp_k+g\). For a full-column-rank correction basis \(P_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\), solve
\[
(P_k^{\mathsf T}HP_k)y_k=-P_k^{\mathsf T}r_k
\]
and update
\[
p_{k+1}=p_k+P_ky_k.
\]
When the reduced matrix is nonsingular and the reduced system is solved exactly, the new residual obeys \(P_k^{\mathsf T}(Hp_{k+1}+g)=0\). An inexact correction may stop when this projected residual is at most \(\tau_k\lVert P_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\rVert_2\), where \(\tau_k\in[0,1)\). Output the last iterate once the prescribed full or projected residual test is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each inner iteration, solve for a correction in a selected subspace so the updated Newton residual becomes orthogonal to that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k^{\mathsf T}HP_k\) is nonsingular for the exact correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k^{\mathsf T}(Hp_{k+1}+g)=0\) after an exact projected correction.

children.title: Projection-Space Selection

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Space Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy-norm adequacy criterion for selecting a Newton projection space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be positive definite, let \(p_\star=-H^{-1}g\), and let \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\) have full column rank. For \(\eta\in[0,1)\), the projection space is \(\eta\)-adequate when
\[
\min_{y\in\mathbb{R}^s}\lVert p_\star-Py\rVert_H\leq\eta\lVert p_\star\rVert_H,
\qquad \lVert z\rVert_H=(z^{\mathsf T}Hz)^{1/2}.
\]
The reduced Galerkin step \(p_P=-P(P^{\mathsf T}HP)^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}g\) is the minimizing vector, so adequacy is equivalent to
\[
\lVert p_\star-p_P\rVert_H\leq\eta\lVert p_\star\rVert_H.
\]
Thus selection is based on approximation of the Newton direction in the curvature metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection space is adequate when its best approximation to the Newton step has prescribed relative error in the Hessian energy norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert p_\star-p_P\rVert_H\leq\eta\lVert p_\star\rVert_H\).

notation.meaning: Galerkin step in the selected space.
Energy norm induced by the positive-definite curvature matrix.

children.title: Sketch-Induced Residual Bias

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Induced Residual Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a sketched residual test to control unobserved residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=I_2\), \(g=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(S=(1,0)\). Minimizing the sketched residual objective
\[
\lVert S(Hp+g)\rVert_2^2=p_1^2
\]
permits every vector \(p=(0,t)^{\mathsf T}\). In particular, \(p=(0,0)^{\mathsf T}\) has zero sketched residual but full residual \(Hp+g=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\). More generally, if \(S\) is not injective on the attainable residual space, then \(\lVert S(Hp+g)\rVert_2\) cannot uniformly control \(\lVert Hp+g\rVert_2\). The bias disappears under a lower embedding bound on that residual space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch can report zero residual while a full residual component remains unseen. A lower embedding bound on attainable residuals excludes this failure.
assumptions_latex: The stopping rule or objective observes only \(S(Hp+g)\).
The sketch has a nontrivial null direction in the attainable residual space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert S(Hp+g)\rVert_2=0\) need not imply \(Hp+g=0\).

children.title: Deterministic Subspace Adequacy

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Subspace Adequacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic coverage test for gradient and minimum-curvature information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\) have orthonormal columns. For tolerances \(\eta_g\in[0,1]\) and \(\eta_H\geq0\), call \(\operatorname{range}(P)\) adequate when
\[
\lVert(I-PP^{\mathsf T})g\rVert_2\leq\eta_g\lVert g\rVert_2
\]
and
\[
\lambda_{\min}(P^{\mathsf T}HP)\leq\lambda_{\min}(H)+\eta_H.
\]
The first inequality controls omitted first-order descent information; the second requires the reduced model to contain a direction whose Rayleigh quotient approximates the most negative full-space curvature. Both predicates are deterministic and can be evaluated independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic subspace is adequate when it captures most of the gradient and contains a direction approximating the matrix’s minimum curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(I-PP^{\mathsf T})g\rVert_2\leq\eta_g\lVert g\rVert_2\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(P^{\mathsf T}HP)\leq\lambda_{\min}(H)+\eta_H\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthogonal projection error and Rayleigh-quotient coverage are explicit deterministic adequacy measures
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two inequalities form a coherent deterministic adequacy definition and match the topic role, but this particular joint gradient-and-curvature criterion is a domain-specific definition choice. children.title: Probabilistic Embedding Adequacy
children.top_down_role: High-probability preservation regimes for randomized models.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Embedding Adequacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability subspace-embedding requirement for a randomized projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a fixed \(k\)-dimensional subspace containing the gradient and curvature directions required by a restricted model. A random matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times n}\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-adequate for \(\mathcal U\) when
\[
\mathbb P\!\left((1-\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2\leq\lVert Su\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\lVert u\rVert_2^2\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\right)\geq1-\delta.
\]
Here \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) controls geometric distortion and \(\delta\in(0,1)\) controls failure probability. Adequacy applies only to a subspace fixed independently of the draw unless a stronger adaptive guarantee is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random projection is adequate when it preserves every norm in the decisive subspace within relative distortion ε with probability at least 1−δ.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a fixed finite-dimensional subspace.
\(S\) is drawn independently of the information used to fix \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(S\text{ embeds }\mathcal U\text{ with distortion }\varepsilon)\geq1-\delta\).

children.title: Dimension–Accuracy–Work Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension–Accuracy–Work Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-model resource bounds for an explicit reduced Newton system of dimension \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_s\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times s}\) have orthonormal columns, and suppose one matrix-free product with \(H\) costs \(C_H\). Forming \(HP_s\), assembling \(P_s^{\mathsf T}HP_s\), and solving the dense reduced system require, respectively,
\[
sC_H,
\qquad O(ns^2),
\qquad O(s^3)
\]
work, with \(O(ns+s^2)\) storage when \(P_s\) and \(HP_s\) are retained. If \(H\) is positive definite and \(p_\star=-H^{-1}g\), the attainable relative accuracy is
\[
\eta_s=\frac{\min_y\lVert p_\star-P_sy\rVert_H}{\lVert p_\star\rVert_H}.
\]
Thus increasing \(s\) cannot increase \(\eta_s\) for nested spaces, but raises derivative-action, assembly, storage, and reduced-solve costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger nested subspaces improve best attainable energy-norm accuracy monotonically, while requiring more Hessian actions, storage, reduced-matrix assembly, and dense-solve work.
assumptions_latex: \(P_s\) has orthonormal columns; accuracy is measured in the energy norm when \(H\) is positive definite.
The reduced matrix is assembled explicitly and solved by a dense direct method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(s)=sC_H+O(ns^2+s^3)\), storage is \(O(ns+s^2)\), and \(\eta_{s+1}\leq\eta_s\) for nested spaces.

children.title: Missed Descent Curvature
children.top_down_role: Restricted spaces omitting curvature directions important for objective decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Descent Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A restricted model may omit a positively curved direction that yields descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(g=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \(H=I_2\), and the restricted space generated by \(P=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\). The reduced quadratic model has projected gradient \(P^{\mathsf T}g=0\), so its unique reduced minimizer is the zero step. Nevertheless, the omitted direction \(d=(0,-1)^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies
\[
g^{\mathsf T}d=-1<0,
\qquad d^{\mathsf T}Hd=1>0,
\]
and the full quadratic model is minimized at \(p_\star=(0,-1)^{\mathsf T}\). Hence positive definiteness of the reduced curvature does not certify absence of a useful full-space descent direction when the projected gradient omits a component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace can have a zero projected gradient and positive curvature yet miss a positively curved full-space direction that decreases the model.
assumptions_latex: Gradient coverage outside that space is not enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{\mathsf T}g=0\) does not imply that no \(d\) satisfies \(g^{\mathsf T}d<0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\).

children.title: Missed Negative Curvature

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Negative Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A restricted Hessian may appear positive definite while the full Hessian is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
H=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad P=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the reduced curvature is \(P^{\mathsf T}HP=1>0\), although the full matrix has \(\lambda_{\min}(H)=-1\) with negative-curvature direction \(v=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\). Thus a positive-definite projected Hessian does not imply positive semidefiniteness of \(H\). More generally, negative curvature is missed whenever the chosen subspace has no vector with a sufficiently large component in the negative eigenspace; equivalently, the minimum Rayleigh quotient over \(\operatorname{range}(P)\) can remain nonnegative while the full-space minimum Rayleigh quotient is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected Hessian can be positive definite even though the full Hessian has negative curvature, as shown by a two-dimensional diagonal example.
assumptions_latex: Curvature is inspected only through \(P^{\mathsf T}HP\).
The projection space need not intersect the negative eigenspace nontrivially.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{\mathsf T}HP\succ0\) does not imply \(H\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance of independent randomized curvature samples and its reduction by averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be independent, identically distributed scalar curvature estimates with \(\mathbb E[X_i]=\mu\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(X_i)=\sigma^2<\infty\). For the sample mean \(\bar X_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N X_i\), independence gives \[\mathbb E[\bar X_N]=\mu,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\bar X_N)=\frac{\sigma^2}{N}.\] Thus achieving root-mean-square sampling error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) requires \(N\geq \sigma^2/\varepsilon^2\). This statement concerns sampling error only; any bias caused by restricting curvature to a sampled subspace is separate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging independent unbiased curvature samples divides variance by the sample count; RMS sampling error at most epsilon requires at least variance divided by epsilon squared samples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_N)=\sigma^2/N\) and \(N\geq\sigma^2/\varepsilon^2\) suffices for RMS error at most \(\varepsilon\).
review_flags: Exact intended curvature estimator is unspecified by the navigation path.

children.title: Curvature-Coverage Probability
