knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Coverage Probability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability that a random subspace approximately captures a prescribed curvature-bearing subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning a target curvature subspace, let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a random subspace, and let \(P_S\) be its orthogonal projector. For tolerance \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\), the curvature-coverage probability is \[p_{\mathrm{cov}}(\varepsilon;U,S):=\mathbb P\!\left(\left\|(I-P_S)U\right\|_2\leq\varepsilon\right).\] The event means that every unit vector in \(\operatorname{range}(U)\) lies within Euclidean distance \(\varepsilon\) of \(S\). Exact coverage is the case \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage probability is the chance that the sampled subspace approximates every direction in a specified curvature-bearing subspace within a chosen tolerance.

children.title: Full-Space Saddle-Point Systems
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal-dual representations retaining the complete KKT structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Saddle-Point Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained Newton equation in coupled primal–dual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained quadratic model with symmetric Hessian \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), constraint Jacobian \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), gradient residual \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and constraint residual \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), the full-space Newton step \((p,y)\) satisfies \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}g\\c\end{pmatrix}.\] Equivalently, \(Hp+A^Ty=-g\) and \(Ap=-c\). If \(A\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), the saddle-point matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-space formulation solves primal and multiplier steps together in the complete KKT saddle-point system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed KKT matrix is nonsingular and uniquely determines \((p,y)\).

children.title: Null-Space Reduced-Hessian Systems
children.top_down_role: Feasible-direction representations centered on projected curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Reduced-Hessian Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-direction reduction of the KKT equation to projected curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), where \(A\) has full row rank. Let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), and choose \(p_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ap_0=-c\). Every feasible step has the form \(p=p_0+Zq\) for some \(q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\). Premultiplying the primal KKT equation \(Hp+A^Ty=-g\), with \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), by \(Z^T\) yields \[(Z^THZ)q=-Z^T(g+Hp_0).\] If \(Z^THZ\) is nonsingular, this equation uniquely determines \(q\), hence \(p\); the multiplier is subsequently recovered from \(A^Ty=-g-Hp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterizing feasible steps by a null-space basis reduces the KKT system to the Hessian projected onto feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(A\) has full row rank, \(AZ=0\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\).

children.title: Range-Space Schur Systems
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-space representations obtained by primal elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Schur Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space reduction obtained by eliminating the primal Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the KKT equations \(Hp+A^Ty=-g\) and \(Ap=-c\), where \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular. Eliminating \(p=-H^{-1}(g+A^Ty)\) gives the multiplier-space Schur system \[(AH^{-1}A^T)y=c-AH^{-1}g.\] After solving it, the primal step is recovered from \(p=-H^{-1}(g+A^Ty)\). If \(H\) is symmetric positive definite and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(AH^{-1}A^T\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step produces a multiplier-space Schur complement system, after which the primal step is recovered by one Hessian solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((AH^{-1}A^T)y=c-AH^{-1}g\), with \(AH^{-1}A^T\) symmetric positive definite.

children.title: Augmented KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Coupled KKT representations modified through augmentation of selected blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactly equivalent KKT representation formed by an augmented-Lagrangian row operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\rho\in\mathbb R\), add \(\rho A^T\) times the constraint equation \(Ap=-c\) to the primal equation \(Hp+A^Ty=-g\). The resulting augmented system is \[\begin{pmatrix}H+\rho A^TA&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}g+\rho A^Tc\\c\end{pmatrix}.\] This row operation is invertible, so the augmented and original KKT systems have exactly the same solutions. When \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), a suitable positive \(\rho\) can improve primal-block definiteness without changing the Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a weighted constraint equation to the primal equation changes the KKT operator but preserves its exact solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented system and the original KKT system have identical solution sets.
review_flags: A source specifically supporting the augmented KKT equivalence and definiteness qualification is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The augmented row operation and its exact-equivalence claim are mathematically plausible, but no source supports the KKT-specific representation or the stated definiteness qualification.

children.title: Regularized KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: KKT representations stabilized by primal, dual, or blockwise regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-diagonally perturbed saddle-point system used to improve solvability or conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a KKT operator \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), primal regularization \(R_p=R_p^T\succeq0\), and dual regularization \(R_d=R_d^T\succeq0\), the regularized KKT system is \[\begin{pmatrix}H+R_p&A^T\\A&-R_d\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}g\\c\end{pmatrix}.\] Unlike an exact augmented row operation, nonzero \(R_p\) or \(R_d\) generally changes the computed step. Scalar regularization uses \(R_p=\delta I_n\) and \(R_d=\gamma I_m\) with \(\delta,\gamma\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized KKT system adds positive semidefinite primal and dual block perturbations, generally trading exactness for improved numerical behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized operator is \(K_{R}=\begin{pmatrix}H+R_p&A^T\\A&-R_d\end{pmatrix}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically identifies the adopted sign convention for regularized KKT systems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent and fits the container, but the dual-block sign convention and interpretation of the perturbations require a cited source.

children.title: Primal Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization focused on primal curvature or primal-system singularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral effect of adding a positive shift to the primal KKT block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar primal regularization \(R_p=\delta I_n\) with \(\delta>0\), every eigenvalue of the symmetric primal block shifts according to \[\lambda_i(H+\delta I_n)=\lambda_i(H)+\delta.\] Consequently, \(H+\delta I_n\) is positive definite whenever \(\delta>-\lambda_{\min}(H)\). In the corresponding regularized KKT equations, the primal stationarity equation becomes \((H+\delta I_n)p+A^Ty=-g\), while the constraint equation remains \(Ap=-c\). Thus primal regularization changes stationarity but does not directly relax linearized feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive primal shift raises every Hessian eigenvalue and can make the primal block positive definite while leaving the constraint equation unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i(H+\delta I_n)=\lambda_i(H)+\delta\), and \(Ap=-c\) is unchanged.
review_flags: The spectral statement is standard, but a source connecting it to primal KKT regularization is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue-shift statement is standard and correct, but no source connects it to the adopted primal KKT regularization model in this taxonomy.

children.title: Dual Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization focused on multiplier blocks or constraint degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-relaxation effect of a negative dual diagonal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar dual regularization \(R_d=\gamma I_m\) with \(\gamma>0\), the regularized KKT equations are \[Hp+A^Ty=-g,\qquad Ap-\gamma y=-c.\] Hence the linearized feasibility residual satisfies \(Ap+c=\gamma y\), rather than vanishing identically. If \(H\) is invertible, eliminating \(p\) gives \[(AH^{-1}A^T+\gamma I_m)y=c-AH^{-1}g,\] so dual regularization shifts the multiplier-space Schur operator by \(\gamma I_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual regularization relaxes linearized feasibility and adds a positive diagonal shift to the multiplier-space Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap+c=\gamma y\) and the Schur operator becomes \(AH^{-1}A^T+\gamma I_m\).
review_flags: A source supporting the adopted dual-block sign convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebra is correct under the displayed negative dual-block convention, but that convention and its KKT interpretation are unsupported by a source.

children.title: Stabilization Bias
children.top_down_role: Distortion of the intended KKT correction caused by excessive stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary quantifying deviation of a stabilized KKT solution from the exact step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kz=b\) be a nonsingular exact KKT system with \(z\neq0\), and let the stabilized system be \((K+E)z_E=b\). If \(\|K^{-1}E\|<1\) in a subordinate norm, then \(K+E\) is nonsingular and \[z_E-z=-(K+E)^{-1}Ez,\qquad \frac{\|z_E-z\|}{\|z\|}\leq\frac{\|K^{-1}E\|}{1-\|K^{-1}E\|}.\] Thus a nonzero stabilization generally biases the step; the bound loses control as \(\|K^{-1}E\|\) approaches one, marking the perturbative stability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero exact KKT solution, regularization generally changes the step, with relative bias controlled while the scaled perturbation norm remains below one.

notation.meaning: stabilizing perturbation of the KKT operator

children.title: Primal-Block Elimination

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Block Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block Gaussian elimination producing a multiplier-space Schur system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\begin{pmatrix}B&C^T\\C&-D\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r\\s\end{pmatrix},\] where \(B\) is nonsingular. From \(p=B^{-1}(r-C^Ty)\), substitution into the second block equation gives \[(D+CB^{-1}C^T)y=CB^{-1}r-s.\] After solving this multiplier-space equation, recover \(p=B^{-1}(r-C^Ty)\). The reduction is algebraically equivalent to the original block system whenever the required solves are exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting the primal block and substituting its solution yields a multiplier-space Schur complement equation with exact back-substitution.

children.title: Dual-Block Elimination

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Block Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block Gaussian elimination producing a primal-space Schur system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\begin{pmatrix}B&C^T\\C&-D\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r\\s\end{pmatrix},\] where \(D\) is nonsingular. The second block equation gives \(y=D^{-1}(Cp-s)\). Substitution into the first equation produces the primal-space system \[(B+C^TD^{-1}C)p=r+C^TD^{-1}s.\] After solving it, recover \(y=D^{-1}(Cp-s)\). The reduction is algebraically equivalent to the original system whenever the block solves are exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting the dual block and substituting its solution yields a primal-space Schur complement equation with exact recovery of the multiplier.

children.title: Implicit Schur Actions
children.top_down_role: Matrix-free reduced actions realized through nested block solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Schur Actions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free action of the dual Schur complement induced by primal elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a block operator \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), with invertible \(H\), define the dual Schur complement \(S=C+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). For an input \(v\), compute \(t=A^{\mathsf T}v\), obtain \(w\) from the nested solve \(Hw=t\), and return \(Sv=Cv+Aw\). Thus applying \(S\) requires only actions of \(A\), \(A^{\mathsf T}\), and \(C\), together with a solve using \(H\); neither \(H^{-1}\) nor \(S\) is formed explicitly. An inexact inner solve replaces \(w\) by \(\widetilde w\) and returns \(Cv+A\widetilde w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the Schur complement by multiplying through the constraint blocks and solving one primal-block system, without explicitly forming the reduced matrix or an inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sv=Cv+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}v

notation.meaning: exact Schur-complement matrix restricted to the multiplier subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectrally equivalent reduced models suitable for scalable multiplier-space preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a finite-dimensional multiplier subspace, and let \(S\) and \(\widetilde S\) be symmetric positive-definite matrices on \(Y\). The accessible matrix \(\widetilde S\) is a spectrally equivalent approximate Schur model if constants \(0<\alpha\leq\beta<\infty\), independent of the discretization size, satisfy \[\alpha\,v^{\mathsf T}\widetilde S v\leq v^{\mathsf T}Sv\leq\beta\,v^{\mathsf T}\widetilde S v\qquad\text{for every }v\in Y.\] Consequently, every eigenvalue of \(\widetilde S^{-1}S\), restricted to \(Y\), lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and \(\kappa_2(\widetilde S^{-1/2}S\widetilde S^{-1/2})\leq\beta/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Schur model is scalable when its quadratic form uniformly bounds the exact Schur form above and below on the multiplier subspace; the corresponding symmetric preconditioned operator then has condition number at most the ratio of the bounds.

children.title: KKT Krylov Solver Families

children.title: Symmetric-Indefinite KKT Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Symmetry-preserving methods for coupled saddle-point operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite KKT Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MINRES-type iteration for self-adjoint, indefinite KKT operators with symmetry-compatible preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric KKT system \(Kz=b\) and a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(P\), apply MINRES to the self-adjoint operator \(P^{-1}K\) in the inner product \(\langle u,v\rangle_P=u^{\mathsf T}Pv\). Starting from \(z_0\), generate the preconditioned Lanczos space \(\mathcal K_k(P^{-1}K,P^{-1}r_0)\), where \(r_0=b-Kz_0\), and choose \(z_k\) in \(z_0+\mathcal K_k(P^{-1}K,P^{-1}r_0)\) to minimize \(\|b-Kz_k\|_{P^{-1}}\). Stop when this residual norm satisfies the prescribed tolerance and return \(z_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use preconditioned MINRES when the KKT operator is symmetric indefinite and the positive-definite preconditioner preserves self-adjointness in its induced inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_k\in z_0+\mathcal K_k(P^{-1}K,P^{-1}r_0)\text{ minimizes }\|b-Kz_k\|_{P^{-1}}

children.title: Nonsymmetric KKT Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods for nonsymmetric systems and symmetry-breaking preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric KKT Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimizing Krylov iteration for nonsymmetric KKT operators or symmetry-breaking preconditioners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular, possibly nonsymmetric KKT matrix \(K\), choose a nonsingular right preconditioner \(P\) and solve \(KP^{-1}y=b\) by GMRES. With \(r_0=b-Kz_0\), construct \(y_k\in\mathcal K_k(KP^{-1},r_0)\) minimizing \(\|r_0-KP^{-1}y\|_2\), and set \(z_k=z_0+P^{-1}y_k\). Arnoldi orthogonalization uses only products with \(K\) and applications of \(P^{-1}\). Stop when \(\|b-Kz_k\|_2\leq\varepsilon\|b\|_2\), and return \(z_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply right-preconditioned GMRES to a nonsymmetric KKT system, minimizing the true residual over the generated Krylov correction space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_k=z_0+P^{-1}y_k,\quad y_k\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathcal K_k(KP^{-1},r_0)}\|r_0-KP^{-1}y\|_2

children.title: Constraint-Preserving Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Projected methods maintaining feasibility or constraint-compatible iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Preserving Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected Krylov iteration whose corrections remain in the null space of the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\), and suppose \(Ax_0=c\). Apply a Krylov method to the reduced system \((Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}g\), generating \(p_k\in\mathcal K_k(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ,-Z^{\mathsf T}g)\), and define \(x_k=x_0+Zp_k\). Stop according to the reduced residual and return \(x_k\). Since \(AZ=0\), every iterate satisfies \(Ax_k=c\); feasibility is preserved independently of the number of Krylov steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate all Krylov corrections in the constraint null space, so an initially feasible iterate remains feasible while the reduced system is solved.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax_k=c\quad\text{for every }k

children.title: Flexible Nested KKT Krylov Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Flexible Nested KKT Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flexible outer iteration allowing iteration-dependent, inexact block-preconditioner applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Kz=b\), start with \(z_0\) and \(r_0=b-Kz_0\). At outer step \(j\), apply a possibly changing nonlinear or inexact preconditioner to the current Arnoldi vector, obtaining \(q_j=\mathcal M_j(v_j)\), and orthogonalize \(Kq_j\) against the existing Arnoldi basis. Flexible GMRES chooses coefficients \(y_k\) minimizing \(\|\beta e_1-\overline H_k y\|_2\) and sets \(z_k=z_0+Q_k y_k\), where \(Q_k=[q_1,\ldots,q_k]\). Stop when the associated true residual meets tolerance; all \(q_j\) must be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flexible GMRES permits each outer iteration to use a different inexact block solve, while minimizing the residual over the stored preconditioned directions.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M_j\text{ returns a finite vector for each Arnoldi vector }v_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_k=z_0+Q_k y_k,\quad y_k\in\arg\min_y\|\beta e_1-\overline H_k y\|_2

children.title: Block-Diagonal KKT Preconditioners

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Diagonal KKT Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent primal- and multiplier-block approximations for saddle-point systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), a block-diagonal KKT preconditioner has the form \[P_D=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\0&\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},\] where \(\widetilde H\) approximates the primal block \(H\) and \(\widetilde S\) approximates the positive Schur operator \(S=C+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Its application decouples into \(\widetilde H u=r_x\) and \(\widetilde S v=r_\lambda\). If a symmetry-preserving Krylov method is intended, both diagonal approximations are required to be symmetric positive definite on their respective spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal KKT preconditioner separately approximates the primal block and positive Schur complement, so its two component solves are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_D^{-1}(r_x,r_\lambda)=(\widetilde H^{-1}r_x,\widetilde S^{-1}r_\lambda)

children.title: Block-Triangular KKT Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Factorization-inspired constructions retaining an elimination direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Triangular KKT Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization-based preconditioners retaining one block-elimination direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\), lower and upper block-triangular preconditioners are \[P_L=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\A&-\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},\qquad P_U=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&A^{\mathsf T}\\0&-\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},\] where \(\widetilde H\) and \(\widetilde S\) are nonsingular approximations to \(H\) and \(S=C+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Applying either preconditioner consists of two sequential block solves and one coupling-block product. The retained off-diagonal block encodes, respectively, forward or backward approximate block elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-triangular preconditioner approximates a KKT factorization and retains one coupling block, producing two sequential rather than independent block solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_L\text{ and }P_U\text{ are nonsingular block-elimination preconditioners}

children.title: Constraint Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Constructions preserving or approximating the constraint block geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT preconditioners retaining the exact constraint coupling while approximating primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle-point matrix \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), a constraint preconditioner is \[P_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\] where \(G=G^{\mathsf T}\) approximates \(H\), while the constraint blocks are retained exactly. If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^{\mathsf T}GZ\) is nonsingular for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\), then \(P_C\) is nonsingular. Solving with \(P_C\) maps a residual through a system having the same linearized constraint geometry as \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner replaces primal curvature but keeps both constraint couplings exact; nonsingularity reduces to invertibility on the constraint null space.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z^{\mathsf T}GZ\text{ nonsingular}\Longrightarrow P_C\text{ nonsingular}

notation.meaning: basis of the constraint null space

children.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Reduced-operator approximations for multiplier-space acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space preconditioning by an accessible approximation of the reduced Schur operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\) with invertible \(H\), let \(S=C+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). A Schur-complement preconditioner supplies a readily invertible \(\widetilde S\) and uses \(\widetilde S^{-1}\) to precondition the reduced multiplier equation \(S\lambda=d\), either directly or inside a block KKT preconditioner. If \(S\) and \(\widetilde S\) are symmetric positive definite and \(\alpha\widetilde S\preceq S\preceq\beta\widetilde S\), then \(\sigma(\widetilde S^{-1}S)\subseteq[\alpha,\beta]\); mesh-independent \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) give a uniformly conditioned reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Schur-complement preconditioner accelerates the multiplier equation using an invertible reduced approximation; spectral equivalence yields uniformly bounded preconditioned eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ and }\widetilde S\text{ are symmetric positive definite}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha\widetilde S\preceq S\preceq\beta\widetilde S\Longrightarrow\sigma(\widetilde S^{-1}S)\subseteq[\alpha,\beta]

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian KKT Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Stabilized block constructions exploiting augmented primal curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian KKT Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT preconditioning based on constraint-augmented primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), choose \(\gamma>0\) and a symmetric positive-definite multiplier weight \(W\). Define the augmented primal block \(H_\gamma=H+\gamma A^{\mathsf T}W^{-1}A\). An augmented-Lagrangian KKT preconditioner uses an accessible approximation \(\widetilde H_\gamma\) of \(H_\gamma\), together with a compatible multiplier block, for example \[P_{AL}=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H_\gamma&0\\0&\gamma^{-1}W\end{bmatrix}.\] The augmentation adds no curvature on \(\ker A\), because \(Z^{\mathsf T}H_\gamma Z=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) whenever \(AZ=0\), while strengthening curvature in constraint-visible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented-Lagrangian preconditioners add weighted constraint curvature to the primal block while leaving the reduced Hessian on feasible directions unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AZ=0\Longrightarrow Z^{\mathsf T}H_\gamma Z=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ

children.title: Explicit Null-Space Bases
children.top_down_role: Reduced systems built from stored bases of feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Null-Space Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stored-basis reduction of equality-constrained Newton equations to feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\). Every solution of \(As=b\) has the representation \(s=s_p+Zp\), where \(As_p=b\). For the quadratic model \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), stationarity over the feasible affine space is equivalent to \[(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}(g+Hs_p).\] If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular, this reduced system uniquely determines \(p\), and hence the constrained step \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store a basis of the constraint null space, represent every feasible step as a particular step plus a null-space correction, and solve the reduced Hessian system.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s=s_p+Zp,\quad (Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}(g+Hs_p)

notation.meaning: particular solution of the linear constraints

children.title: Implicit Null-Space Projections
children.top_down_role: Projected actions without explicit basis formation.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Null-Space Projections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection for full-row-rank equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), compute the unique \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying \((AA^{\mathsf T})y=Av\), and set \(Pv=v-A^{\mathsf T}y\). Then \(APv=0\), \(P^{\mathsf T}=P\), \(P^2=P\), \(\operatorname{range}(P)=\ker A\), and \(v-Pv\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\). Thus the feasible-direction projection is applied without forming a null-space basis or the dense matrix \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve one constraint-space system and subtract its range-space component to project a vector onto feasible directions without forming a null-space basis or dense projector.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=I_n-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), and its action requires only products with \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\) and solves with \(AA^{\mathsf T}\).

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Krylov Solves
children.top_down_role: Iterative solution of projected curvature systems in feasible-direction space.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Krylov Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite reduced system solved by projected conjugate gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(p_0=0\) and \(r_0=-Pg\). Apply conjugate gradients on \(\ker A\), replacing each curvature product by \(P(Hd_k)\), where \(d_k\in\ker A\) is the current search direction. Stop when \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta\|r_0\|\) for a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), or when \(d_k^{\mathsf T}Hd_k\leq0\) is detected. Every returned iterate \(p_k\) satisfies \(Ap_k=0\). If the reduced operator is positive definite and arithmetic is exact, conjugate gradients reaches the exact reduced-system solution in at most \(\dim(\ker A)\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected conjugate gradients solves the reduced Newton equation using curvature and projection products while keeping every iterate in the feasible-direction space.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
The restriction of \(PHP\) to \(\ker A\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projected conjugate gradients generates feasible iterates and solves \((PHP)|_{\ker A}p=-Pg\) using only matrix-free actions of \(H\) and \(P\).

notation.meaning: model gradient or reduced-system right-hand-side generator

children.title: Normal-Tangential Step-Space Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Step decompositions separating feasibility restoration from objective reduction.

children.title: Normal Step Spaces
children.top_down_role: Step components oriented toward reduction of constraint infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Step Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal space induced by a linearized equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the normal step space associated with \(A\) by \(\mathcal N_A:=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\). A normal step \(n\in\mathcal N_A\) has the form \(n=A^{\mathsf T}y\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Since \(\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=(\ker A)^{\perp}\), every normal step is orthogonal to every first-order feasible direction. For \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(-c\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), the unique least-norm solution of \(An=-c\) belongs to \(\mathcal N_A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal steps lie in the Jacobian-transpose range, are orthogonal to feasible directions, and contain the least-norm correction of a consistent linearized constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normal step space is \(\mathcal N_A=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=(\ker A)^{\perp}\).

children.title: Tangential Step Spaces
children.top_down_role: Step components oriented toward objective improvement within linearized feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Step Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized feasible-direction space for equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the tangential step space associated with \(A\) by \(\mathcal T_A:=\ker A=\{t\in\mathbb{R}^n:At=0\}\). If \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\), a normal step \(n\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(An=-c\), and \(t\in\mathcal T_A\), then \(A(n+t)=-c\). Under the Euclidean inner product, \(\mathcal T_A=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})^{\perp}\), whether or not the rows of \(A\) are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangential steps are null-space directions that preserve any linearized constraint correction already achieved by a normal step.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangential step space is \(\mathcal T_A=\ker A=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})^{\perp}\).

children.title: Normal-Tangential Coupling
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between feasibility-restoration components and reduced objective components.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Tangential Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-curvature term in a normal-tangential quadratic step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\) and \(p=n+t\), \[q(n+t)=q(n)+g^{\mathsf T}t+\tfrac12t^{\mathsf T}Ht+t^{\mathsf T}Hn.\] Although \(n^{\mathsf T}t=0\), the coupling term \(t^{\mathsf T}Hn\) need not vanish. The quadratic curvature separates for the selected pair \((n,t)\) exactly when \(t^{\mathsf T}Hn=0\). It separates for every \(n\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\) and \(t\in\ker A\) exactly when \(H\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal and tangential steps are Euclidean-orthogonal, but a selected pair remains coupled through its cross-curvature term unless that term vanishes; global separation is equivalent to curvature preserving the normal space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic curvature separates for a selected normal-tangential pair exactly when \(t^{\mathsf T}Hn=0\); Euclidean orthogonality alone does not ensure this.

notation.meaning: linear coefficient of the quadratic model

children.title: Inexact Decomposition Leakage
children.top_down_role: Loss of role separation under approximate projections or inner solves.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the exact orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(\|A\widetilde Pv\|\) and \(\|(I-P)\widetilde Pv\|\) measure leakage of an intended tangential action into the normal space.
review_flags: exact leakage bounds need a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility loss caused by an inexact tangential projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an intended tangential vector \(\widetilde t=\widetilde Pv\), exact decomposition requires \(A\widetilde t=0\). If \(\widetilde P\neq P\), then \(A\widetilde t=A(\widetilde P-P)v\), so \(\|A\widetilde t\|\leq\|A\|\,\|\widetilde P-P\|\,\|v\|\). Equivalently, its normal leakage is \((I-P)\widetilde t=(I-P)(\widetilde P-P)v\). Thus a small inner-solve residual is insufficient by itself: the approximate action must control the induced feasibility defect, or repeated projected operations can accumulate nonzero normal components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate tangential projector leaks into the normal space in proportion to its projector error, producing a measurable linearized feasibility defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Decomposition Leakage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic leakage identities are plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source is supplied for the norm bound's use as a decomposition diagnostic or for the claim about accumulation under repeated approximate projections.

children.title: KKT Structural Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions disrupting reductions, Krylov geometry, preconditioning, or residual interpretation.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Jacobians
children.top_down_role: Dependent constraints and nonunique multiplier directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Jacobians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained KKT system with dependent constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any symmetric \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), the KKT matrix \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) is singular when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\). For every consistent KKT system, if \((p,\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\) is a solution, then \((p,\lambda+y)\) is also a solution for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). Thus the multiplier is determined only modulo \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\), although the primal step can remain unique under suitable reduced-curvature conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraint rows make the KKT matrix singular and leave multiplier components in the transpose null space nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT matrix is singular, and multiplier components in \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\) are unidentifiable.

children.title: Singular Reduced Curvature
children.top_down_role: Weak or absent curvature along feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained system with full-rank constraints but degenerate feasible curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\). If \(R\) is singular, then the reduced equation \(Ru=b\) lacks a unique solution for every \(b\) for which it is consistent and is inconsistent for some \(b\). Under the stated full-row-rank assumption on \(A\), singularity of \(R\) also implies singularity of the KKT matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular curvature on the feasible-direction space prevents unique reduced Newton solves and makes the equality-constrained KKT matrix singular.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) has columns forming a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is singular, the reduced Newton equation is not uniquely solvable for all right-hand sides, and the KKT matrix is singular.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Schur Complements
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-space stiffness and unstable nested elimination.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Schur complement \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite, but small eigenvalues or a large condition number amplify multiplier-solve errors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for exact primal elimination in an equality KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminating the primal variable produces \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). For every \(0\neq y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(y^{\mathsf T}Sy=(A^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}y)>0\), so \(S\) is positive definite. If \(S\delta\lambda=r\) is perturbed to \(S(\delta\lambda+e)=r+d\), then \(\|e\|_2\leq\|S^{-1}\|_2\|d\|_2\). Consequently, a small \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\), or large \(\kappa_2(S)\), makes multiplier recovery and nested elimination sensitive even though the KKT system is structurally nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Schur complement can still amplify multiplier errors severely when its smallest eigenvalue is small or its condition number is large.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Schur Complements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement formula and perturbation bound are standard and fit the failure-boundary leaf, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting the conditioning and nested-elimination interpretation.

children.title: KKT Residual Scaling Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Primal, dual, and complementarity diagnostics measured on incompatible scales.

assumptions_latex: The KKT residual is partitioned into dual, primal, and complementarity blocks.
Each block is measured in a fixed vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unscaled aggregate residual is not invariant under equivalent rescaling of constraints or variables; blockwise normalized residuals are required for comparable stopping tests.
review_flags: scaling convention and authoritative source required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise stopping diagnostics for scaled KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the raw test \(\max\{\|r_d\|,\|r_p\|,\|r_c\|\}\leq\varepsilon\). Replacing an equivalent constraint equation by \(\alpha r_p=0\), with \(\alpha>0\), changes this test although its solution set is unchanged. Define instead \(\widehat r_i=\|r_i\|/s_i\) for \(i\in\{d,p,c\}\), where each \(s_i>0\) reflects the corresponding data and iterate scale. A scale-aware stopping condition is \(\max_i\widehat r_i\leq\varepsilon\). Without compatible normalization, one block can dominate or disappear numerically, causing premature termination or unnecessary inner iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw KKT block norms depend on equation scaling; normalized primal, dual, and complementarity residuals provide a meaningful combined stopping test.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Scaling Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rescaling counterexample is sound, but the asserted normalization requirement depends on how the block scales transform with equivalent equation and variable scalings. An authoritative stopping-criterion source and a precise scaling convention are required.

children.title: Structure Loss under Nested Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximate block actions that invalidate symmetry or feasibility properties.

assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) and \(P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2\) are exact outer operators.
\(\widetilde H\) and \(\widetilde P\) denote their approximate actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent approximate block actions need not preserve symmetry, idempotence, or feasibility, so a symmetric outer Krylov method may no longer be mathematically applicable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic invariants required by nested projected Krylov operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The exact projected operator \(K=PHP\) is symmetric and maps \(\operatorname{range}(P)\) into itself. For nested approximations \(\widetilde K=\widetilde P\widetilde H\widetilde P\), either \(\widetilde H\neq\widetilde H^{\mathsf T}\) or \(\widetilde P
eq\widetilde P^{\mathsf T}\) can yield \(\widetilde K
eq\widetilde K^{\mathsf T}\); moreover, \(\widetilde P^2
eq\widetilde P\) permits feasibility drift. Consequently, conjugate-gradient recurrences and reduced-space invariance are not justified merely because each inner action is accurate in norm. Structure preservation requires compatible adjoint actions and explicit control of \(\|\widetilde P^2-\widetilde P\|\) and \(\|A\widetilde P\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested approximations can destroy symmetry, projection, and feasibility invariants even when individual inner errors are small, invalidating the intended outer solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure Loss under Nested Approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the algebraic risks are plausible, but no source supports the stated structure-preservation requirements or the conclusion about applicability of symmetric outer Krylov recurrences under nested approximations.

children.title: Limited-Memory BFGS
children.top_down_role: Positive-curvature limited-memory family for large-scale smooth models.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two-loop recursion applies the positive-definite limited-memory inverse-BFGS operator using \(O(mn)\) work and \(O(mn)\) storage.
review_flags: authoritative L-BFGS source and exact locator required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-loop inverse-Hessian recursion with curvature-positive stored pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Retain the newest \(\min\{m,k\}\) pairs. Given \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), set \(q=g_k\). In reverse chronological order set \(\alpha_i=\rho_i s_i^{\mathsf T}q\) and \(q\leftarrow q-\alpha_i y_i\). Set \(r=H_k^0q\). In chronological order set \(\beta_i=\rho_i y_i^{\mathsf T}r\) and \(r\leftarrow r+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)\). Return \(p_k=-r\), and stop according to a prescribed gradient test such as \(\|g_k\|\leq\varepsilon\). Positive curvature and \(H_k^0\succ0\) imply that the represented inverse-BFGS operator is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: L-BFGS uses recent curvature pairs and a two-loop recursion to compute a positive-definite quasi-Newton direction without storing a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory BFGS

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-loop recursion, curvature condition, positive-definiteness claim, and complexity bounds are standard and the algorithm kind fits the L-BFGS leaf, but the record supplies no source or locator for this specific algorithm.

children.title: Limited-Memory SR1
children.top_down_role: Indefinite-capable compact curvature family.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory SR1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limited-memory direct SR1 with skipped unstable updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), retain at most \(m\) pairs \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(y_i=\nabla f(x_{i+1})-\nabla f(x_i)\). Starting from a symmetric base \(B_0\), process retained pairs chronologically. For each pair set \(r_i=y_i-B_i s_i\). If \(|r_i^\top s_i|\ge \varepsilon\lVert r_i\rVert\lVert s_i\rVert\), update \[B_{i+1}=B_i+\frac{r_i r_i^\top}{r_i^\top s_i};\] otherwise set \(B_{i+1}=B_i\). Use the resulting, possibly indefinite operator in a safeguarded linear or trust-region solve, and discard the oldest pair when storage exceeds \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store only recent secant pairs, apply stable SR1 rank-one corrections, skip nearly singular denominators, and use safeguards because the model may be indefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and gradients are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{i+1}\) is symmetric and satisfies \(B_{i+1}s_i=y_i\) whenever the SR1 update is accepted.

notation.meaning: direct curvature approximation after processed pairs

Starting from a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), process each retained pair satisfying \(y_i^\top s_i>0\). Define \[B_i^{\mathrm{BFGS}}=B_i-\frac{B_i s_i s_i^\top B_i}{s_i^\top B_i s_i}+\frac{y_i y_i^\top}{y_i^\top s_i},\qquad v_i=\frac{y_i}{y_i^\top s_i}-\frac{B_i s_i}{s_i^\top B_i s_i}.\] For a chosen \(\phi_i\in[0,1]\), set \[B_{i+1}=B_i^{\mathrm{BFGS}}+\phi_i(s_i^\top B_i s_i)v_i v_i^\top.\] Apply the resulting operator through its limited-history representation and delete the oldest pair when the capacity \(m\) is exceeded.

knowledge_statements.title: Memoryless Quasi-Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pair inverse-BFGS model reset to a scaled identity at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current secant pair \((s,y)\) with \(s^\top y>0\), reset the inverse base to \(H_0=\gamma I\), where \(\gamma>0\), rather than retaining earlier pairs. With \(\rho=(s^\top y)^{-1}\), the memoryless inverse-BFGS model is \[H=(I-\rho s y^\top)\gamma I(I-\rho y s^\top)+\rho s s^\top.\] Given the current gradient \(g\), output \(p=-Hg\). The model requires storage only for \(s\), \(y\), and a constant number of vectors; after computing the next pair, replace the old pair completely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memoryless BFGS resets to a scaled identity and applies one inverse update, producing a secant direction with constant-vector storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succ0\), \(Hy=s\), and computing \(p=-Hg\) uses \(O(n)\) arithmetic and storage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Memoryless BFGS Method with Periodic Restart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal-storage inverse-BFGS iteration formed from the identity and the latest displacement-gradient pair, with restart every n iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and choose any \(x_0\). At a restart index set \(H_k=I\); otherwise use the matrix produced below from the preceding pair. Set \(d_k=-H_kg_k\), choose \(\alpha_k\ge 0\) by minimizing \(f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\) accurately enough that, with \(p_k=\alpha_kd_k\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), and \(q_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), one has \(p_k^Tq_k>0\). Between periodic restarts, define
\[
H_{k+1}=I-\frac{q_kp_k^T+p_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}+\left(1+\frac{q_k^Tq_k}{p_k^Tq_k}\right)\frac{p_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}.
\]
After incrementing the iteration index, reset \(H_k=I\) whenever the new index is an integer multiple of \(n\); otherwise continue with the computed matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from any point, take a quasi-Newton direction using the current inverse-metric matrix and perform a nonnegative line search accurate enough to satisfy positive curvature. Form the next inverse metric by applying the inverse-BFGS formula to the identity using only the latest step and gradient difference. Thus the update is memoryless; the identity is restored periodically at iteration indices that are multiples of the dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_{k+1}=I-\frac{q_kp_k^T+p_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}+\left(1+\frac{q_k^Tq_k}{p_k^Tq_k}\right)\frac{p_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\text{ between periodic identity restarts, so each update uses no earlier metric history.}

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Compact Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic compact representation of a direct limited-memory curvature operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a symmetric base operator, let \(\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), and let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\) be symmetric. A direct compact curvature form is \[B=B_0+\Psi M\Psi^\top.\] For every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), its matrix-free product is \[Bv=B_0v+\Psi\bigl(M(\Psi^\top v)\bigr).\] Thus the full \(n\times n\) matrix need not be formed; only applications of \(B_0\), the columns of \(\Psi\), and the small dense matrix \(M\) are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct curvature matrix is represented as a base operator plus a symmetric low-rank correction, enabling products without forming a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=B^\top\), and each product reduces to one base product and dense operations involving dimension \(r\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb{N}\), \(B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\), and \(\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\). Suppose \(B_0\) and \(M\) are nonsingular and define \(B=B_0+\Psi M\Psi^\top\), \(H_0=B_0^{-1}\), and \(K=M^{-1}+\Psi^\top H_0\Psi\). If \(K\) is nonsingular, then \[H=B^{-1}=H_0-H_0\Psi K^{-1}\Psi^\top H_0.\] Consequently, for every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[Hv=H_0v-H_0\Psi\bigl(K^{-1}(\Psi^\top H_0v)\bigr).\] Thus inverse products use base solves with \(B_0\) and a dense solve of order \(r\), without inversion of an \(n\times n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Woodbury converts a direct compact correction into its exact inverse form using base solves and one small dense system, provided the base, correction, and reduced matrices are nonsingular.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb{N}\), \(B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\), and \(\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), with \(B_0\) and \(M\) nonsingular. Whenever \(K\) is nonsingular, \[H=B^{-1}=H_0-H_0\Psi K^{-1}\Psi^\top H_0.\] Inverting this compact inverse form recovers \(B\), and the determinant relation is \[\det(B)=\det(B_0)\det(M)\det(K).\] Thus the direct and inverse compact forms encode the same operator pair through corresponding reduced systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank-Plus-Base Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free curvature model built from an applicable base operator and low-rank correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a symmetric base operator whose products are available without forming a dense matrix. Let \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) and symmetric \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\). The low-rank-plus-base model is \[B=A+UCU^\top.\] It covers scalar, diagonal, sparse, and implicit choices of \(A\). For any \(v\), \[Bv=Av+UC(U^\top v).\] If \(A\) is invertible and \(C^{-1}+U^\top A^{-1}U\) is invertible, inverse products follow from the Woodbury formula using only base solves and an \(r\)-dimensional dense solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature is modeled as an easy base operator plus a low-rank correction, supporting matrix-free products and reduced-dimensional inverse calculations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying \(B\) requires one application of \(A\) and low-rank work; under the stated invertibility conditions, applying \(B^{-1}\) requires only base solves and an \(r\)-dimensional solve.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb{N}\), \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\gamma,\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\). Define \[B=\gamma I_n+UMU^\top,\qquad a=\gamma+\lambda,\qquad K=M^{-1}+a^{-1}U^\top U.\] If \(a\ne0\) and \(M\) and \(K\) are nonsingular, then the unique solution of \((B+\lambda I_n)p=-g\) is \[p=-a^{-1}g+a^{-2}UK^{-1}U^\top g.\] Thus the full-space solve reduces to forming \(U^\top g\), solving the dense \(r\times r\) system with \(K\), and lifting the result through \(U\). When \(r=O(m)\) for a retained history size \(m\), the reduced factorization dimension is independent of \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shifted compact linear system reduces to a dense system on the stored-curvature subspace followed by a lift to the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Base Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible direct and inverse base metrics for limited-memory curvature models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct base metric is a symmetric positive-definite operator \(B_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) used before stored secant corrections are applied. Its inverse base metric is \(H_0=B_0^{-1}\). Admissibility for a matrix-free limited-memory model requires that products \(B_0v\), and inverse applications \(H_0v\) when needed, be computable without forming a dense \(n\times n\) matrix. Scalar identities, positive diagonal operators, sparse positive-definite matrices with available solves, and implicit positive-definite preconditioners are admissible examples. The induced norms are \(\lVert v\rVert_{B_0}=(v^\top B_0v)^{1/2}\) and \(\lVert w\rVert_{H_0}=(w^\top H_0w)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base metric is an efficiently applicable positive-definite operator underlying compact secant corrections; its inverse defines the dual metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_0=B_0^{-1}\succ0\), and both displayed quadratic expressions define norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Metric Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility conditions linking scalar scaling, base metrics, and positive-curvature secant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succ0\) be a fixed reference metric and choose \(B_0=\gamma G\). The scaling is compatible with an inverse base precisely when \(\gamma>0\) and \[H_0=B_0^{-1}=\gamma^{-1}G^{-1}.\] For a secant pair \((s,y)\), the metric-aware least-squares scale fitting \(B_0s\approx y\) is \[\gamma=\frac{s^\top Gy}{s^\top G^2s},\] provided \(s\ne0\). It is positive exactly when \(s^\top Gy>0\). Thus positive definiteness of both bases and reciprocal direct-inverse scaling require a positive fitted scalar; otherwise the pair or scaling rule must be rejected or safeguarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled base metric and its inverse must use reciprocal positive scales; metric-aware secant fitting is admissible only when its numerator is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility holds when \(\gamma>0\), \(H_0=\gamma^{-1}G^{-1}\), and the fitted scale is positive exactly if \(s^\top Gy>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Poor Base-Metric Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies instability caused by an ill-conditioned positive-definite initial inverse metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, with eigenvalues \(0<\lambda_{\min}\leq\lambda_{\max}\), and define the base direction \(p=-H_0g\). Then \(\lambda_{\min}\lVert g\rVert_2\leq\lVert p\rVert_2\leq\lambda_{\max}\lVert g\rVert_2\). Moreover, for eigenvectors \(u_{\min}\) and \(u_{\max}\) of unit norm, \(\lVert H_0u_{\max}\rVert_2/\lVert H_0u_{\min}\rVert_2=\kappa_2(H_0)\). Thus a large \(\kappa_2(H_0)=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}\) permits strongly direction-dependent scaling before any stored curvature correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned base inverse metric can amplify equally sized gradient components by factors differing by its spectral condition number.

children.title: Curvature-Pair Acceptance

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scale-invariant positive-curvature test for admitting a secant pair to limited memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iterate displacement \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and gradient displacement \(y_k=\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)\), fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\). The pair \((s_k,y_k)\) is accepted when \[s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\geq \eta\lVert s_k\rVert_2\lVert y_k\rVert_2>0.\] This predicate ensures that both vectors are nonzero and that their angle has cosine at least \(\eta\); in particular, the positive-curvature denominator required by BFGS-type updates is bounded away from zero relative to the pair norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a pair when its curvature is positive and sufficiently large relative to the product of the displacement norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\)

children.title: Curvature-Pair Damping

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Damping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell-type damping enforces positive curvature relative to the current direct metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), a nonzero \(s_k\), a vector \(y_k\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \[\theta_k=\begin{cases}1,&s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\geq\eta s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k,\\(1-\eta)s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k/(s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k-s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k),&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] and \(\widetilde y_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k\). Store \((s_k,\widetilde y_k)\) in place of \((s_k,y_k)\). The resulting pair satisfies \(s_k^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y_k\geq\eta s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend the observed gradient change with the metric prediction so the stored pair has uniformly positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k^{\mathsf T}\widetilde y_k\geq\eta s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k>0\)

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Skipping

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H_k\) be the ordered history of at most \(m\) stored curvature pairs, and let \((s_k,y_k)\) be a candidate pair. If \(A(s_k,y_k)\) is false, set \(\mathcal H_{k+1}=\mathcal H_k\) and construct the next curvature operator from that unchanged history and the selected base metric. If the predicate is true, append the pair and, when necessary, apply the designated capacity policy. The skipping branch performs no secant update using \((s_k,y_k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Aggressiveness Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders normalized-curvature safeguards by their acceptance thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\), define \(A_{\eta}=\{(s,y):s^{\mathsf T}y\geq\eta\lVert s\rVert_2\lVert y\rVert_2>0\}\). Then \[A_{\eta_2}\subseteq A_{\eta_1}.\] Hence increasing the threshold can never increase the set of undamped accepted pairs: it weakly increases skipping or damping decisions while guaranteeing the stronger normalized-curvature lower bound \(s^{\mathsf T}y/(\lVert s\rVert_2\lVert y\rVert_2)\geq\eta_2\) for every pair accepted without modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher normalized-curvature threshold accepts fewer raw pairs but gives every accepted pair a stronger curvature margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_{\eta_2}\subseteq A_{\eta_1}\)

children.title: Persistent Pair Rejection
children.top_down_role: Regimes where repeated safeguard activation prevents useful curvature accumulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Pair Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent safeguard failure can eliminate all recent curvature information under finite-age retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every candidate pair generated at iterations \(k\geq K\) fails the acceptance predicate. If the history policy deletes every stored pair after at most \(m\) subsequent iterations and never inserts rejected pairs, then \(\mathcal H_k=\varnothing\) for every \(k\geq K+m\). Consequently, from iteration \(K+m\) onward, the limited-memory operator equals its base metric until a pair is accepted. Thus persistent rejection removes the secant corrections rather than merely delaying one update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all new pairs are rejected and old pairs expire, the limited-memory operator eventually reduces to its base metric.
assumptions_latex: each stored pair expires within \(m\) iterations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\geq K+m\Rightarrow\mathcal H_k=\varnothing\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-age history and skipped insertion imply finite-time history exhaustion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-time exhaustion claim is correct under the explicitly assumed finite-age deletion policy and fits a failure-boundary container. The retention model and its limited-memory interpretation have no cited source.

children.title: Curvature-History Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Policies for retaining, replacing, aggregating, and discarding stored information.

children.title: History Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing which stored curvature information remains active.

knowledge_statements.title: History Retention Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bounded FIFO policy retains the most recent accepted curvature pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a capacity \(m\geq1\) and initialize \(\mathcal H_0=()\). At iteration \(k\), leave the history unchanged if no pair is accepted. If \((s_k,y_k)\) is accepted, append it to obtain \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{k+1}=\mathcal H_k\mathbin{\|}((s_k,y_k))\), and set \(\mathcal H_{k+1}\) equal to the last \(\min\{m,|\widehat{\mathcal H}_{k+1}|\}\) entries of \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{k+1}\). Output \(\mathcal H_{k+1}\); therefore \(|\mathcal H_{k+1}|\leq m\) and accepted pairs are ordered by recency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FIFO retention stores at most the most recent m accepted curvature pairs, preserving their chronological order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal H_{k+1}|\leq m\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical bounded FIFO limited-memory policy
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded FIFO procedure is well defined, preserves chronological order, and has the correct algorithm content kind. It lacks an authoritative limited-memory source with a specific locator.

children.title: History Replacement Policies
children.top_down_role: Structures for replacing stored information under limited-memory budgets.

assumptions_latex: ties use a fixed deterministic rule
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal H_{k+1}|\leq m\)

notation.meaning: retention score of stored pair i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract score-based bounded replacement policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based replacement preserves a fixed history capacity while admitting a selected new pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H_k=((s_i,y_i))_{i\in I_k}\) be a history with \(|I_k|\leq m\), where \(m\geq1\), and let \(q_i\in\mathbb{R}\) be a prescribed retention score for each stored pair. Given an accepted candidate \((s_k,y_k)\), if \(|I_k|<m\), append the candidate at the newest position. If \(|I_k|=m\), choose \(j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in I_k}q_i\), delete \((s_j,y_j)\), and insert \((s_k,y_k)\) at the newest position. Resolve ties by a fixed deterministic rule. The resulting history is well defined and has size at most \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Append an accepted pair when capacity remains; at capacity, replace a stored pair having minimal prescribed retention score, using a deterministic tie rule.

children.title: Curvature-Pair Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Compressed representations formed from multiple stored curvature pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Pair Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear aggregation preserves exact secant relations on the aggregated displacement subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), and suppose a linear curvature operator \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfies \(BS=Y\). For any aggregation matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times q}\), define \(\bar S=SA\) and \(\bar Y=YA\). Then \(B\bar S=\bar Y\). Consequently, replacing the original pairs by the columns of \((\bar S,\bar Y)\) preserves their combined secant equations, although information outside \(\operatorname{range}(A)\) may be lost when \(q<r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear combinations of exact secant pairs remain exact secant pairs for the same curvature operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(SA)=YA\)

notation.meaning: matrices of stored displacement and gradient-change columns

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linearity of simultaneous secant equations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear secant-preservation identity is correct and property accurately describes its mathematical role. It does not by itself specify a practical pair-aggregation method, and no source supports its placement as limited-memory history aggregation.

children.title: History Discarding Policies
children.top_down_role: Boundaries for removing stale, redundant, or unreliable stored information.

knowledge_statements.title: History Discarding Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate-based deletion removes stored pairs that have become stale or numerically unsuitable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k(s_i,y_i)\) be a prescribed Boolean discard predicate, possibly depending on pair age, normalized curvature, or finite-value checks. Given an ordered history \(\mathcal H_k=((s_i,y_i))_{i\in I_k}\), define \[\mathcal H_{k+1}^{-}=((s_i,y_i))_{i\in I_k:\,\neg D_k(s_i,y_i)},\] preserving the relative order of surviving pairs. Apply any subsequent accepted-pair insertion to \(\mathcal H_{k+1}^{-}\). The deletion stage satisfies \(|\mathcal H_{k+1}^{-}|\leq|\mathcal H_k|\) and contains no pair for which \(D_k\) is true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete every stored pair satisfying a fixed staleness or numerical-quality predicate, while preserving survivor order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathcal H_{k+1}^{-}\Longleftrightarrow (s_i,y_i)\in\mathcal H_k\text{ and }\neg D_k(s_i,y_i)\)

notation.meaning: history after deletion and before insertion

children.title: Limited-Memory Matrix-Free Roles
children.top_down_role: Uses of compact curvature operators that remain within this chapter's inner-solver boundary.

children.title: Limited-Memory Krylov Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Compact secant operators used to accelerate Newton and KKT inner solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Krylov Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an SPD limited-memory inverse-curvature operator as a matrix-free Krylov preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To solve \(Az=b\) with \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), choose a symmetric positive-definite limited-memory operator \(M_k^{-1}\) represented by a base metric and stored curvature pairs. In preconditioned conjugate gradients, initialize \(z_0\), set \(r_0=b-Az_0\), compute \(v_0=M_k^{-1}r_0\) by the compact recursion, and use \(d_0=v_0\). At every Krylov iteration apply \(A\) only through a matrix-vector product and replace each residual \(r_j\) by its preconditioned vector \(v_j=M_k^{-1}r_j\). Stop when \(\lVert r_j\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\), returning \(z_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a positive-definite limited-memory inverse operator to Krylov residuals without forming either the system matrix or preconditioner densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert b-Az_j\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\) at termination
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard left-preconditioned conjugate-gradient recurrence with an SPD compact quasi-Newton operator

children.title: Limited-Memory Trust-Region Models
children.top_down_role: Compact curvature operators used in large-scale restricted-step subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic trust-region model whose curvature products use a compact limited-memory operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(g_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) be represented by a base metric plus at most \(m\) stored curvature pairs. The limited-memory trust-region step is any global or prescribed approximate solution of \[\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;q_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp\quad\text{subject to}\quad\lVert p\rVert_2\leq\Delta_k.\] Matrix-free subproblem methods evaluate \(B_kv\) through the compact representation and need not form a dense \(n\times n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust-region model uses a compact limited-memory curvature operator and restricts the trial step to a norm ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lVert p\rVert_2\leq\Delta_k}q_k(p)\) for an exact solve

source_refs.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic trust-region representation is standard and fits the terminal topic, but the cited basic trust-region section does not explicitly support the limited-memory compact representation or matrix-free product claim. A source specific to limited-memory trust-region models is required.

children.title: Reduced-Space Limited-Memory Curvature
children.top_down_role: Secant information represented or applied within feasible-direction spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Limited-Memory Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected secant representation on a fixed feasible-direction subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(Z^{T}Z=I_r\), and let stored pairs \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) obey \(Z^{T}s_i\neq0\). Define \(\widehat s_i=Z^{T}s_i\) and \(\widehat y_i=Z^{T}y_i\). A reduced limited-memory curvature operator is any \(\widehat B:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^r\) obtained by applying a specified secant update to the retained pairs and satisfying \(\widehat B\widehat s_i=\widehat y_i\) for every enforced pair. Its full-space feasible-direction action is \(v\mapsto Z\widehat BZ^{T}v\); hence neither \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) nor its factorization need be formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project stored secant pairs into the feasible-direction basis, build curvature there, and lift its action back without forming a full Hessian approximation.
assumptions_latex: The feasible-direction subspace is fixed while the retained update is formed.
The chosen secant update is well-defined for the projected pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{\mathrm{red}}v=Z\widehat BZ^{T}v\) and \(\widehat B\widehat s_i=\widehat y_i\) for each enforced pair.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the feasible-direction subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and reduced-space context fit the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. An authoritative locator is also needed to delimit when a specified limited-memory update can enforce multiple projected secant equations simultaneously.

children.title: Subspace Enrichment by Curvature History
children.top_down_role: Stored displacements and curvature information used to enrich restricted Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Enrichment by Curvature History
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-augmented restricted Newton or trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current trial subspace basis \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), retained pairs \((s_i,y_i)\), a gradient \(g_k\), and an operator \(H_kv\), form \(W_k=[V_k,s_{i_1},\ldots,s_{i_p},y_{i_1},\ldots,y_{i_p}]\). Remove dependent columns and orthonormalize to obtain \(Q_k\). Compute \(z_k\) from the restricted model \[\min_{\|Q_kz\|\leq\Delta_k}\; g_k^{T}Q_kz+\tfrac12 z^{T}(Q_k^{T}H_kQ_k)z.\] Output \(p_k=Q_kz_k\), stopping the enrichment when no retained column has orthogonal residual exceeding a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add independent stored displacement and curvature vectors to the trial subspace, then solve the Newton or trust-region model in the enriched basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\operatorname{span}(V_k,\{s_i,y_i\}_{i\in I_k})\) and \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
