children.title: Limited-Memory Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which compact histories become unrepresentative, unstable, or incompatible with solver geometry.

children.title: Insufficient Curvature Diversity
children.top_down_role: Histories failing to represent important spectral directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Curvature Diversity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficient history cannot determine curvature outside sampled directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=[s_1,\ldots,s_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(S)=r<n\), and suppose an approximation is constructed solely from \((S,Y)\) and a fixed baseline \(B_0\). For any nonzero \(u\in\ker(S^{T})\), the symmetric matrices \(H\) and \(H+\alpha uu^{T}\) produce identical sampled products whenever \(Y=HS\), because \((H+\alpha uu^{T})S=HS\). Thus the history cannot identify curvature along \(u\); arbitrarily large or sign-changing curvature may remain invisible as \(\alpha\) varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If stored displacements span too few directions, the same history is compatible with arbitrarily different curvature on their orthogonal complement.
assumptions_latex: Only the sampled products \(Y=HS\) and a fixed baseline are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist distinct symmetric operators consistent with the same history but having different curvature on \(\ker(S^{T})\).

notation.meaning: Unrepresented direction orthogonal to the stored displacements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and identifiability statement fit the leaf and are mathematically coherent, but the record has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Definiteness Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Conflict between nonconvex curvature and updates designed to preserve positive curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Definiteness Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite secant updates suppress sampled negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a symmetric secant update constrained to remain positive definite. If a nonconvex model supplies a pair \((s,y)\) with \(s^{T}y\leq0\), no positive-definite matrix \(B\) can satisfy \(Bs=y\), since positive definiteness would require \(s^{T}Bs>0\). Therefore an update that preserves positive definiteness must reject, damp, or alter this pair and cannot simultaneously reproduce its nonpositive directional curvature. Such an approximation is unsuitable as an exact representation of negative curvature in the sampled direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite update cannot satisfy a secant pair with nonpositive curvature, so damping or rejection necessarily hides that negative-curvature evidence.
assumptions_latex: The update requires \(B\) to be symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No admissible \(B\) satisfies \(Bs=y\).

source_refs.locator: 9.3 Second Order Conditions p. 207

source_witnesses.locator: 9.3 Second Order Conditions p. 207

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary statement is mathematically correct and matches the definiteness-mismatch leaf, but the cited locator on second-order conditions does not specifically substantiate the positive-definite secant incompatibility or its update consequences.

children.title: Stale or Noisy Curvature History
children.top_down_role: History degradation under rapidly changing, noisy, active-set, or barrier models.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale or Noisy Curvature History
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant errors quantify degradation from model drift or noisy gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current symmetric curvature operator \(H_k\), define the defect of a retained pair by \(e_i=y_i-H_ks_i\). If \(y_i=H_is_i+\eta_i\), then \(e_i=(H_i-H_k)s_i+\eta_i\). Consequently, even an exact historical pair becomes stale when \(H_i\neq H_k\), while gradient noise contributes \(\eta_i\). If \(\|e_i\|>\tau(\|y_i\|+\|H_ks_i\|)\) for a prescribed \(\tau>0\), enforcing the pair imposes a relative secant inconsistency exceeding \(\tau\); the pair should not be treated as reliable current-curvature information without filtering or resetting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model drift and noise create a measurable secant defect; a history pair exceeding the chosen relative tolerance is unreliable for current curvature.
assumptions_latex: A current product \(H_ks_i\) can be evaluated or estimated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_i=(H_i-H_k)s_i+\eta_i\), with unreliability declared when \(\|e_i\|>\tau(\|y_i\|+\|H_ks_i\|)\).

notation.meaning: Error in the stored curvature observation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The defect identity is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the relative rejection threshold and the resulting reliability classification are algorithmic conventions requiring a noisy or nonstationary quasi-Newton source.

children.title: Compact-System Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Dependence and scaling failures within stored-history reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-System Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearly dependent or poorly scaled history destabilizes compact reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a limited-memory action require solving \(Mz=b\), where \(M\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) is the compact history matrix. If \(M\) is nonsingular, perturbations satisfy to first order \(\|\delta z\|/\|z\|\lesssim\kappa_2(M)(\|\delta M\|_2/\|M\|_2+\|\delta b\|/\|b\|)\). Thus nearly dependent stored vectors or extreme pair scaling that makes \(\sigma_{\min}(M)\) small can amplify data and rounding errors. At \(\sigma_{\min}(M)=0\), the compact formula is undefined without dropping pairs, regularizing, or using a pseudoinverse convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependence or bad scaling can make the compact history solve highly sensitive; singular compact systems require pair removal, regularization, or a pseudoinverse.
assumptions_latex: The limited-memory formula contains a compact linear solve \(Mz=b\).
Perturbations are sufficiently small for first-order conditioning analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sensitivity is governed by \(\kappa_2(M)=\sigma_{\max}(M)/\sigma_{\min}(M)\), and the ordinary solve fails when \(\sigma_{\min}(M)=0\).

notation.meaning: Compact matrix assembled from stored history.
Spectral condition number of the compact system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditioning statement fits the compact-system failure leaf and correctly distinguishes nonsingular sensitivity from singular failure, but no source with a compact limited-memory formula and conditioning locator is supplied.

children.title: Operator-Evaluation Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted oracle count for a matrix-free solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a run performs \(N_r\) residual evaluations, \(N_d\) derivative-vector or adjoint-vector evaluations, and \(N_c\) curvature-vector evaluations. In an operator-oracle model with respective costs \(c_r,c_d,c_c\), its operator-evaluation work is \[W_{\mathrm{op}}=c_rN_r+c_dN_d+c_cN_c.\] If each cost is bounded above by \(\bar c_r,\bar c_d,\bar c_c\), then \(W_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\bar c_rN_r+\bar c_dN_d+\bar c_cN_c\). Vector arithmetic, orthogonalization, communication, and preconditioner setup are excluded unless separately included in an oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free work is the weighted count of residual, derivative-product, and curvature-product calls, with other costs reported separately.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle-call category has an assigned nonnegative cost.
The accounting interval and inclusion rules are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{op}}=c_rN_r+c_dN_d+c_cN_c\).

notation.meaning: Counts of residual, derivative-product, and curvature-product evaluations.

children.title: Inner–Outer Work Complexity
children.top_down_role: Nested accounting relating nonlinear progress to Krylov and preconditioner effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner–Outer Work Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nested work identity with uniform per-iteration bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an outer nonlinear method take \(K\) iterations. At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k\) be the number of inner Krylov steps, \(a_k\) the outer-only work, and \(b_{k,j}\) the work of inner step \(j\), including its operator and preconditioner applications. Then \[W=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(a_k+\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}b_{k,j}\right).\] If \(a_k\leq\bar a\), \(b_{k,j}\leq\bar b\), and \(m_k\leq\bar m\), then \(W\leq K(\bar a+\bar m\bar b)\). This is a work bound, not an iteration bound, unless \(K\) and \(\bar m\) are themselves controlled by convergence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total nested work sums outer overhead and every inner Krylov step; uniform bounds yield the product-type upper bound shown.
assumptions_latex: The outer method terminates after \(K<\infty\) iterations.
All included work categories are counted exactly once.
Uniform bounds \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar m\) hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\leq K(\bar a+\bar m\bar b)\).

notation.meaning: Inner Krylov steps at outer iteration k.

children.title: Krylov-Basis Storage Complexity
children.top_down_role: Storage growth associated with active Krylov basis representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov-Basis Storage Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-vector storage for unrestarted and restarted Krylov bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vectors in \(\mathbb R^n\), explicitly storing \(m\) Krylov basis vectors requires \(nm\) scalar words. If an orthogonalization method also stores at most \(c\) additional length-\(n\) work vectors and an \(m\times m\) projected matrix, total storage is at most \(n(m+c)+m^2\) words. Hence storage is \(O(nm+m^2)\), and it is \(O(nm)\) when \(m\leq n\). Restarting with maximum basis dimension \(m_{\max}\) replaces \(m\) by \(m_{\max}\), independently of the total number of Krylov steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit m-vector Krylov basis uses nm words; work vectors and the projected matrix give total storage of order nm plus m squared.
assumptions_latex: Basis and work vectors are stored densely in \(\mathbb R^n\).
At most \(c\) auxiliary full-length vectors are live.
The projected matrix is stored densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{Krylov}}\leq n(m+c)+m^2=O(nm+m^2)\).

notation.meaning: Constant number of auxiliary full-length vectors.

children.title: Recycled-Subspace Storage Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Recycled-Subspace Storage Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage of a retained dense recycling basis and projected data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) contain \(r\) retained recycling vectors. Storing \(U\) densely costs \(nr\) scalar words. If the method additionally retains one operator image per vector, \(AU\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and dense projected data of size at most \(r\times r\), its recycling state costs at most \(2nr+r^2+O(r)\) words. Without cached operator images the bound is \(nr+r^2+O(r)\). Thus fixed-rank recycling adds \(O(nr+r^2)\) storage beyond the active Krylov state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r recycled subspace costs order nr words, doubled when operator images are cached, plus order r squared projected data.
assumptions_latex: Recycling vectors are dense elements of \(\mathbb R^n\).
At most one length-\(n\) operator image is cached per retained vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{recycle}}\leq2nr+r^2+O(r)=O(nr+r^2)\).

notation.meaning: Cached operator images of the recycling basis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated dense storage accounting fits the recycled-subspace storage leaf, but no authoritative recycling-method source with a storage or data-structure locator is supplied.

children.title: Sketch Storage Complexity
children.top_down_role: Storage requirements for randomized or compressed subspace representations.

assumptions_latex: The sketch dimension is \(s\) and the ambient dimension is \(n\).
Scalar words are the storage unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{dense}}=O(s(n+q))\), whereas seeded implicit storage is \(O(sq)\) apart from metadata.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit storage for dense or structured matrix-free sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sketching map \(\Omega:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^s\), storing an explicit dense matrix \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\) requires \(sn\) scalar words, while storing \(q\) sketched vectors requires an additional \(sq\) words. Thus explicit-sketch storage is \(sn+sq+O(s)=O(s(n+q))\). If \(\Omega\) is generated reproducibly from an \(O(1)\)-word seed or a structured transform with \(O(n+s)\) parameters, the matrix term falls respectively to \(O(1)\) or \(O(n+s)\), but the \(sq\) stored sketch values remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense s-by-n sketch costs sn words, while implicit generation removes that matrix cost but not storage of the sketched vectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Storage Complexity

children.title: Curvature-History Storage Complexity
children.top_down_role: Memory costs associated with reduced-memory curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-History Storage Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage for limited-memory secant pairs and compact coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Retaining \(m\) displacement-curvature pairs \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) requires \(2nm\) scalar words. If a compact limited-memory representation also stores dense \(m\times m\) inner-product or factor data and \(O(m)\) coefficients, then total history storage is \[S_{\mathrm{hist}}=2nm+O(m^2).\] When \(m\leq n\), this is \(O(nm)\). A circular buffer changes neither bound; storing only one member of each pair is valid only when the other can be regenerated and changes the vector term accordingly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Storing m secant pairs costs 2nm words, with compact coefficients adding order m squared; fixed memory therefore scales linearly with dimension.
assumptions_latex: Each retained pair contains two dense vectors in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{hist}}=2nm+O(m^2)=O(nm)\) when \(m\leq n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and dense word count fit the curvature-history storage leaf, but no authoritative limited-memory secant source with a storage or compact-representation locator is supplied.

children.title: Point-to-Point Communication Costs
children.top_down_role: Data-transfer costs between participating processes or devices.

knowledge_statements.title: Point-to-Point Communication Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path latency–bandwidth accounting for direct messages in a distributed matrix-free iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the latency–bandwidth model, suppose the critical path of one iteration contains \(m\) point-to-point messages carrying a total of \(w\) words. If initiating a message costs \(\alpha\) time units and transmitting one word costs \(\beta\), then its point-to-point communication time is bounded by \[T_{\mathrm{p2p}}\le m\alpha+w\beta.\] Concurrent messages contribute only through the critical path; messages serialized by data dependence contribute additively. Thus a work certificate records both \(m\) and \(w\), since word volume alone does not capture latency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Point-to-point time is bounded by message count times latency plus critical-path word volume times inverse bandwidth.
assumptions_latex: The counted messages and words lie on the iteration's communication critical path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{p2p}}\le m\alpha+w\beta\).

notation.meaning: Total words carried by those messages.

children.title: Global Reduction Costs
children.top_down_role: Synchronization costs induced by collective scalar reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Reduction Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-based cost model for scalar or short-vector collective reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge2\) processes perform an all-reduction of \(q\) words using a balanced binary reduction tree followed, if required, by a broadcast tree. Each tree has \(L=\lceil\log_2 p\rceil\) communication levels. Under the latency–bandwidth model, one reduction tree costs at most \(L(\alpha+q\beta)\); an all-reduction implemented by reduction plus broadcast costs at most \[T_{\mathrm{allred}}\le2L(\alpha+q\beta).\] Consequently, \(r\) sequential all-reductions incur \(2rL\) synchronization levels and cannot generally be charged only by total word volume.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree all-reduction has logarithmic synchronization depth; sequential reductions multiply that latency cost even when each payload is small.
assumptions_latex: Communication levels are serialized, while transfers within one level proceed concurrently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{allred}}\le2\lceil\log_2p\rceil(\alpha+q\beta)\).

notation.meaning: Depth of the balanced binary tree.

children.title: Basis-Management Data Movement
children.top_down_role: Traffic associated with storing, accessing, or redistributing basis information.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Management Data Movement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data-volume accounting for storing, redistributing, and restarting distributed Krylov bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a Krylov basis contain \(k\) vectors of global length \(n\), distributed without replication. Storing the basis requires \(kn\) scalar words globally. Any redistribution or checkpoint that transfers every stored coefficient once moves \(kn\) words; retaining only \(k_r\le k\) vectors at restart moves at most \(k_rn\) words. Under a per-process balanced distribution, the corresponding local volumes are at most \(kn/p\) and \(k_rn/p\), up to rounding. These volumes exclude reductions used to form inner products and therefore must be reported separately from synchronization costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed basis of k length-n vectors stores kn words; full redistribution moves kn words, while restart movement scales with retained vectors.
assumptions_latex: Basis coefficients are distributed without replication and transferred at most once in the counted operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{store}}=kn\) and \(W_{\mathrm{restart}}\le k_rn\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the input vector among \(p\) processes. In one distributed operator application, let process \(i\) send \(h_i\) scalar words in \(d_i\) point-to-point messages. Counting sender-side traffic, the aggregate network volume and communication critical-path time satisfy \[W_{\mathrm{op}}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}h_i,\qquad T_{\mathrm{op}}\le\max_{1\le i\le p}(d_i\alpha+h_i\beta),\] when each process serializes its own messages, distinct processes communicate concurrently, and contention is neglected. If communication overlaps perfectly with local computation of duration \(T_{\mathrm{loc}}\), the combined exposed time is at most \(\max\{T_{\mathrm{loc}},T_{\mathrm{op}}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using sender-side accounting, operator traffic is the sum of words sent, while the communication critical path is bounded by the largest per-process latency-bandwidth cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\) for \(s\in\mathbb R^n\). An inner-solve status certificate reports a step \(s\), its residual \(r=Hs+g\), and at least one applicable condition: approximate stationarity, \(\|r\|\le\eta\|g\|\); negative curvature, witnessed by a vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \(d^THd\le-\gamma\|d\|^2\); or a model-decreasing trust-region boundary step satisfying \(\|s\|=\Delta\) and \(q(s)<q(0)\). Each condition certifies only its named status and is checkable using operator actions, inner products, and norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve can report directly checkable evidence of a small residual, a negative-curvature direction, or a model-decreasing trust-region boundary step; each condition certifies only the corresponding status.

children.top_down_role: Nonlinear residual, stationarity, and globalization diagnostics.

notation.meaning: Outer-iteration model expressed in step coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(x_k,s_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] For tolerances \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\) and \(0<\eta<1\), an outer-progress certificate reports the positive predicted reduction and either stationarity, \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_g\), or an accepted trial, \(\rho_k\ge\eta\). An accepted trial certifies actual decrease of at least \(\eta[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer progress is certified by a gradient norm below a nonnegative tolerance or by an accepted trial whose actual decrease is at least the stated fraction of its positive predicted decrease.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) over \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\). For multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\), define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\) and \[r_{\mathrm{stat}}=\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\|_\infty,\quad r_{\mathrm{eq}}=\|c(x)\|_\infty,\quad r_{\mathrm{ineq}}=\|[g(x)]_+\|_\infty,\] \[r_{\mathrm{dual}}=\|[-\mu]_+\|_\infty,\qquad r_{\mathrm{comp}}=\|\mu\odot g(x)\|_\infty.\] The tuple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) is a componentwise approximate KKT certificate when \(r_j\le\varepsilon_j\) for each \(j\in\{\mathrm{stat},\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{ineq},\mathrm{dual},\mathrm{comp}\}\), with every \(\varepsilon_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate KKT status is certified by separately specified nonnegative bounds on stationarity, equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity residuals.

children.title: Operator-Product Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Fidelity regimes for matrix-free derivative or linear-operator products.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Product Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform relative error condition for an inexact matrix-free linear operator action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear and let \(\widetilde H\) denote the implemented matrix-free action on a specified subspace \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). The action has operator-product accuracy \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\) on \(S\) when \[\|(\widetilde H-H)v\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|\qquad\text{for every }v\in S.\] Equivalently, the induced norm of the restricted error is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\). An absolute-error variant replaces the right side by a fixed \(\delta_{\mathrm{op}}\), but the two conventions must not be interchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate operator action is accurate on a subspace when every product error is bounded proportionally to the input norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{v\in S\setminus\{0\}}\|(\widetilde H-H)v\|/\|v\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\).

notation.meaning: Subspace on which accuracy is required.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: induced-norm definition of operator perturbation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The induced-norm condition is mathematically precise and condition is the correct role for this leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The standard-field rationale supports candidate retention but not source-backed review acceptance.

children.title: Linear-Solve Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Attainable accuracy regimes for inner iterative solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Solve Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative residual condition for an inexact matrix-free linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the linear system \(Hs=b\), an approximate solution \(\widetilde s\) has relative residual accuracy \(\eta\) when the exact-operator residual \[r=b-H\widetilde s\] satisfies \(\|r\|\le\eta\|b\|\). If only an implemented action \(\widetilde H\) is available, the computable residual \(\widetilde r=b-\widetilde H\widetilde s\) defines implemented-residual accuracy \(\|\widetilde r\|\le\eta\|b\|\); this condition alone does not imply the exact-operator residual bound unless the product error is also controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-solve accuracy is a relative residual bound; a residual formed with an inexact operator needs a separate product-error allowance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact residual accuracy is \(\|b-H\widetilde s\|\le\eta\|b\|\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H,\widetilde H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and let \(\widetilde s\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(\widetilde r=b-\widetilde H\widetilde s\). Suppose \(\|\widetilde r\|\le\eta\|b\|\) and \(\|(\widetilde H-H)\widetilde s\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\|\widetilde s\|\). Then \[\|b-H\widetilde s\|\le\eta\|b\|+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\|\widetilde s\|.\] For any \(\theta\ge0\), the compatibility condition \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\|\widetilde s\|\le\theta\eta\|b\|\) guarantees \(\|b-H\widetilde s\|\le(1+\theta)\eta\|b\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly defined exact and implemented operators, product error is compatible with the solve tolerance when its contribution at the computed step is bounded by a chosen fraction of the implemented residual budget.

children.title: Fidelity-Limited Stopping Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where operator uncertainty limits meaningful inner-solve refinement.

assumptions_latex: \(H,\widetilde H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) are linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and \(s\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\eta,\tau\ge0\), \(\delta(s)\ge0\), and no information beyond the displayed residual and product-error bounds is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\delta(s)>\tau\|b\|\), no \(\eta\ge0\) can certify \(\|b-Hs\|\le\tau\|b\|\) from the displayed bounds; equality requires \(\eta=0\).

notation.meaning: Exact and implemented linear operator actions.
Certified error allowance for the implemented operator action at the computed step.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consequence of the residual perturbation inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual targets below the certified operator-error floor cannot be guaranteed from implemented-residual control alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H,\widetilde H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and let \(s\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(\widetilde r=b-\widetilde Hs\), and suppose only \(\|\widetilde r\|\le\eta\|b\|\) and \(\|(\widetilde H-H)s\|\le\delta(s)\) are known. The available bounds certify only \[\|b-Hs\|\le\eta\|b\|+\delta(s).\] Therefore a target \(\|b-Hs\|\le\tau\|b\|\) is guaranteed by these bounds only when \(\eta\|b\|+\delta(s)\le\tau\|b\|\). If \(\delta(s)>\tau\|b\|\), no nonnegative \(\eta\) can provide the guarantee; if \(\delta(s)=\tau\|b\|\), the displayed bounds provide it only when \(\eta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening the implemented solve tolerance cannot certify an exact residual target strictly below the operator-error allowance; equality leaves no positive residual budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Fidelity-Limited Stopping Boundaries

children.title: Nested Schur-Solve Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy coupling between block inversions and outer reduced-system convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Schur-Solve Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient residual-budget coupling for an inexact block elimination and an outer Schur solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Ax+B^{\mathsf T}y=f\) and \(Bx-Cy=h\), where \(A\) is nonsingular, and define \(S=C+BA^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\) and \(b=BA^{-1}f-h\). Suppose approximate applications satisfy \(\|\widehat A^{-1}v-A^{-1}v\|\leq\eta_A\|v\|\), producing \(\widehat S=C+B\widehat A^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\widehat b=B\widehat A^{-1}f-h\). If \(\|\widehat b-\widehat S\widehat y\|\leq\eta_S\), then the exact reduced residual obeys \[\|b-S\widehat y\|\leq\eta_S+\|B\|\eta_A\bigl(\|f\|+\|B^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\|\bigr).\] Thus an outer tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is guaranteed whenever the right-hand side does not exceed \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Schur residual budget must cover both the iterative reduced solve error and errors from approximate block inversions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonsingular and all norms are compatible induced norms.
The approximate inverse has uniform error at most \(\eta_A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|b-S\widehat y\|\leq\eta_S+\|B\|\eta_A(\|f\|+\|B^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\|)\).

notation.meaning: Schur operator formed with approximate block solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normwise Schur-residual bound is algebraically plausible and fits the condition container, but no cited source supports the uniform approximate-inverse model or this exact coupling formula.

children.title: Inner-Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Quality regimes for inexact local models produced by nested solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy condition for a computed matrix-free quadratic model and its predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(s)=f_0+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\) be an exact local model and \(\widetilde m\) its computed counterpart on \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta\}\). For a trial step \(s\), define \(p=m(0)-m(s)>0\) and \(\widetilde p=\widetilde m(0)-\widetilde m(s)\). The inner model has relative accuracy \(\eta_m\in[0,1)\) at \(s\) when \[|\widetilde m(0)-m(0)|+|\widetilde m(s)-m(s)|\leq\eta_m p.\] Consequently, \(|\widetilde p-p|\leq\eta_m p\) and \((1-\eta_m)p\leq\widetilde p\leq(1+\eta_m)p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors in the computed model at the base and trial points must be a controlled fraction of the exact predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is quadratic on the trust region.
The selected step has positive exact predicted reduction \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde p-p|\leq\eta_m p\) and \((1-\eta_m)p\leq\widetilde p\leq(1+\eta_m)p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and its predicted-reduction bounds are internally consistent, but the particular relative-error normalization has no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Globalization-Decision Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Reliability regimes for outer acceptance or rejection decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Globalization-Decision Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A margin certificate ensuring that inexact trust-region ratio evaluation preserves an accept-or-reject decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=f(x)-f(x+s)\), \(p=m(0)-m(s)>0\), and \(\rho=a/p\). Let computed quantities satisfy \(|\widetilde a-a|\leq\epsilon_a\), \(|\widetilde p-p|\leq\epsilon_p<p\), with \(\widetilde\rho=\widetilde a/\widetilde p\). Then \[|\widetilde\rho-\rho|\leq\delta_\rho:=\frac{\epsilon_a+|\rho|\epsilon_p}{p-\epsilon_p}.\] For an acceptance threshold \(\tau\), the computed decision is certified correct if \(|\widetilde\rho-\tau|>\delta_\rho\): accept when \(\widetilde\rho>\tau+\delta_\rho\), and reject when \(\widetilde\rho<\tau-\delta_\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed ratio gives a reliable globalization decision only when its distance from the threshold exceeds the certified ratio error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde\rho-\tau|>\delta_\rho\) certifies that exact and computed threshold decisions agree.

notation.meaning: Exact and computed actual-to-predicted reduction ratios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio-error calculation and margin certificate fit the certificate container, but no source supports the exact hypotheses and bound.

children.title: Model-to-Acceptance Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Relationships between inner model quality and outer decision reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-to-Acceptance Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint error budget making model accuracy compatible with a ratio-based acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=f(x)-f(x+s)\), \(p=m(0)-m(s)>0\), and \(\rho=a/p\). Suppose computed reductions satisfy \(|\widetilde a-a|\leq\epsilon_a\) and \(|\widetilde p-p|\leq\epsilon_p<p\). For a threshold \(\tau\), model and evaluation accuracies are compatible with the exact acceptance decision whenever \[\epsilon_a+(|\tau|+\gamma)\epsilon_p<\gamma p,\qquad \gamma:=|\rho-\tau|.\] Under this strict inequality, \(\widetilde\rho=\widetilde a/\widetilde p\) lies on the same side of \(\tau\) as \(\rho\); hence model error cannot reverse the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combined actual- and predicted-reduction errors must be smaller than the exact ratio’s margin from the acceptance threshold.
assumptions_latex: The exact ratio is separated from the threshold: \(\gamma=|\rho-\tau|>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sign}(\widetilde\rho-\tau)=\operatorname{sign}(\rho-\tau)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed joint budget is a sufficient, though conservative, compatibility condition. Its exact formulation lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Acceptance Misclassification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where model error can alter globalization decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance Misclassification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uncertainty interval for a threshold decision based on an inexact acceptance ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact ratio \(\rho\) and computed ratio \(\widetilde\rho\) satisfy \(|\widetilde\rho-\rho|\leq\delta\), where \(\delta\geq0\), and accept precisely when the relevant ratio is at least \(\tau\). If \(\widetilde\rho<\tau-\delta\), both ratios are below \(\tau\), and if \(\widetilde\rho\geq\tau+\delta\), both ratios are at least \(\tau\); hence misclassification is impossible in either case. If \(\tau-\delta\leq\widetilde\rho<\tau+\delta\), the admissible interval \([\widetilde\rho-\delta,\widetilde\rho+\delta]\) contains ratios on both sides of the acceptance boundary, so the error bound alone cannot certify the decision. Thus the decision-uncertainty region is \([\tau-\delta,\tau+\delta)\) for the tie convention \(\rho\geq\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With acceptance at equality, classification is uncertifiable when the computed ratio lies from one error radius below the threshold up to, but not including, one error radius above it; outside that interval the decision is stable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error bound alone leaves the decision uncertain exactly when \(\tau-\delta\leq\widetilde\rho<\tau+\delta\).

children.title: Finite-Precision Reliability
children.top_down_role: Numerical effects separating computed nested behavior from exact-arithmetic models.

children.title: Recursive Residual Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Divergence between recursively tracked and explicitly evaluated residual information.

children.title: Explicit-to-Recursive Residual Gaps
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies between explicitly evaluated residuals and recursively tracked values.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-to-Recursive Residual Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise discrepancy between an explicitly recomputed residual and the residual maintained by a finite-precision recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear system \(Ax=b\), let \(x_k\) be the computed iterate, let \(\widehat r_k\) be the residual updated recursively by the Krylov implementation, and let \(r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}:=b-Ax_k\) be the residual recomputed using the stored data and arithmetic under consideration. The explicit-to-recursive residual gap is \[g_k:=r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}-\widehat r_k.\] Its absolute and relative sizes are \(\|g_k\|\) and \(\|g_k\|/\|r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}\|\), respectively, with the relative quantity undefined when \(r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual gap is the difference between the residual recomputed from the current iterate and the residual maintained by recurrence.
assumptions_latex: Both residuals are interpreted in the specified finite-precision arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k=(b-Ax_k)-\widehat r_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally precise, including the zero-denominator case, but it has no finite-precision Krylov source or arithmetic-model citation.

children.title: Recursive Residual Drift
children.top_down_role: Accumulated finite-precision deviation in recursively maintained residual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Residual Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulation law for local rounding defects in a recursively updated residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume computed updates satisfy \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k+e_k^x\) and \(\widehat r_{k+1}=\widehat r_k-\alpha_kAp_k+e_k^r\), where \(e_k^x\) and \(e_k^r\) are local finite-precision defects. With \(g_k=(b-Ax_k)-\widehat r_k\), direct substitution gives \[g_{k+1}=g_k-Ae_k^x-e_k^r.\] Hence \(g_k=g_0-\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(Ae_j^x+e_j^r)\), and \(\|g_k\|\leq\|g_0\|+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(\|A\|\|e_j^x\|+\|e_j^r\|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local errors in iterate and residual recurrences accumulate into drift between recursive and explicitly recomputed residuals.
assumptions_latex: The displayed computed recurrences use the same stored operator \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{k+1}=g_k-Ae_k^x-e_k^r\) with the stated cumulative norm bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The drift identity follows from the stated defect recurrences and fits a property container, but the selected finite-precision error model has no supporting source.

children.title: Residual-Gap Growth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem and iteration regimes associated with increasing residual discrepancies.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Gap Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case bounded, linear, and geometric regimes induced by different local residual-defect models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a nonnegative residual-gap bound satisfy \(G_{k+1}\leq(1+\beta_k)G_k+d_k\). If \(\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k\leq d\), then \(G_k\leq G_0+kd\), giving at most linear growth; if additionally \(\sum_{j\geq0}d_j<\infty\), then \(G_k\) remains bounded. If \(\beta_k\leq\beta\) and \(d_k\leq d\) for \(\beta>0\), then \[G_k\leq(1+\beta)^kG_0+d\frac{(1+\beta)^k-1}{\beta},\] permitting geometric amplification. These are worst-case regimes, not assertions of realized growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable defects yield bounded gaps, uniformly bounded additive defects permit linear growth, and multiplicative amplification permits geometric growth.
assumptions_latex: The scalar recurrence bounds the norm of the actual residual gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence yields bounded, linear, or geometric worst-case growth under the stated defect regimes.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative upper bound for the residual-gap norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar recurrence bounds are correct as worst-case regimes, but no source establishes that this recurrence models the intended Krylov residual-gap setting.

children.title: Residual-Replacement Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability thresholds motivating explicit residual reevaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Replacement Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold rule for replacing a drifting recursive residual by an explicit recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A,b,x_k,\widehat r_k\), a target tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and parameters \(0<\theta<1\) and \(\sigma>0\), compute \(r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}=b-Ax_k\) at a scheduled reliability check. Replace \(\widehat r_k\leftarrow r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}\) whenever \[\|r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}-\widehat r_k\|>\theta\max\{\|r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}\|,\varepsilon\}\quad\text{or}\quad \|\widehat r_k\|\leq\sigma\varepsilon.\] Otherwise retain the recurrence. Declare convergence only from an explicit residual satisfying \(\|r_k^{\mathrm{exp}}\|\leq\varepsilon\); output the associated \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute and replace the residual when drift is relatively large or the recursive residual approaches the stopping scale; certify convergence explicitly.
assumptions_latex: Explicit residual checks can be performed with the stored operator and iterate.
The stopping criterion uses an absolute residual tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacement resets the measured gap to zero, and termination requires \(\|b-Ax_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the two-trigger replacement policy and its parameters are an uncited template rather than a source-supported residual-replacement algorithm.

children.title: Krylov-Geometry Degradation Modes
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision degradation of Krylov basis geometry.

children.title: Orthogonality Loss
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision degradation of mutual basis orthogonality.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonality Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision departure of computed Krylov residuals or basis vectors from their exact orthogonality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_k=[v_1,\ldots,v_k]\) contain computed normalized Krylov basis vectors. Their orthogonality-loss matrix is \(E_k:=V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k-I_k\), and a scalar measure is \(\omega_k:=\|E_k\|_2\). Exact orthonormality is equivalent to \(E_k=0\); finite-precision orthogonality loss occurs when \(E_k\neq0\). For a residual sequence intended to be mutually orthogonal, the analogous normalized pairwise measure is \[\omega_k^{(r)}:=\max_{0\leq i<j\leq k}\frac{|r_i^{\mathsf T}r_j|}{\|r_i\|_2\|r_j\|_2},\] provided all residuals are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonality loss is measured by deviation of the computed Krylov Gram matrix, or normalized residual inner products, from exact orthogonality.
assumptions_latex: The basis vectors are normalized and nonzero.
Residual-based measures include only nonzero residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orthogonality is exact precisely when the corresponding Gram-matrix deviation vanishes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram-matrix and normalized residual measures are coherent definitions, but no source supports these particular orthogonality-loss conventions in the intended Krylov context.

children.title: Conjugacy Loss
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision degradation of operator-relative direction conjugacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision departure of computed search directions from pairwise conjugacy under a symmetric positive-definite operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(P_k=[p_0,\ldots,p_{k-1}]\) contain nonzero computed search directions. Define \(D_k:=\operatorname{diag}(p_0^{\mathsf T}Ap_0,\ldots,p_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}Ap_{k-1})\). The normalized conjugacy-loss matrix is \[C_k:=D_k^{-1/2}(P_k^{\mathsf T}AP_k-D_k)D_k^{-1/2}.\] Its scalar size is \(\chi_k:=\|C_k\|_2\). The directions are pairwise \(A\)-conjugate exactly when \(C_k=0\); nonzero off-diagonal entries quantify conjugacy loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugacy loss is the normalized off-diagonal part of the search-direction Gram matrix in the operator-induced inner product.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is real, symmetric, and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_k=0\) if and only if \(p_i^{\mathsf T}Ap_j=0\) for every \(i\neq j\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of squared operator norms of search directions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized operator-Gram definition is mathematically sound for an SPD operator and fits the definition container, but its normalization convention lacks a source.

children.title: Coupled Krylov-Geometry Degradation
children.top_down_role: Interactions between multiple forms of degraded Krylov basis geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Krylov-Geometry Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint conditioning effect of orthogonality and conjugacy defects on projected Krylov systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(V_k\) have normalized computed columns, and write \(V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k=I+E_k\) and \(V_k^{\mathsf T}AV_k=T_k+F_k\), where \(T_k\) is the projected matrix prescribed by the exact Krylov recurrence. If \(\|E_k\|_2<1\), then \(V_k\) has full column rank and \[\kappa_2(V_k)\leq\sqrt{\frac{1+\|E_k\|_2}{1-\|E_k\|_2}}.\] Moreover, if \(\|T_k^{-1}F_k\|_2<1\), the perturbed projected system remains nonsingular; approaching either unit boundary permits coupled loss of basis geometry and projected-system reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonality defects condition the Krylov basis, while conjugacy or projection defects perturb the reduced system; either unit-scale defect can destroy reliability.
assumptions_latex: The computed basis columns are normalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounds \(\|E_k\|_2<1\) and \(\|T_k^{-1}F_k\|_2<1\) ensure full-rank basis geometry and a nonsingular perturbed projected system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basis-conditioning and perturbation conditions are standard matrix consequences, but identifying \(F_k\) as a Krylov conjugacy or projection defect and interpreting the two boundaries jointly requires a method-specific source.

children.title: Precision-Driven Geometry Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Precision regimes where basis geometry no longer supports reliable Krylov behavior.

assumptions_latex: Binary floating-point arithmetic uses round-to-nearest with unit roundoff \(u\).
The matrix-free oracle stores or rounds matrix coefficients before evaluating products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\delta\) with \(\operatorname{fl}(1+\delta)=1\), exact and computed Krylov dimensions disagree: \(\dim\mathcal K_2(A_\delta,q)=2\) but \(\dim\widehat{\mathcal K}_2(A_\delta,q)=1\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal test matrix whose spectral separation is below the working-precision resolution.
Exact order-two Krylov space generated by a matrix and vector.
Krylov space generated using the rounded matrix-free oracle.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete spectral-resolution boundary causing computed Krylov geometry to collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_\delta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1+\delta)\), \(q=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(0<\delta\) satisfy \(\operatorname{fl}(1+\delta)=1\). In exact arithmetic, \(q\) and \(A_\delta q\) are linearly independent, so \(\dim\mathcal K_2(A_\delta,q)=2\). If the matrix-free oracle stores or rounds \(1+\delta\) to \(1\), it acts as the identity on this problem; hence its first product equals \(q\), and \(\dim\widehat{\mathcal K}_2(A_\delta,q)=1\). Thus spectral distinctions below representable precision can destroy the Krylov geometry required by exact-arithmetic orthogonality, conjugacy, and termination certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a spectral separation rounds to zero, an exact two-dimensional Krylov space may collapse computationally to one dimension, invalidating geometry-based certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Driven Geometry Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed dimension collapse is mathematically consistent with the stated coefficient-rounding oracle and fits the failure-boundary container. However, no citation supports the specific floating-point oracle model or the broader claim about affected Krylov certificates, so source validation is required.

children.title: Mixed-Precision Nested Solves
children.top_down_role: Precision hierarchies across products, preconditioners, recurrences, and outer corrections.

assumptions_latex: The outer iteration supplies a linearized system \(H_k s=-g_k\) and a forcing tolerance \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\).
Products, preconditioning, Krylov recurrences, and residual corrections are available at precisions \(u_p,u_M,u_K,u_r\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step \(s_k\) is accepted only when the high-precision residual satisfies \(\|g_k+H_k s_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\); otherwise precision is raised or the inner solve reports failure.

notation.meaning: Outer linearized operator and right-hand side at iteration k.
Relative forcing tolerance for the nested linear solve.
Unit roundoffs for products, preconditioning, Krylov recurrences, and residual correction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic residual-corrected mixed-precision template for an inexact matrix-free second-order step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H_k\), \(g_k\), \(s^{(0)}=0\), and \(\eta_k\in(0,1)\), apply a preconditioned Krylov method using products at precision \(u_p\), preconditioner applications at \(u_M\), and recurrences at \(u_K\). Periodically compute \(r^{(j)}=-(g_k+H_k s^{(j)})\) at precision \(u_r\), solve approximately \(H_k d^{(j)}=r^{(j)}\), and set \(s^{(j+1)}=s^{(j)}+d^{(j)}\). Stop and output \(s_k=s^{(j)}\) only if the recomputed residual obeys \(\|g_k+H_k s^{(j)}\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\). If correction stagnates or this test is unreliable, raise the implicated precision and restart; if no higher precision is available, return inner-solve failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use inexpensive precisions internally, but recompute residuals more accurately and accept an outer step only after a reliable forcing test.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Precision Nested Solves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the mixed-precision-solves topic, and the acceptance test is coherent. No source supports the proposed correction, stagnation detection, precision-escalation, and restart policy. The precision used to apply H_k during residual recomputation and correction is also not fully specified, making the algorithm unreliable without a cited formulation.

children.title: Nondeterministic Execution Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Execution-order variability affecting reductions, stopping decisions, and nonlinear trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondeterministic Execution Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-invariance certification boundary for reduction-based stopping and branching decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let admissible execution trees produce reduced values \(\widehat\phi_T\) satisfying \(|\widehat\phi_T-\phi|\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{red}}\). If \(|\phi-\tau|>\Delta_{\mathrm{red}}\), every admissible tree gives the same strict comparison between \(\widehat\phi_T\) and \(\tau\). If \(|\phi-\tau|\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{red}}\), this error bound alone does not certify schedule invariance: admissible trees may produce values on opposite sides of \(\tau\), although differing decisions are not guaranteed. A schedule-independent certificate therefore requires additional information, such as a deterministic reduction or a verified decision margin larger than the applicable reduction-variation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction-based decision is certified as schedule invariant when its distance from the threshold exceeds the reduction-variation bound; within that bound, differing decisions are possible but not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: Floating-point addition is round-to-nearest and is not assumed associative.
A parallel reduction may combine the same terms according to different admissible execution trees.
An outer decision compares a reduced statistic \(\phi\) with a threshold \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|\phi-\tau|>\Delta_{\mathrm{red}}\), the strict comparison is schedule invariant; if \(|\phi-\tau|\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{red}}\), the bound alone does not certify schedule invariance.

notation.meaning: Reference scalar statistic associated with the reduction.
Floating-point statistic produced by admissible execution tree T.
Uniform bound on the deviation of admissible reduced values from the reference statistic.
